Reasons (script-written): the sizing analyses/PCL1_sizing.json gives a median 95 % half-width of the randomized fast-minus-slow total difference of 3.3 pp at 60 paired days and 2.6 pp at 100 (4.4 pp at 30), the upper bound of P(G2 PASS) is 0 at 60, 80, 100 and 160 paired days, and the cadence effect measured by thinning is about 1 pp (analyses/M442_result_rerun.json G1: native v2 shift 0.8-0.9 pp, harmonized shift 0.3-0.4 pp on halving), below what the protocol can resolve; the cost is about five months of switching the polling setting before every trip. Consequence: stage ME takes the cadence-stratified route (native v2 levels per polling stratum with the resolution bracket b of M442), which needs its own pre-registered spec, a blind audit, a Director ruling and Andrii's explicit sign-off before any display.

## M443 (2026-10-15): PCL-1: paired-cadence logging protocol (proposed; spec Rev 2.1, schedule generator, report-only monitor, one-shot analysis) to estimate the randomized cadence effect and test G2; awaiting the owner's START DATE; ME stays blocked

**Rationale.** PCL1 spec sha256 bef2d8d6c8383d9b4078214e470e700388fa411b7ba0fdaf1476684b4136838e (analyses/PCL1_spec.md Rev 2.1, recorded here at the proposal; the schedule hash 'PCL1 schedule sha256 <hash>' is recorded in a later CHANGELOG entry when the owner chooses the START DATE and the schedule is generated; the one-shot analysis refuses to run without both). Fifth step of the regeneration programme: M442 Rev 1.3 left gate G2 NOT TESTABLE (only 3 even days with both fast and slow drives; the existing corpus confounds the logger polling cadence with season, day and conditions), so stage ME stays blocked. PCL-1 is a PROPOSED paired-cadence logging protocol that randomizes the logger polling setting within each day (design A: permuted blocks of two trips; design B: seeded half-day arms, fallback fixed before the START DATE), identifies the randomized cadence effect on the native v2 level (primary estimand b) and evaluates G2 once, at 60 to 100 paired days (hard stop 2027-09-30, one extension of up to 160 paired days with 97.5 % intervals, first result reported beside it). Director reviews 2026-10-15: Rev 1 revise (B1-B9: view-total precision rule, deviation statements, end-date rule, holding rule, START DATE and hash freeze, slot rule, bracket frozen from M442_result_rerun.json, Director before any PASS if compliance < 90 % or ITT differs, fallback fixed before START) and Rev 2 minor revise (b primary, G2 secondary; view-total tolerance from OWN brackets without the 0-10 km/h bin; extension rule; script-written sizing). Script-written sizing (analyses/PCL1_sizing.json): the view-total tolerances are about 2.2 pp (temperature) and 1.4 pp (speed), the median 95 % half-width of the fast-minus-slow total difference is 3.3 pp at 60 paired days and 2.6 pp at 100, and the upper bound of P(PASS) is 0 at 60, 80, 100 and 160 days (trip heterogeneity dominates; no true effect simulated): a G2 PASS is not expected, the protocol is worth running for estimand (b) (a -12 pp gap is detectable at about 40 paired days). Code: tools/pcl_schedule.py (seeded schedule, designs A and B), tools/pcl_monitor.py (report-only ingestion stage pcl_monitor, counts and compliance only), tools/pcl_gate.py (the one-shot analysis with lock, freeze check, B1-B8 rules and a smoke mode), the holding rule in tools/regen_v2_agg.py (protocol drives stay out of the cadence-stratified views until the analysis has run), tests/synthetic/test_pcl1.py. No payload key, no display change, no master change. STATUS: PROPOSED; it needs Andrii's consent, the choice of design and START DATE, and the schedule hash in the CHANGELOG before the first protocol trip. Nothing about the protocol drives is looked at before the analysis.

## M441 (2026-10-15): Regen programme MC: interval-based extractor v2, per-drive cache and observed apparent KE recovery by pack temperature, speed and SOC band (additive keys regenCaptureV2 / regenCaptureV2Study; no display change; ME blocked by the cadence gate)

**Rationale.** Third stage (MC) of the regeneration programme (outside prompt regen_pack_temperature_soc_implementation_prompt.md; owner decisions (a)-(g) of 2026-10-14, recorded in CLAUDE.md Owner decisions together with the per-drive cache amendment (f)). Spec analyses/M441_spec.md Rev 2.2 (Director: Rev 1 revise B1-B7 -> Rev 2; confirmation revise R1-R6 -> Rev 2.1; ruling on the result: accept as an additive observed layer = Rev 2.2). New interval-based extractor v2 (tools/regen_v2.py): consecutive native speed samples with their actual duration (no fixed 1 s step, gaps over 5 s never bridged), RPM known at both ends (unknown is never engine-off), current and voltage interpolated through every native sample, charge as the positive-power integral on <= 0.05 s slices, speed bins by the instantaneous speed (overflow bin >= 130 km/h), pack temperature (all four probes) and SOC as interval-start attributes, plateau handling by episodes. Per-drive cache regen_cache/ (git-ignored; keyed by raw sha256, loader / despike / speed-priority versions, policy hash, extractor source hash, variant; offset charge in a separate file keyed by i_off): 578 drives in about 15 s, re-runs hit the cache. Aggregation (tools/regen_v2_agg.py): ratio of sums per cell by pack temperature, speed during braking and SOC band (edges 40/50/55/60/63/66/69/72/100 plus below 40 and missing), day-clustered percentile bootstrap (B = 4000, seed 42), support status (supported = >= 200 strict-drop intervals on >= 10 drives and >= 5 days), exact reconciliation (bands + below 40 + missing = SOC-free baseline), ordered bridge from the legacy rule, legacy comparison, cadence regime views. Additive keys regenCaptureV2 (refreshed every ingestion by the new stage regen_v2) and regenCaptureV2Study (on demand, carried forward: lag +-1 s and 2 s-ceiling sensitivities, cadence-invariance study B6); no legacy key and no display changes. RESULT (cohort all, 565 drives, 113 days): 98,557 strict-drop + 17,138 kept plateau intervals, apparent KE recovery 68.9 % [67.3, 70.4] (assumed masses; 72.4 % if the trimmed plateaus are included; 7 drives above 100 %, unclipped); the observed cells are strongly SOC-confounded (band 40-50: 23 %, 72-100: 86 % in the 30-40 C bin). Synthetic cadence test: v2 spread 0.18 pp against 26 pp for the legacy rule. Blind analytical-auditor (own extractor from the spec text): 26/26 per-drive rows and every total and listed cell reproduced exactly (ratios 0.00 pp); one finding adopted: the exclusion-reason precedence (speedGap > rpmUnknown > engineOn > currentOrVoltageUnsupported > notDecel) is now declared. B6 cadence-invariance gate (per-channel half-rate extraction of 177 fast drives): FAILED on 14 of 21 supported decision cells (full minus half-rate about +1 pp, of the order of the mass half-width; common support does not remove it); the strict-drop-only population is invariant (-0.09 pp [-0.41, 0.33]) and the plateau rule carries the residual. Director ruling: accept MC as an additive layer; stage ME stays BLOCKED until a Rev 3 plateau rule is pre-registered, B6 is re-run unchanged and passes (or the display is cadence-matched), a blind audit reproduces one bootstrap interval and the Director rules; MD may use the cadence regime as a stratum (payload only, no effect claims). No sign-off needed for MC (additive, no display, no article). Also in this commit: CLAUDE.md owner-decision entry, semantic-gate block and language rule M441-regen-v2, CI test list, ingestion stage regen_v2, .gitignore entry for regen_cache/.

## M440 (2026-10-15): Regen programme MB: sensitivity of the legacy apparent KE recovery to its extraction rules (additive block regenLegacySensitivity; no published number changes)

**Rationale.** Second stage (MB) of the regeneration programme (outside prompt regen_pack_temperature_soc_implementation_prompt.md; owner decisions (a)-(g) of 2026-10-14). Spec analyses/M440_spec.md Rev 2.2 (Director: Rev 1 revise B1-B4 -> Rev 2; confirmation R1-R6 = Rev 2.1; ruling on the result: accept = Rev 2.2). New tool tools/m440_regen_sens.py (+ tools/m440_analyse.py): a step-by-step replica of the legacy 'regen capture' block that also records, per qualifying step, what the variants need. GATE G1 (before any variant was read): all 123,076 qualifying steps from 565 drives on 113 days reproduce every published temperature and speed bin exactly (n and eff). Variants, each applied alone with a paired day-clustered bootstrap (B = 4000, seed 42): V1 RPM known, V2(k) native-sample age <= k s (k = 2, 5, 10), V3 consecutive rows, V4 speed bins by START speed, V5 all four probes, V6 declared current offset (-0.3888 A, discharge-positive frame), combined VCa / VCb. RESULT (cohort all): V1, V3, V5, V2(5), V2(10) not material (<= 0.3 pp, < 0.2 % of KE removed); V2(2) material in all four valid temperature bins (+0.75 to +1.72 pp) and speed bins 15-95 (removed steps' own ratio 20-40 %); V4 material at low speeds (bin 5: 9.7 -> 1.6 %, bin 15: 43.0 -> 34.5 %, bin 105: 65.5 -> 62.0 %); V6 lowers every bin by 0.2-1.7 pp (material in 15 bins; coupled to CAP_KWH, verified:false); VCa temperature immaterial, VCb -0.6 to -1.2 pp. Blind analytical-auditor (own raw rebuild): reproduced every number (three small slips in my claim prose: 5 not 4 V1 steps, 0.005 % of steps = 0.045 % of KE for V3, +0.0601); findings: the V2 effect is a polling-cadence effect not long staleness (99.7 % of the steps aged 2-5 s are on slow-cadence drives; the legacy rule books a multi-second native speed change as ONE 1 s step with one second of charge, which lowers the ratio of slow-cadence steps; the retained set is not cadence-free); legacy bin 5 is a mixture of sub-10 km/h steps (46 % of KE, ratio 1.6 %, 97 % zero-charge steps, 1 km/h speed quantum) and threshold-crossing fade-out steps (54 % of KE, 92 % of charge, ratio 16.6 %), and V4 moves steps one way only; the offset sign is consistent with the v6 frame but not confirmable from rest periods. Dashboard: a collapsed note beside the regeneration views bound to S.regenLegacySensitivity (per-cohort table of the rule changed, KE retained, material bins and the largest difference with its interval, plus the required cadence / end-speed / one-way / resolution statements); language rule M440-regen-sensitivity. Block regenLegacySensitivity is on demand and carried forward at ingestion (ingest_core.carry_forward) with a staleness label; age-stratified ratios and the cadence split are written by the tool. DESIGN CONSEQUENCES for stage MC (Director): integrate KE and charge over the same native speed-update interval, keep start AND end speed, report the sub-10 km/h fade-out separately, offset as a mandatory dual report (not the point basis), fixes for RPM / contiguity / probes on design grounds, age bound only as a sensitivity; known-answer test: the same trajectory polled at 1.0 s and 1.4 s must give the same ratio. Gates: G1 exact reproduction, G3 byte-identical rerun (and splice --verify), identity Delta = w (eff_ret - eff_rem) to 1e-14, KATs (tests/synthetic/test_m440_regen_sens.py, in CI), semantic gate 1311 passed 0 failed, test_regen_axes.js extended. No published number changes (the legacy bars are untouched until MC / ME). LIMITS: no ground truth (a difference shows sensitivity, not which rule is closer to the truth); 'material' is a low bar (0.15-0.8 pp); 0-10 C (n 46, 1 day) not evaluable and no sub-zero data; warm / shoulder / cold descriptive; single vehicle, assumed masses. No article use.

## M437 (2026-10-14): F17 follow-up: forward-fill and trip-end-tolerance sensitivity of the time-to-threshold headline cells (range over declared conventions; S0 stays the record)

**Rationale.** Follow-up of the M435 Director ruling and blind audit (the cold-start population depends on the 3 s forward fill; the audit's 13 and 35). Spec analyses/M437_spec.md Rev 2.2 (Director: Rev 1 revise B1-B6 -> Rev 2 -> approve with clarifications C1-C5 = Rev 2.1; ruling on the result: accept, wording requirements = Rev 2.2). Additive key thermalSupportLedger.timeToThreshold.fillSensitivity produced by the ledger stage in the same pass over the frames (tools/m437_fill.py: the three grids come from one resample per frame; whole ledger stage 1.6-2.0 min on this machine), regenerated at every ingestion. Facts it rests on: ffill(limit=F) fills the first F seconds of every gap, a filled second repeats an earlier value, so the first second at or above a threshold is always a sampled second: event times cannot move with F (0 of 2,944 first crossings fall on a filled second in the blind audit); F acts only through the cold-start population (>= 30 valid seconds), the censoring time and the trip-end / channel-loss split. Settings F in {0, 3*, 6} s (full re-estimation, headline cells cohort all, coolant 80 C and oil 70 C, h = 600 s), tolerance X in {5, 10*, 30} s as a reason-count table. RESULT: coolant 80 C observed share 0.356 / 0.344 / 0.344 and Kaplan-Meier (product-limit) estimate 0.473 / 0.469 / 0.468 at F = 0 / 3 (record) / 6; oil 70 C 0.144 / 0.139 / 0.139 and 0.217 / 0.216 / 0.216; the reading classes are identical in all 3 settings (coolant: both readings depend on the censoring assumption; oil: fewer than half reached holds for every theta 0.5-2, half or more reached depends on the censoring assumption). F = 0 drops 13 coolant / 12 oil short, sparsely sampled cold starts (none reached by 600 s; 30 valid seconds are 30 raw samples, about 78 s at the median coolant interval 2.61 s, p95 7.11 s; oil median 1.17 s): a population effect, not faster warm-up; F = 3 and F = 6 have identical populations. Event times changed: 0; censoring times of the drives censored in both settings move by at most 3 s (coolant 188 at F = 0, 88 at F = 6; oil 173 and 8). Reason labels: 35 coolant drives tripEnd -> channelLoss at (F = 0, X = 5) (the audit's 35, the same drives; a sampling artefact because X = 5 is below the coolant p95 interval), 2 oil channelLoss -> tripEnd at (F = 6, X = 10), all others at most 2. Gates: checks.allOk in the payload (G1 equals the M435 block, nesting F=0 subset of the record subset of F=6, eventTimeChanged 0, censoring shift <= |dF|; a failure raises and no leaf is written), G2 (deep diff: only the new key and the stamp), G3 (second ledger run: nChanged 0), known-answer tests (tests/synthetic/test_m437_fill.py: grid equals _twl_grid, gap fill semantics, the 30-valid-second rule, equal event times across F with seed 42, tolerance comparison <=, paired counts), semantic gate 1287 passed 0 failed. Blind analytical-auditor reproduced every number to 4 decimals (own raw rebuild) and confirmed the 13 and 35 drives are the same as in its M435 notes. LIMITS: the fill range 0-6 s is below the 95th percentile of the coolant sample interval (7.11 s), so longer gaps stay missing in every setting; the ranges are of point estimates and the bootstrap resample sets differ between settings; the sensitivity does not address informative censoring (the M435 bounds and tilt rows do), so the coolant reading stays dependent on the censoring assumption; headline cells of cohort all only; single vehicle, one driver, May-October. The M435 sentence 'the headline classes are unchanged' is replaced by the script-written statement; its old wording is now a language rule (M437-fill-sensitivity). No article use. Follow-up: a fill grid reaching the coolant p95 interval (about 8 s) needs its own spec.

F26: tools/record_spread_fit.py computed the Huber fits and 4000-draw bootstraps before checking the append-only history; it now builds the complete cheap key first (master md5, m19b and huber_slope_ci hashes, python / numpy / pandas / scikit-learn versions, T_REF, epsilon, max_iter, n_boot, seed; the five existing records carry all these fields) and computes only on a miss (a hit ran in 3.5 s; history and records unchanged; a different library version is a miss and appends a record, not a rewrite). ## M431 (2026-10-14): F14: fit_glm silent fallback is latent, not live (549 replayed fits, 0 fallbacks); strict recorded fit for new callers, module change bundled with the next M119 refit

**Rationale.** Audit F14 (external audit 2026-10-13), verified in code first: m119v2_model.fit_glm refits with tol 1e-6 and scale=1.0 on ANY exception of the primary fit (cluster-robust covariance when groups are given), which can drop the clustered covariance and accept a singular design without a record. Call sites: oos_predict and rolling_origin_predict (no clusters), _final_fit (clustered, four fits), tools/m320_ladder.py (no clusters; it discards non-converged draws and swallows every other exception), tools/m428_oot.py. No downstream code reads bse / cov_params / conf_int / pvalues, so the clustered covariance is computed and never consumed: only params feed any published number. CENSUS (read-only, tools/fit_glm_census.py; the spy is a line-for-line copy of fit_glm and returns identical parameters and standard errors, tested): the published M119-v2 fit sequence replayed on the 489-drive basis (run_ladder both sides k=5, sensitivity_screen, rolling_origin_cv, _final_fit) plus _final_fit on all 578 drives = 149 fits, and a deterministic sample of the M320 ladder bootstrap draws (every 20th of 4000 per side, rebuilt with the same SeedSequence(42, spawn_key=(k,)), 400 fits; a first run with 10 workers hit a memory limit and was redone with 5): 0 fallbacks, 0 non-converged, 0 rank-deficient, 0 NaN parameters, 0 statsmodels warnings, 0 swallowed exceptions (maximum 13 IRLS iterations; evidence analyses/F14_fit_glm_census.json and analyses/F14_m320_draw_census.json). Conclusion: LATENT risk, not live; no published number came from the fallback path and no figure changes. The other 3600 M320 draws were not replayed (stated limitation). WHY NO IN-MODULE EDIT NOW: m119v2_model.py is in the M321 selection-code hash (whole file); editing it makes the release gate FAIL (cache-invalid) until the monitor is rebased and invalidates both W2/W3 acknowledgements (bound to that hash), which need a fresh Director record; the documented remedy belongs with a refit. DELIVERED: tools/fit_contract.fit_glm_strict (same primary estimator, identical numbers when the contract holds, never falls back, raises FitContractError on a primary-fit exception, non-convergence, a rank-deficient design, non-finite parameters or a convergence-class warning, returns a JSON-ready record) for NEW callers; tests/synthetic/test_fit_contract.py pins today's silent behaviour of fit_glm (a singular design is accepted via the fallback, a non-converged fit is returned without a record) so any change to it is deliberate, proves the strict fit and the census spy are numerically identical to fit_glm, and checks each refusal; a refit checklist in docs/workflow-and-tools.md (replay the refit's fits with the census and require zero fallbacks, replace the silent fallback by the strict contract and write the per-fit record into the block, re-key the monitor and re-issue the W2/W3 acknowledgements). This is a measurement and tooling change, not a new estimand: no pre-registered spec, no blind audit, no Director ruling was needed or run (a census count with a tested-faithful spy). NOT DONE: the in-module change (bundled with the next explicit M119 refit); an F14-style audit of other bare except Exception sites (F28).

## M430 (2026-10-14): Held-out fit quality of the parked-soak time-constant fits (audit F05); in-sample R2 printed, single exponential improves on persistence but is not shown to describe the soak

**Rationale.** Audit F05 (external audit 2026-10-13), verified first: the in-sample R2 of the three soak fits is negative (pack -1.051, coolant -16.124, oil -16.775 on the through-origin Sen line against a free-level mean of ln(resid/init excess)); the Thermal tab said R2 'is not a meaningful diagnostic ... and is omitted here', the coolant and oil R2 were shown nowhere, and no prediction error or held-out result existed. Pre-registered spec analyses/M430_spec.md Rev 2 + 2.1 (Director: revise with six blocking items, then approve): estimand = out-of-sample error of the EXISTING single-exponential line (Sen slope refit on training days) with whole arrival-day blocks held out (k = 10 contiguous blocks), PRIMARY metric = MAE skill on the retained fraction exp(y) against persistence, a constant level and gap-bin medians (loss-consistent references), secondaries = log-scale MSE skill and log MedAE skill with a declared 'metric disagreement' flag, paired day-clustered bootstrap (B = 4000, seed 42) conditional on the fold assignment, statements only for pooled / gap < 1 h / gap >= 1 h with >= 20 pairs and >= 10 days, zero-denominator rule, bins descriptive. Point estimates, R2, M429 intervals and every other leaf reproduce exactly (G1 passed for pack, coolant, oil); 6 payload leaf roots changed (G2), the single-key recompute is byte-identical to the spliced payload (G3). KNOWN-ANSWER TEST (criteria declared before any result, planted on the real per-day gap sets with a day-shared offset, integer-degree temperatures and the real selection; tau 12 h, total sd 0.35, ICC 0.25): single exponential 1.00 of replications (criterion 0.85), two timescales 0.94 (0.60), no decay 1.00 (0.85); power applies to the pack design only. RESULT (primary skill, pooled): vs persistence pack 0.395 [0.307, 0.484], coolant 0.690 [0.659, 0.720], oil 0.695 [0.652, 0.735] (improvement over persistence established in all three; for gaps >= 1 h in all three; NOT for the pack below one hour, -0.057 [-0.122, -0.002]); vs gap-bin medians pack -0.022 [-0.058, 0.011], coolant -0.090 [-0.176, -0.016] (worse than the empirical bins), oil +0.010 [-0.044, 0.064]; at 1 h or longer the line is worse than the bins for coolant and oil; coolant and oil below one hour beat the bins (+0.098, +0.110; no statement by rule); leave-one-day-out changes no statement. The log-scale squared-error skill is negative and wide (pack -0.853 [-3.82, 0.58]) and is flagged 'metric disagreement': pairs parked 12 h or longer (9.1 / 10.3 / 8.3 % of the pairs) carry 89.1 / 98.4 / 98.3 % of the line's held-out log squared error, where the outcome-selection floor (pairs with residual excess <= 0.5 C are excluded: 151 / 39 / 50 pairs, recounted from analyses/M430_prefilter_pairs.json) and a shape misfit are confounded; held out the line retains too much at short gaps and too little at long gaps for coolant and oil. Reading: a negative R2 alone does not mean no decay where an improvement over persistence is established, and it does not show that one exponential describes the soak; tau stays a gap-mix-dependent, model-derived summary. BLIND AUDIT (analytical-auditor, independence partial: reused the M429 pair tables): reproduced every value (max difference 0.003), no leakage; methodological findings adopted by the Director as post-hoc descriptive leaves (labelled not pre-registered): postHoc.logSqErrShareGapGe12h, b2EqualsB0AllFolds (pack below one hour: S3 restates S1, 43 % of y is exactly 0), blockBootstrap per eligible cell (oil gap >= 1 h: S3 does not survive a 5-day moving-block bootstrap; the producer computes it in every eligible cell, generalising the single case the Director named), MedAE shown as 'no comparison' where its denominator is zero (pack below one hour, 117/4000 draws). DIRECTOR (2026-10-14): outcome accepted, no Andrii sign-off needed, no article use. Language: rule M430-r2-dismissed with the old wording ('not a meaningful diagnostic', 'omitted here', 'does not describe the pairs', the bare 'not that there is no decay'); the older sentences that called the soak fit one that 'does not describe the pairs' were reworded (conclusions and Thermal tab). Payload by tools/m430_splice.py; dashboard block bound to S.heatSoakCarryover.soakFitQuality and S.interDriveCarryover.thermalDecay.{coolant,oil,battery}.fitQuality; semantic_gate checks (block rendered, R2 and exclusion counts equal the payload, pooled statements equal the payload, design and caveats stated). Cost: the whole recompute takes about 4.5 minutes; B stays 4000. NOT DONE (own specs): a gap-stratified or two-timescale soak model with interval censoring of the floor; the ambient-offset sensitivity of these diagnostics. Not article-eligible (Opus audit and Andrii's sign-off).

## M429 (2026-10-14): Day-clustered interval for the parked-soak time constants (audit F06); pack tau CI [9.96, 13.75] -> [9.77, 13.93] h, point estimates unchanged

**Rationale.** Audit F06 (external audit 2026-10-13), verified in code first: the pack soak CI (heatSoakCarryover.soakTauCI, copied to interDriveCarryover.thermalDecay.battery.tauCI) resampled the fitted drive pairs i.i.d. (1000 draws) although its docstring and the interDriveCarryover methodology said day-clustered; coolant and oil already resampled arrival days (1000 draws); all three silently dropped bootstrap draws with a non-negative slope. Pre-registered spec analyses/M429_spec.md Rev 2 (Director: revise, then approve; four blocking items adopted: D1 on the finite decay rate, one exact percentile and unbounded rule, the pack day key, an explicit G2 leaf list plus a G3 identity gate). METHOD: one shared helper tools/soak_tau.py used by both producers: whole arrival-day clusters (calendar day of the following drive's start) resampled with replacement, B = 4000, a fresh default_rng(42) per method, percentile of the draw slopes on the slope scale mapped by tau = -1/slope, draws with slope >= 0 counted (tau = +infinity) not dropped, upper bound unbounded iff the 97.5th slope percentile >= 0. Point estimates, R2, gapBins and every other leaf reproduce EXACTLY (G1 passed for pack, coolant, oil). RESULT: pack tau 11.55 h, CI [9.96, 13.75] (pairs i.i.d., 1000 draws, published) -> [9.77, 13.93] (98 arrival-day clusters, Kish 67.8 of 350 pairs); decay rate k 0.0866 /h [0.0718, 0.1024]; departure-day [9.91, 13.62]; ISO-week [9.62, 13.66] (22 blocks, coarse); coolant 3.40 [3.00, 3.91] -> [3.02, 3.91]; oil 3.45 [3.18, 3.76] -> [3.19, 3.77]; no draw was non-decaying anywhere, so the unbounded rule never triggered on real data (exercised only in the known-answer test) and the old drop rule dropped 0 draws. The agreement of the methods means weak between-day dependence here (arrival/i.i.d. k-width ratio 1.08 / 1.02 / 1.07), not its absence. KNOWN-ANSWER TEST (criteria declared in the spec before any result): coverage of the day-clustered interval 0.935 (criterion 0.88-1.00), of the pair-i.i.d. interval 0.58 (criterion < 0.85); a first planted design with a day offset independent of the gap left the pair-i.i.d. interval calibrated (0.965) because pair dependence matters only when the regressor clusters by day, as the real gaps do; the published old-rule intervals are reproduced on the stored pair sets. BLIND AUDIT (analytical-auditor, independence partial: it reused the pair table analyses/M429_pairs.json and the Sen slope definition): reproduced every value to printed precision with an identical RNG stream, gaps and days of all 1255 pairs match drive_master; scripts in analyses/M429_audit/. POST-HOC FINDING (audit, not pre-registered, Director ruling: disclose): 28 % of the pack ln-ratios are exactly 0 (whole-degree temperature logging); pack pairs parked under 1 h (n = 202) show no resolvable decay (k 0, CI [0, 0.168]) and the pooled pack tau rests on the 148 pairs of 1 h or longer (k 0.0767, tau 13.04 h); coolant and oil decay faster over short gaps (k 0.592 / 0.514 below 1 h, 0.135 / 0.152 above; tau 1.69 / 1.95 h versus 7.40 / 6.58 h), so tau is a gap-mix-dependent summary of a single-exponential fit. Shipped as leaves soakTauGapSplit and thermalDecay.{coolant,oil}.gapSplit (computed by the producer, labelled post-hoc) with a sentence under the soak panel; the older sentence 'treat the fitted tau as the SHORT-GAP behavior it is best supported by' contradicted this and was reworded (language rule M429-soak-ratio with the old wording); the 'physically consistent' coolant/oil-versus-pack sentence is now a point-estimate ratio with the interval overlap stated. Frozen historical rows (analyses/M429_published_rule.json) are never recomputed at ingestion. PAYLOAD: leaf splice tools/m429_splice.py inside the G2 list (31 leaves, none removed), G3 passed (a single-key recompute with tools/m429_soak.py is byte-identical to the spliced payload); drive_master.csv MD5 a641f34d7528d004b900c151cbde3d6d unchanged. COST: the recompute takes about 4 minutes (including 40 s for the trajectories); B stays 4000, no spec amendment. NOT DONE (own specs): a gap-stratified or two-timescale soak model with interval censoring for the y = 0 mass; the i.i.d. bootstrap of the parked standby-draw fit (_car_off_standby); the sentence on this panel that calls R2 'not a meaningful diagnostic' is untouched here and belongs to audit F05. Not article-eligible (Opus audit and Andrii's sign-off).

## M416 (2026-10-12): Journaled release for the stage runner (audit F20): snapshot, commit, rollback with tree re-hash, crash recovery, lock and failure-injection tests

**Rationale.** Tooling milestone (analyses/M416_spec.md; deep audit F20; owner direction 2026-10-12 'F20/F11 - OK', read as the recommendation: journaled copy-swap now, release directories only after the MIGRATION.md reproduction test). tools/release_journal.py + tools/run_ingest.py: before the first stage the working tree outside raw/ and the regenerable caches is hashed and copied (real tree: 858 files, 208 MB hashed, 67 MB copied, 3.4 s; files above 30 MB are hash-only); a failed gate, an exception or SIGINT/SIGTERM restores every changed file, removes created files, re-creates deleted files and re-hashes the whole tree (rolled_back, or rollback_failed with the mismatches, exit 4); a green run commits and records its write set and the undeclared writes in journal.json; a killed runner leaves the journal started and runs/.release.lock, the next run is refused (exit 5) until run_ingest.py --recover; a live second release is refused; --keep-on-failure keeps the mixed state for inspection; --no-journal for development. Failure injection (tests/synthetic/test_release_journal.py, in CI, 9 scenarios): a failure at each of three stages leaves the previous file set byte-identical; hard kill then refuse then recover; keep-on-failure then recover; lock held by a live process; a rollback that cannot restore is rollback_failed (verified by re-hashing, never assumed). run_ingest computes the fingerprint plan only when --skip-unchanged is requested (behaviour otherwise unchanged). Docs: docs/workflow-and-tools.md section 'Journaled release', ingest-drive skill sentence. Not covered (disclosed): raw/ is never modified by a rollback (raw files added by a failed run are listed in status.json journal.rawAdded); there is still no single-pointer release directory (flat-tree rule), so readers can see the mixed state during a run (the lock and the journal mark the window); files in the excluded directories are not rolled back. No figure, payload, dashboard or master change.

**State.** `drive_master.csv` 554 rows, MD5 `64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525`.

## M397 (2026-10-11): run_ingest: launch stages with the running interpreter (Windows Store python3 alias fails intermittently, WinError 1920) and record a launch failure as a failed stage; found by the clean-room replay of the M388 ingestion

**Rationale.** Tooling robustness fix in tools/run_ingest.py found by the clean-room replay of the M388 ingestion (a scratch git worktree at the pre-M388 commit f37e8d8 with today's code overlaid, the 30 new raw files visible as new drives, ambients and odometer entered by the documented manual steps, both report-only monitors baselined at the pre-M388 corpus). No change to the master, any estimator or any payload value. FINDING: the replay run executed the preflight, ingest_core and stage_raw and then crashed while LAUNCHING the fourth stage (raw_temp_pass) with 'OSError: [WinError 1920] The file cannot be accessed by the system' raised by subprocess.run inside run_ingest.py, so neither status.json nor failure.json was written. Cause: every stage command in tools/ingest_stages.json starts with 'python3', which on this Windows machine resolves (PATH) to the Microsoft Store app-execution alias C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python3.exe; that alias intermittently fails to launch (it had worked for the three earlier stages of the same run and for the M395 run) and, when it works, runs an interpreter that is not necessarily the one running the orchestrator. A long real ingestion could die the same way part-way, leaving a half-run with no failure record. FIX: resolve_cmd() replaces a leading 'python3' / 'python' by sys.executable (the interpreter running run_ingest; other commands such as node are unchanged; the input list is not mutated); launch() wraps subprocess.run so that an OSError (the stage never started) becomes an ordinary failed stage (return code 127, the error written to the stage log, failure.json and status.json written, the run stops with result gate_failed) instead of an uncaught exception. Known-answer test tests/synthetic/test_run_ingest_launch.py (added to ci.yml): python3 / python -> the running interpreter, node unchanged, empty and tuple commands, input not mutated, a real stage keeps its own return code, a non-existent command is returned as a failure value. Replay findings recorded here for the next steps: (1) with today's code the replayed ingest_core produced a master that is CELL-FOR-CELL identical to the merged M388 master (554 rows x 190 columns, 0 differing cells), i.e. the SoC filter, the M392 recalibration rules and the despiking reproduce by themselves what was done by hand at M388 (the one-row fix); (2) the byte checksum differs (816f48ca... vs 64dfd0cb...) only because the committed M388 master has CRLF line endings (the unshimmed one-row fix tools/m388c_resplice_drive.py wrote it on Windows) while the pipeline and tools/normalize_eol.py convention is LF; content-neutral, preflight and CI pass on the committed bytes; a separate decision (it changes the corpus anchor bytes), not done here. **Rationale.** Disclosure and wording change for the pack-resistance proxy slope (powerFade); spec analyses/M395_spec.md, follows M393 (analyses/M393_resistance_cadence.py); blind audit 'fix' -> all points fixed -> scoped re-check; Director: accept as disclosure. ## M396 (2026-10-10): Report-only flag for the logger PID polling cadence: tells the owner when a new drive is slow while fast polling is expected

**Rationale.** New report-only ingestion stage cadence_monitor (tools/cadence_monitor.py, registered after cadence_regime; spec analyses/M396_spec.md). Owner request (chat, 2026-10-09): flag explicitly when the logger PID polling cadence is slow again; the owner re-activated fast polling after the app setting changed on 2026-10-08 and expects it to work from the next ingestion's drives. No change to the master (MD5 64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525), any estimator, the regime rule or any payload value. Background (script output, cadence_regime.csv): median HV-current polling interval 0.82-0.86 s per day from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-07 (fast); on 2026-10-08 the first three drives are fast (0.81-0.89 s) and every drive from 10:15 on (12 drives) is 1.35-1.55 s, slower than the earlier slow regime (about 1.25 s); the M379a rule (fast: master I_sample_period_s < 1.05 s) labels it 'slow'; the column set did not change (about 80 columns incl. fuel rate, throttle, boost, SoC). The CSVs cannot show the cause; the owner attributes it to the app. Monitor: state analyses/cadence_monitor.json (deterministic, no timestamps): expected regime fast (since 2026-10-09, owner), last drive seen, last regime, last_update, cumulative flag_history. The first run BOOTSTRAPPED on the current corpus (baseline = through 2026-10-08_21-24-03, 554 drives, no flags; committed here). Later runs look only at drives after the last seen one: cadence_slow_while_fast_expected (FLAG: first slow drive file / date / time, number of slow and fast new drives, median interval of the slow ones, reference medians of the fast regime (last 30 fast drives) and the slow regime, slower_than_reference_slow = median > 1.10 x the reference slow median, action 'check the app PID / polling settings'), fast_polling_confirmed (info), cadence_unknown (info, not evaluable, never a pass). A run with no new drives leaves the file untouched; a flag enters flag_history once per first slow drive; the stage never stops an ingestion (main() prints monitor_error and exits 0). Surfacing: tools/delta_report.py gains an informational cadenceMonitor block (never in flags / route_to_audit); the ingestion skill (step 7) now makes the FIRST LINE of every ingestion report the cadence status (fast confirmed, or the flag with its details), followed by any dissipationMonitor flags, because report-only monitors only help if the agent reads and reports them; the stage output prints FLAG / INFO lines in the run log. Known-answer test tests/synthetic/test_cadence_monitor.py (added to ci.yml): bootstrap without flags; nothing new leaves the file untouched; all-fast batch confirms; fast then slow in one batch raises the flag with its details; history once; a slow batch at the earlier slow level is flagged but not 'slower'; unknown is info; ordering independent of sidecar row order; main() never raises. Not diagnosed: the cause of the 2026-10-08 change. Limits: the rule is the M379a threshold (a setting between 1.05 s and the earlier slow level is also 'slow'); fixed factors, not tuned.

## M394 (2026-10-09): Winter-readiness monitor for the unfuelled (motored) engine dissipation mode: report-only ingestion stage; baseline 35 sustained events, none below 10 C, thresholds unvalidated for cold

**Rationale.** New report-only ingestion stage dissipation_monitor (tools/dissipation_monitor.py, library tools/dissipation_events.py, registered after cadence_regime; spec analyses/M394_spec.md; blind audit 'fix' -> all points fixed -> scoped re-check pass; Director: accept). Owner request: the system must be ready to detect the unfuelled (motored) engine dissipation mode when it appears in winter and normal driving. No change to the published census (dissipationCensus), the master (MD5 64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525), any estimator or any payload value; release_check unchanged. Mode (the code's own description, M46): series hybrid, the ICE couples only to the generator; when the pack cannot accept surplus / regenerative energy the VCM can dump it by motoring the engine unfuelled (closed throttle, deep vacuum, calc load ~0) at elevated rpm. HYPOTHESIS, NOT OBSERVED: a cold pack accepts less charge, so the mode may become more frequent, start at lower SoC or at a different rpm in winter. Detectors on the 1 s grid (bins aligned to the wall-clock second; thresholds fixed, not tuned): PUB (the census classifier) rpm > 2000 & boost < -0.70 & calc load < 8; FUEL (independent, logged / app-calculated fuel rate, 60-column logging generation only) rpm > 1200 & fuel rate < 0.2 L/h & absolute throttle B < 10 %; event = run >= 3 s; SUSTAINED = >= 10 s and |rpm slope| < 30 rpm/s (FUEL alone fires on engine start / stop transients: 80 FUEL-only events, median 5 s, 69 % falling rpm). Evidence (script output: analyses/M394_dissipation_scan.py, M394_fuel_crosscheck.py, the monitor bootstrap; blind audit reproduced the counts event for event): census samples have median logged fuel rate 0.0 L/h, engine power 0.0 kW, throttle about 2 % (fuelled > 2000 rpm: 6.2 L/h, 24 kW, 90 %); 0 of 24 census sustained events fail the fuel check on fuel-capable drives; relaxing the census rpm gate is not an option (85 % of low-manifold-pressure samples sit at 1200-2000 rpm, the fuelled generator floor is about 1500 rpm). BASELINE (554 drives, 496 census-evaluable, 324 fuel-capable): 35 sustained events = 24 census (13 drives) + 11 fuel-indicated that the census does not see (9 drives, mean rpm 1520-1736, just above the generator floor: 'fuel-indicated unfuelled (unconfirmed by census; low-power fuelled generation not ruled out)'); all at mean SoC 76.9-84.8 % (the census CEIL_SOC = 85 sits above where the mode appears); pack-temperature bands: 10-15 C 2 sustained events (one drive at 14.9 C), 15-25 C 10, >= 25 C 23, < 10 C none. VALIDATION GAP: no drive below 5 C, one drive in 5-10 C, lowest pack temperature 9.7 C, no sustained event below 10 C; the intake-air channel is unavailable since 2026-08-24, so pack temperature is the temperature axis. THRESHOLDS WERE SET ON DATA >= 9.7 C PACK TEMPERATURE AND ARE UNVALIDATED FOR COLD. Monitor: state analyses/dissipation_monitor.json (one record per drive, deterministic, about 240 KB); the first run bootstraps the baseline without flags, later runs record unseen drives and flag each against the drives with an earlier (date, file): first_sustained_in_band (bands < 5, 5-10, 10-15, 15-25, >= 25 C), below_baseline_soc (mean SoC more than 5 pp below every earlier sustained event), fuel_event_not_in_census, census_event_not_fuel_confirmed, channel_gap (not evaluable, never a pass), sustained_event_unknown_temperature, read_error (unreadable raw file: not recorded, retried, the batch continues), info flags; it never stops an ingestion (main() prints monitor_error and exits 0 on an unexpected failure), a run with no new drives leaves the file untouched, flag_history is cumulative and a persistent read_error enters it once per file; a recorded drive is never recomputed (its band is the one at first recording). tools/delta_report.py gains an informational dissipationMonitor block (flags listed, never in flags / route_to_audit); reviewer action: list any flag in the CHANGELOG acknowledgement. Known-answer tests tests/synthetic/test_dissipation_monitor.py (added to ci.yml): steady unfuelled spin = sustained for both detectors; start / ramp transient not sustained; fuelled 1500 rpm floor not an event; missing channels not evaluable; each flag has a firing and a non-firing case; backfill ordering; unknown temperature; error isolation; idempotence and rerun safety. STOP RULE / COLD VALIDATION (Director, stated in the spec): trigger = the first first_sustained_in_band flag below 10 C; steps = a manual event check recorded in the CHANGELOG (SoC, rpm trend, pack current, ambient and context from the driver), then a separate pre-registered spec reviewing the cold-band thresholds, the census CEIL_SOC = 85, the census rpm gate and the classifier on the cold data, then a blind audit, then a Director ruling; Andrii signs off any change to the census or estimators; neither the monitor nor the main session changes a threshold on its own. Dashboard display deferred until cold sustained events exist (any display binds to S.* keys); with zero cold events a cold rate is reported with a Wilson CI only once cold drives exist, never as 'no effect'. OWNER ACTIONS (Director): keep the 60-column PID set unchanged through winter (the fuel and throttle channels are the independent indicator; a PID change also changes sampling cadence, see M393, and would confound winter against summer); when a cold drive is flagged note the ambient temperature and anything unusual (preconditioning, short trip, full-SoC start); if possible restore the intake-air temperature PID. Limits: FUEL needs the 60-column generation (324 of 554 drives); the grid is anchored at 1900-01-01 (a drive crossing midnight would wrap; none does); same-date drives are ordered by file name; thresholds from summer data.

## M393 (2026-10-09): Pack-resistance proxy slope (powerFade +0.552 mOhm/month): reproduced, cadence influence verified (emulation); result is a null with a cadence-dependent point estimate (analysis only)

**Rationale.** Analysis-only milestone (owner question 2026-10-09: 'Is the estimated proxy slope +0.552 correct? Does the recent PID polling cadence change influence the computation? Verify the cadence influence.'); no change to any estimator, the master (MD5 64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525) or the payload. Study script analyses/M393_resistance_cadence.py, output analyses/M393_resistance_cadence.json (all numbers below are script output; day-clustered percentile bootstrap, seed 42, 4000 draws; model R ~ 1 + months + T_pack_mean_avg + vreg_I_p95_A [+ cadence covariates] on the v2-clean set, 242 drives, 89 days, proxy vreg_R_pack_mohm, as compute_drive_summary_v6._powerfade_trend). (A) CORRECTNESS: the published powerFade slope +0.552 mOhm/month (95% CI [-0.929, 2.124], p(slope>0) 0.776) is reproduced by the pipeline function on the live master, by an independent implementation of the same OLS (+0.5518, same CI, 242 drives), and a cluster-robust (day) OLS gives the same slope with CI [-0.880, 1.984] (p 0.45, 89 clusters): the arithmetic is correct and the result is a statistical null (the stored block's own minimum detectable slope is 1.526 mOhm/month = 14.2 %/yr over a 4.8-month window; +0.552 is about a third of it). It is not an estimate of fade. (B) SPECIFICATION SENSITIVITY (same clean set unless stated; logger regimes from cadence_regime.csv: slow 152 clean drives, fast1 = 2026-08-14..09-06 67, fast2 = from 2026-10-01 23): no cadence covariate +0.989 [-0.294, 2.233]; published density covariates +0.552 [-0.929, 2.124]; regime dummies (fast1, fast2) instead of density -0.032 [-1.633, 1.605]; density + dummies -0.232 [-1.895, 1.445]; published model on drives up to 2026-09-30 (n 217, before the latest change) +0.242 [-1.365, 2.019]; slow-regime drives only +0.198 [-1.366, 1.859]; before the latest change with a fast1 dummy +0.077 [-1.570, 1.829]. Every interval contains zero; the point estimate ranges from -0.23 to +0.99 with the cadence handling, i.e. its size and even its sign are not robust. The 23 drives of the latest regime move the published slope from +0.242 to +0.552 (+0.31). Era medians of the proxy: slow 124.1, fast1 132.2, fast2 154.8 mOhm (the fast2 level is 30.7 mOhm above slow, far more than the 1.5-1.7 mOhm cadence bias measured in (C); the model attributes the gap to its temperature and current covariates, which this study did not decompose); median HV-current interval 1.252 s (slow), 0.784 (fast1), 0.839 (fast2). (C) PROXY-LEVEL EMULATION (tools/cadence_emulate.py, the M379b method: every PID column of a fast-regime log thinned to the slow-regime interval distribution, seeded pools from 40 slow drives, 3 seeds, analyze_bytes re-run; emulated sampling sensitivity, NOT a causal cadence effect: PID order, I-V co-timing and jitter are not emulated): per-drive emulated minus original vreg_R_pack_mohm = -1.545 mOhm (median -1.678) for fast1 (52 drives, 20 days, day-clustered CI [-2.290, -0.658]) and -1.738 (9 drives, 5 days, CI [-3.321, -0.590]) for fast2: denser logging raises the proxy by about 1.5-1.7 mOhm (about 1.2 % of the level) with no change in the pack, as the M170 docstring states; 29 of the 90 fast-regime clean drives (32 %; fast1 15 of 67, fast2 14 of 23) lose the proxy altogether at slow sampling, so proxy availability itself depends on cadence in the latest regime. SAME-DRIVE slope comparison (213 drives = 152 slow + the 61 fast drives whose proxy survives emulation, identical on both sides): no covariate +0.9996 [-0.359, 2.381] original vs +0.708 [-0.631, 2.073] emulated (cadence accounts for 0.29 mOhm/month); published density design +0.483 [-0.979, 2.069] original vs +0.408 [-0.998, 1.914] emulated (the M170 density covariates absorb most of the cadence effect, about 0.07 remains). CONCLUSION (for wording): the cadence change does influence the computation; the published design controls most of it but not all of it (a regime-dummy design gives about zero), the fast2 regime contributes about +0.3 mOhm/month to the published point estimate, and no specification gives an interval excluding zero: report as 'no detectable resistance trend; point estimate cadence-dependent (-0.2 to +1.0 mOhm/month across cadence handling)', never as a fade rate. The stored note's sentence 'Sampling cadence IS controlled (M170)' overstates; proposed follow-up (needs spec, blind audit, Director): add the specification range and the emulation result to the powerFade disclosure, and report the proxy-availability loss. Not done here; nothing published changed. Caveats: 3 emulation seeds; the emulated fast2 comparison rests on 9 drives / 5 days; the emulation pool is 40 seeded slow drives.

## M392 (2026-10-09): Recalibration gate: one calibrated window-null drift rule for offsets and spread; batch-alone-outside-CI demoted to informational; not evaluable is soft

**Rationale.** Method change to the corpus-refit recalibration gate's FLAG LOGIC only (tools/recal_gate.py; spec analyses/M392_spec.md; blind audit pass; Director: accept). No change to any estimator, the master (MD5 64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525) or any payload value; the gate output is a superset of the old keys (window_null, mdd95, n_eff, nominal_vs_effective, not_evaluable, carry_forward added; nothing renamed). Rule: hard flag = pooled (old+batch) estimate outside the old 95% CI, or window-null p <= 0.01 over ALL contiguous k-day windows of the old corpus (k = the batch's observed days; n_windows >= 99); soft flag = p < 0.05, pooled shift > 0.25 of the old CI half-width, or not_evaluable (never hard). Offsets: deviation of the window ratio-of-sums from the old pooled estimate; spread: the existing joint Mahalanobis statistic with window validity = at least 8 drives with spread data (previously: at least as many drives as the batch). The comparison 'batch alone outside the old CI' is kept as the informational key new_only_outside_old_ci (it had fired on 50-71% of real historical batches, audit 60-74%: a k-day estimate against a CI built for a ~100-day pooled mean; it was the cause of the hard flags acknowledged at M376 and M388). Evidence (script output, analyses/M392_calibration.py, M392_calibration_spread.py, M392_backtest.py; real history replayed batch by batch against the preceding corpus, seed 42, 4000 draws): pooled-outside-CI fires on 0% (a 4-day batch would need to shift the offset by about 1.2 A to trigger it; effectively dead, kept); old spread block-null computable on only 43-64% of historical batches and 'p is None' counted as hard (M388: 5 valid windows); window-null p <= 0.05 fires on 0-5% of historical offset batches (k = 2..7; audit 5-10%); two-sample day-clustered bootstrap rejected (34% / 20% / 9-12% at k = 2 / 4 / >=7). Back-test of the new rules on the real ingestions: M310 (446 -> 489), M376 (489 -> 524), M388 (524 -> 554): no hard flag in any; soft only on spread coefficients at M310 (b0, bT) and M376 (bT), none at M388; joint spread tests now evaluable with 85-102 windows (was 5 at M388); offset window-null p = 0.58 (pass 1) / 0.57 (pass 2) at M388 and 0.49 / 0.45 at M376, i.e. those batches deviated ordinarily. The M376 and M388 acknowledgements (raised by the superseded batch-only rule) stand unedited; under M392 they replay as no hard flag. POWER, to be read with every pass: the offset minimum detectable shift (mdd95, 95th percentile of the window deviations) is about 0.39 A at k = 2, 0.24 A at k = 4, 0.14 A at k = 7, 0.11 A at k = 10 against an offset of about 0.38 A; at M388 it is 0.236 A (about 60% of the offset). A pass means no shift above mdd95 was detected; smaller shifts are not excluded; drift test not established. Limits (Director-accepted, disclosed): overlapping windows give only about N/k independent windows (n_eff = 25.5 at M388), so the nominal 1% hard level is effectively about 1/(n_eff+1) = 1/26 (roughly 3-4%); fewer than 99 windows caps the test at soft; a batch with fewer than 8 spread drives is not evaluable (soft, carry_forward) and can then only hard-flag through the pooled check; the null is centred on the old pooled estimate and ignores batch denominator size and calendar gaps; the replay has 19 / 10 batches, too few to verify the 1% level. Reviewer action on a soft or not_evaluable flag: the CHANGELOG acknowledgement names the quantity, k, drives, p or reason and mdd95 and states 'drift test not established for this batch'; never 'stable' or 'no drift'. Follow-ups (Director): simulated-shift power study; trailing-window and detrended null variant reported beside the rule (disagreement reported, not tuned away); carry-forward pooling of not_evaluable batches; null weighted by batch denominator and calendar gaps; re-check the realised false-alarm rate once more than 30 replay batches exist. Known-answer tests: tests/synthetic/test_recal_gate.py (window-null rank with a known null, hard only with >= 99 windows, capped soft below, not evaluable soft, n_eff, carry_forward).

## M391 (2026-10-09): Recalibration gate reports the rows each offset fit uses (pass 1 / pass 2); offset eligibility item closed as by design

**Rationale.** Reporting change in the corpus-refit recalibration gate (tools/recal_gate.py), no figure change, no change to any estimator, master or payload. Finding (script output, current 554-drive master): the gate re-fits the offset with the SAME eligibility as the pipeline estimator (compute_drive_summary_v6._v5_postprocess_master M13: residual, duration and median pack voltage present); the pipeline is deliberately two-pass: pass 1 (I_offset_A) fits all eligible rows, then ens_invalid = f_domain_2p = ens_outlier_v2 (hard physical rules, canonical exclusion) is derived from the pass-1 corrected residuals and pass 2 (I_offset_2p_A, columns *_corr2p) refits without those rows. So the gate was not misaligned; the published pass 2 IS the canonical-clean offset, and the counts that looked inconsistent were pass 1 vs pass 2 eligibility (pre-M388 master: 510 drives / 105 days vs 508 / 104; the audit's canonical-clean set is the pass-2 set) next to the gate's all-rows counts (524 / 108), which described the master, not the fits. ## M390 (2026-10-09): SoC logger-glitch rejection: short-side time guard and shared frame-loader hook (1 sample flagged, master unchanged)

**Rationale.** Method change (spec analyses/M390_spec.md; blind audit pass; Director: accept), no change to the master (MD5 64dfd0cbff3db404d9b83e180f777525 unchanged, 0 row diffs, ML16 untouched). SoC logger-glitch rejection (M388c rule: a sample is dropped iff both jumps to its time-adjacent samples are >= 20 pp and the two neighbours agree within 1.0 pp; edge samples never) gains a short-side time guard (min(t_b - t_a, t_c - t_b) <= 5 s; fixed, not tuned; a >= 20 pp move within 5 s would imply roughly 300 kW if CAP_KWH = 2.1 (verified:false), above the 150 kW motor rating (unverified); an order-of-magnitude plausibility bound; a spike whose both sides are long gaps is not flagged) and moves into the shared raw frame loader (soc_spike.despike_frame: the flagged SoC cell becomes missing, row alignment kept), so every cached-frame reader sees the glitch as missing; the per-drive code and the two rainflow functions pass times to the same rule (new module soc_spike.py, known-answer test tests/synthetic/test_soc_spike.py in CI). Corpus (script output, tools/data_health.py soc_spike): 552 files with a SoC channel, 605,604 SoC intervals, 1 sample flagged (2026-10-08 10-14-58: 69.5 / 0.0 / 69.5, intervals 45.775 s before and 1.569 s after, i.e. the first reading after a PID dropout), 0 samples that fail only the time guard, no other consecutive SoC jump >= 20 pp. DISCLOSED CORRECTION: the first design-time interval scan divided pandas-3 datetime64[us] integers as ns and understated every SoC interval 1000x (it suggested a 0.047 s window and a whole-span 5 s guard that would never have flagged the real glitch); found when the loader flagged nothing, re-measured with explicit units (SoC interval median 1.16 s, p99 2.47 s, p99.9 4.1 s, max 1791.7 s, 22 intervals over 60 s) and the guard redesigned before any apply. Hardening from the audit: a missing (NaT) time fails the guard, string time columns are coerced. Apply: fresh arrays builds with and without the patch from the same input (tools/m388c_rebuild_arrays.py) differ in exactly 4 value leaves, all SoC readers and all one removed sample on that drive: socHysteresis.nAtRiskStart 417811 -> 417810, crossVehicle.eventDetectors.socHysteresis.primary.nAtRiskStart 417811 -> 417810, socControlSurface.nSamplesTotal 699408 -> 699407, socBySpeed 0-20 km/h bin minimum SoC 0 -> 42 (and the seasonalCharts SocBySpeed all/shoulder mirror of it); the other 272 changed leaves are timestamps and hashes. Against the shipped payload the GTR-family blocks changed only in provenance labels (rerunMilestone / status M388 -> M390, source file hash); no GTR, seasonal or other value moved; delta_report.json: no flags. First real use of the M389 stage restamp_ingest (ran without stopping). tools/data_health.py now writes a soc_spike block (rule and constants verified:false, counts above, the flagged sample, the uncovered readers and that no time guard applies to them). Still NOT covered (named for disclosure): raw-bytes readers outside the frame loader - compute_summary_arrays._hf_perdrive (soc-balanced fuel dSoC, last minus first, interior spike has no effect), _fcs_snapshot (full-cell case-study SoC), _of_grid (warm-up / thermal fuel penalty SoC statistics), the frame_loader-is-None fallbacks, energy_mc_precompute (path to be confirmed), recon_engine (first-to-last dSoC, unaffected), m119v2_model (frozen, hash-gated, sees the glitch at 1 Hz). Wording: logger glitch rejection (flagged as missing), never a correction of data or figures; SoC is a logged BMS value.

## M387 (2026-10-09): Stop-go phase energy (_csg_events): NumPy helpers replace the per-window pandas chain (iloc, dropna, sum, clip); bit-identical; CrawlStopGo builder 8.6 -> 5.0 min

**Rationale.** The M386 profile showed about 204k Series.clip calls inside _csg_events._phase and 115k inside _phx (the M356 phase energy) costing roughly 210 s of a 1,663 s profiled regen_seasonal_raw run: each call slices a Series of a few samples, drops NaN, sums, clips and sums again, so pandas overhead dominates. compute_summary_arrays._csg_phase_np / _csg_phx_np (module level) do the same arithmetic on the precomputed float array: NaN removal by mask, sum() on the contiguous result (same summation), clip(lower=0) as np.where(x >= 0, x, 0.0), which is what pandas does (a -0.0 is kept). Verification: tests/synthetic/test_csg_phase_np.py compares the helpers with the verbatim former pandas code on 4,800 random windows (NaN runs, +0.0/-0.0, all-NaN and all-zero series, empty windows, negative and out-of-range indices): bit-identical including the sign of zero. Real data: regen_seasonal_raw --check --no-cache --only CrawlStopGo against the stored top-level block (written by the old code): parity superset with the same 15 splice-owned additive leaves as before (M384), 0 changed leaves. Measured (pinned Python 3.11.15, scratch copy, no cache, one run each): CrawlStopGo builder 5 min 01 s versus 8 min 35 s (1.71x). Other clip callers (_buffer_impulse_events about 8 s, _isc_context about 5 s in the profile) are not changed. No published value changes.

## M384 (2026-10-06): Parity guard of regen_seasonal_raw: superset equality with splice-registered additive leaves (Director ruling, blind audit PASS); diagnosis of the no-new-files rerun failure

**Rationale.** Diagnosis (analyses/M384_parity_diag.json): regen_seasonal_raw's byte-equality guard failed on a no-cache run for CrawlStopGo and EngineStartsByType with 0 changed values, because the stored blocks carry additive leaves written by post-build splices (post_splices blindAudit, 15 leaves; M362 per-type short-drive statistics, 44 leaves). A real ingestion rebuilds the top-level blocks fresh, so parity held there; a no-new-files rerun keeps the leaves, the two charts dropped out of refreshedRawCharts and leaf_guard stopped the run. The committed M341_check.json of M376 had been produced from cached results (framesLoaded cached), so its parity was never evaluated. Deviation from the M341 byte-equality rule (spec analyses/M384_spec.md Rev 2, Director ruling revise-then-go): tools/parity_compare.py accepts exact equality, or superset equality where the stored block has extra DICT keys only at paths registered by the owning splice (read from tools/post_splices.ADDITIVE_LEAVES and tools/m362_splice.ADDITIVE_KEYS), arrays of equal length compared element-wise; M341_check.json now records parityMode, additiveStoredLeaves and framesLoadedAllRows; the all-rows result is never taken from cache and parity is not evaluated without loaded frames; refreshedRawCharts gains additiveLeavesNotRefreshed. Blind audit (analytical-auditor, independent cases): 44 cases, 0 mismatches, no false-optimistic path. Live no-cache check: both charts superset (15 and 44 additive leaves), frames loaded 3,668 and 524. No published value changes; the guard does not verify the additive leaves themselves.

## M380 (2026-10-05): Regime-stratified view and regime-covariate re-run of the gross-throughput decision figures (0 flips); both estimators stored

**Rationale.** Milestone M380 of analyses/M380_spec.md (Rev 2 frozen before the run; Rev 3 documentation addendum after the audit and the ruling). Implements the M379b follow-up: a regime-stratified view and a regime covariate for the gross-throughput decision figures. Read-only scratch analysis (tools/regime_stratified.py): nothing in the master, the estimators or the published values changes; it reproduces the published EnergyIntensity values (all, warm, shoulder) and the warm_vs_shoulder adjusted contrast exactly before any variant runs. Inventory (script-written): 180 python files scanned; the gross-throughput family is referenced in 34; within a +-6 line window it co-occurs with a trend or test token in only two lines (an older follow-up script and the new script); the heuristic is static, the decision-bearing consumers (EfficChart adjusted contrasts, EnergyIntensity, riskColdEngineBattery Mann-Whitney) are covered by the exact reproductions; no trend of any quantity against cumulative GTC and no gross-throughput TOST was found; the partial-Spearman block uses no gross-throughput column and is out of scope. P1: warm 109 fast / 289 slow drives (25 / 69 days; fast share of gross throughput 19.7 %), shoulder 20 / 85 (8 / 28 days; 12.4 %), cold-insufficient 2 / 5 (non-identifiable, fewer than 5 days; warm_vs_cold not available, no substitute). P2 (observational): warm energy intensity fast 20.4 kWh/100 km (109 drives, 25 days) vs slow 16.4 (288, 69); shoulder 29.9 (19, 7) vs 26.6 (85, 28). P3: warm vs shoulder adjusted contrast -1.34 (CI -3.46 to +0.35); with a binary regime indicator -1.69 (-3.49 to +0.39); with a three-level indicator -1.19 (-3.51 to +1.37); the CI includes 0 in all three; regime-term VIF 1.02, condition number 4.6; support unchanged (397 warm / 104 shoulder); composition-adjusted fast-minus-slow difference within warm -1.23 (CI -2.58 to +0.34), within shoulder -2.83 (-7.84 to +2.28): the raw +24 % gap within warm is composition / regime period, never a cadence effect. P4 (emulated harmonisation sensitivity, not a correction; uniform r): energy-intensity shifts at most 0.06 of the original CI half-width at the emulated ratio 0.974 and its CI endpoints, 0.20 at the stress bound 0.908, 0.21 in the reverse direction at the central ratio, 0.82 at the reverse stress bound (material to report; a stress bound, not a plausible range). P5 arithmetic only: corpus gross-throughput sum 0.49 % lower if the fast drives were logged at the slow cadence (central), 1.75 % at the stress bound; reverse direction +2.2 % central. P6: cold-vs-warm Mann-Whitney p 0.280 original, 0.285 at the central ratio, 0.332 at the stress bound, 0.285 reverse; fast-only 0.56, slow-only 0.11. P7: 0 flips in any direction; no STOP. Observations ruled by the Director: (i) the descriptive slow-only warm-vs-shoulder contrast excludes 0 (-2.12, CI -4.21 to -0.24): a confounded subset, not a counted flip; (ii) METHOD DISAGREEMENT: the blind audit (definitions document sha256 e25f088c8715d0b6fd2e5a13a30f7262a5bd885553224bca8ec901a7950036d4; analyses/M380_audit.json) agrees exactly on the table, the regime-stratified warm energy intensity, the slow-equivalent warm intensity (16.996, shift -0.087) and the support counts, but its plain OLS gives the same sign with a CI marginally on either side of zero depending on the seed (variant a -1.81, CI -3.74 to -0.07) against the repository's standardised common-support estimator; both estimators are stored in the payload and the side of zero is described as estimator- and seed-dependent and marginal. Payload and dashboard: additive block loggerCadence.stratified (frozen summary with its basis, rebuilt by the cadence_regime stage from the committed files), a Methods paragraph and a line in the EnergyIntensity note bound to it (A2 REQUIRED checks in semantic_gate.py); spec P8 deviation recorded: the adjusted contrast is stored in cohort_arrays.json and is NOT rendered in the dashboard, so no line sits next to it, and the Director ruled that it is not rendered now. .github/workflows/ci.yml only adds the new test. Open: the generator / traction family (f_gen, eta_bus) is not covered; follow-up with recon_engine emulation. Language: observational, confounded by season, ambient and drive mix; a regime period, never a cadence effect; slow-equivalent / sensitivity, never corrected; not M299-reproducible.

## M379b (2026-10-05): Emulated sampling-sensitivity study of the pipeline keys to the logger PID cadence (gross throughput 0.974 at the slow-regime interval distribution); disclosure and headline sensitivity line

**Rationale.** Split M379b of analyses/M379_spec.md (Rev 2-3 frozen before the run; Rev 4 documentation addendum after the audit and ruling). Emulated sampling sensitivity, NOT a causal cadence effect: 130 of the 131 fast-regime drives (26 days; the 131st has no energy block) have every PID column thinned independently to the slow-regime interval distribution (dithered selection; pools from 40 seeded slow drives; the mean interval below 5 s matches the slow pool within 0.4 %, the median is quantized 1.49 vs 1.26 s; 20 seeds per drive) and the pipeline function analyze_bytes is re-run on the original and the emulated logs (nothing is written to the master; the offset keys are recomputed with the frozen formula, checked against the master to 5e-05 kWh). Validation: keep-all identity maximum difference 0.0; analyze_bytes reproduces the master gross throughput exactly on 230 drives; a ramp and a step current signal with a known integral run through the pipeline (ramp exact at the native cadence, thinning does not bias it, the step moves by about one interval over its span); the peak keys (negative controls) move. Results (analyses/M379_cadence_sensitivity.json; all from the script): gross throughput ratio emulated / original 0.974 (95 % day-clustered CI 0.973-0.976), 0.908 at twice the slow intervals, 0.917 for a control that thins 100 slow-regime drives to twice their intervals (dose-response consistent); gross discharge, gross charge, FCE and rainflow EFC move the same way; distance 1.000; n_I_samples scales by 0.595. Classification at the slow level under the frozen margins: cadence-sensitive (outside the margin, CI excludes the neutral value): gross throughput, gross discharge, gross charge, net_draw_kwh_corr (+0.0019 kWh per drive), energy_residual_kwh, rf_efc, fce, ev_kwh_per100km; not established as insensitive (outside the margin, CI includes the neutral value): net_draw_per100km_corr (shift 0.034 kWh/100 km, CI -0.013 to 0.082; below the quarter of the EnergyIntensity.all CI half-width, 0.52, which is necessary but not sufficient); insensitive within the margin: distance, offset_kwh_removed, engine_on_pct, regen_share_of_charge, ev_dist_pct, soc_delta_kwh. Robustness: the nearest-sample variant (30 drives, 5 seeds) classifies regen_share_of_charge as sensitive (flagged: classification depends on the emulator). Corpus arithmetic (descriptive, under the emulation; no published value is corrected): fast-regime drives carry 19.0 % of the corpus gross throughput, so the sum would be about 0.5 % lower had they been logged at the slow cadence. Deviations (pre-registered in Rev 3 before the run, accepted by the Director): the interval match is evaluated on the mean, not the median; the emulated I-V co-timing gap is 43 % below the slow regime (outside the +-25 % flag: the emulation likely understates that mechanism); the pipeline distance differs from the master's post-processed distance on 1 of 230 study-set drives (maximum 2.94 km; the paired differences use the same pipeline distance for both versions). Limits: the generator / traction reconstruction (f_gen, eta_bus, GTR blocks) and the fuel keys are not covered; fast regime confined to Aug-Sep and Oct (confounded with season and drive mix); fast -> slow direction only. Blind audit (analytical-auditor, definitions document sha256 9068892e6868c8afa082f0032bc445a0951941195e66546122f7665ae17062a6; analyses/M379_audit.json; input lists in analyses/M379_audit_inputs/): regime counts and runs identical, identity 0.0, mean interval +0.32 %, 10-drive gross-throughput ratio 0.9752 (study-side 0.9786, seed SD 0.0105) and 0.9108 at factor 2, both outside [0.99, 1.01]. Director ruling recorded in the spec Rev 4: disclosure wording, the not-established class wording, the headline sensitivity line (next to GTC / FCE / rainflow EFC, bound to S.loggerCadence.sensitivity), language_gate rules (cadence effect proven / measured / corrected, corrected for cadence, cadence bias), distance disclosure. The payload block loggerCadence carries the frozen study summary with its basis (master MD5, 524 drives) and is rebuilt by the cadence_regime stage from the committed study file; .github/workflows/ci.yml only adds tests/synthetic/test_cadence_emulate.py to the unit-test step. Follow-ups (Director): a regime-stratified report and a regime covariate for every time-trend, seasonal or TOST figure that uses gross throughput (GTC, FCE, rainflow EFC, kWh/100 km), escalating if any decision flips; emulation through recon_engine with the refresh of the five stale GTR blocks. Language: emulated sampling sensitivity, never a cadence effect that is proven / measured / corrected; not M299-reproducible.

## M379a (2026-10-05): Logger PID-cadence regime per drive (descriptive covariate, sidecar + payload block) and the amended cadence disclosure: two fast regimes

**Rationale.** Split M379a of analyses/M379_spec.md (Rev 2, Director revise applied; frozen before any run). New stage cadence_regime (tools/cadence_regime.py): regime per drive derived deterministically from the master column I_sample_period_s (median update interval of the HV-current PID): fast if below 1.05 s (the midpoint of the empty gap), slow if at or above, null if missing (12 drives with fewer than three HV-current samples: 11 with none, 1 with two); STOP on any drive inside the declared empty gap [1.0, 1.1) s (the distribution is bimodal: 131 drives in 0.70-1.0 s, 0 drives in 1.0-1.1 s, 381 drives in 1.1-1.9 s; script output). Written as the sidecar cadence_regime.csv and the additive payload block loggerCadence (rule, counts 131 fast / 381 slow / 12 null on 27 / 80 days, the runs in time order, the days with both regimes 2026-09-06 and 2026-10-01); the master and its MD5 anchor are not touched; the block carries its artifact stamp and the stage is idempotent. AMENDED DISCLOSURE (Director required change 8; supersedes the framing of the M376 entry): the logger PID cadence has two fast-cadence regimes in the corpus, not one: 2026-08-14 10:10 to 2026-09-06 12:29 (100 drives, 22 days) and 2026-10-01 16:46 onward (30 drives, 4 days; the change described at M376), plus one isolated fast drive on 2026-05-13 18:30; slow runs are 2026-05-15 to 2026-08-13 (224 drives, 54 days) and 2026-09-06 13:08 to 2026-10-01 08:14 (157 drives, 26 days). The effect of the regime on the pipeline keys is NOT yet quantified (emulated sampling-sensitivity study = M379b); observational comparisons across regimes are confounded by season, ambient and drive mix; published figures that span the 2026-08-14 to 2026-09-06 run carry this open caveat. The dashboard Methods block (Data provenance) now renders the disclosure from the payload (A2 REQUIRED check in semantic_gate.py binds the counts, the days, the runs, 'not yet quantified' and the confound statement). Tests: tests/synthetic/test_cadence_regime.py (rule, STOP inside the gap, nulls do not split a run, days with both regimes, block statements). ## M377c (2026-10-05): gtrClosure refreshed on the live corpus as an ingestion stage (292 drives); expected-set rule, one-time re-pin after the M376 recalibration

**Rationale.** Milestone M377c of analyses/M377c_spec.md (Rev 3; Director rulings Rev 2-3). Closes the carry-forward left open by M377b: stage gtr_closure_refresh (tools/gtr_closure_refresh.py) recomputes gtrClosure on the live corpus with the producers in --ingest mode: expected-set rule (every previous closure ID must stay eligible; the new IDs are listed) instead of the M336 baseline equality, raw originals sha256 check, ens_outlier_v2 == ens_invalid check, previous-ID per-drive identity against a pinned file (analyses/gtr_closure_record.json), allow-listed splice (gtrClosure and staleBlocks minus gtrClosure; crossval stays), delta to analyses/gtr_closure_delta.json and delta_report. STOP on a key-set change, a flag / verdict flip, an estimate outside its previous 95% CI, a type change (a stratum crossing n >= 10), a list-length change outside the documentation lists, a missing previous ID or a changed pin; escalation band 10% relative (0.01 absolute when |previous| < 0.1) and n_days 20%. ## M371 (2026-10-04): CI cost cut: pull_request-only triggers, per-ref concurrency, one merged job (GitHub Actions minutes at 90 %)

**Rationale.** Tooling only (owner request in chat, 2026-10-04: GitHub alert "used 90 % of the Actions minutes"; "Apply 1-3 and consider option 4"). Analysis from the run history (gh run list): 268 runs since Oct 1 (207 push, 61 pull_request), about 1,065 wall minutes with two parallel jobs per run, i.e. about 2,000 billed minutes (an estimate from run history, not the billing page). Causes: the workflow triggered on push to claude/** AND on pull_request (every commit of a PR branch ran twice: about 185 of the 207 push runs), on every merge to main (the merged code had already passed in the PR run), without cancelling superseded runs, with two jobs that each checked out the ~1 GB repository (about 105 s of every job; per-step timing of a recent run: checkout 103-113 s, pip 15-20 s, unit tests 95 s, release_check 194 s). Change to .github/workflows/ci.yml: (1) triggers = pull_request and workflow_dispatch only (the PR run validates the branch head; manual dispatch for a branch without a PR); (2) concurrency group ci-<ref> with cancel-in-progress; (3) no run on push to main; (4) the two jobs (checks, release-gate) merged into ONE job named release-gate: one checkout and one dependency install per run, the cheap unit tests first (a failure stops the job early), then release_check.py; timeout-minutes 30. Estimated cost per run about 7 billed minutes instead of about 11, and about 1 run per push to an open PR instead of about 2-3 (push + PR + main): roughly 70-75 % fewer minutes per milestone. Consequences recorded in CLAUDE.md and the handoff: there is no push trigger, so a branch without a PR is not checked by CI (run release_check.py locally; keep pushes to an open PR few); the merge condition applies to the PR run's check(s): one check, release-gate (four before). No branch protection or rulesets exist on this plan (the API returns 403 for private free repositories), so no required check names change. Not done: paths-ignore for docs-only changes (it can leave a PR without any check status, which conflicts with the merge rule); a self-hosted runner and making the repo public were considered and not recommended. No code, payload, dashboard or figure change; drive_master.csv MD5 unchanged.

**Rationale.** Defect repair (not an error correction of results). float(master.get('I_offset_A_applied') or 0.0) kept NaN, so the battery power of two published per-drive rows (20260813_145651, 20260813_150341) was NaN, dropped out of the traction sum, and gave f_gen = 1 and batt->traction = 0 by construction (scan: exactly these two rows). Root cause: the master stamps ONE global offset (compute_drive_summary_v6._v5_postprocess_master; n = 475 calibrated drives, 1 distinct value at 4 dp) only where energy_residual_kwh, duration_s and V_pack_median are all non-NaN; 14 rows lack it (all energy_residual and V_pack_median NaN); 12 of them have no fuel_recon row (10 without a fuel-flow PID, 1 zero distance, 1 with no usable battery chain), only the two Aug 13 files carry a published row. Repair (Director Rev 2): fail-closed helper resolve_offset/corpus_offset in fuel_recon.py; a NaN offset takes the corpus-applied constant read from the master at run time (the offset is imputed with the corpus-applied constant shared by the 475 calibrated drives; never typed); the run aborts if calibrated offsets are not single-valued; exclusion only behind --exclude-nan-offset with the count written (fuel_recon_offset_report.json). Control build, no new drive: fuel_recon_master.csv changed on those 2 rows only (10 cells); summary_arrays.json 32 leaf differences, all allow-listed and equal to the pre-registered effect table (analyses/M349_effect.json): reconstructed/estimated corpus f_gen 0.467 -> 0.466 (day-clustered bootstrap CI 0.381-0.544, 260 drives, 50 days; the change -0.0019 is far inside the published CI 0.384-0.545), gen->traction 8.64 -> 8.62, batt->traction 9.85 -> 9.89, traction gross 18.49 -> 18.51 kWh/100 km, Warm f_gen 0.493 -> 0.491, Shoulder and gtrClosure unchanged (control), drive_master.csv MD5 unchanged. Sensitivities: exclusion (258 drives) 0.466, offset 0 0.466. The two per-drive rows move f_gen 1.0 -> 0.575 and 0.363; they are short, coarsely sampled drives (321 s and 869 s; 72/238 current samples; I and V alternate about 1.8 s apart) so their per-drive values are low precision. Warnings: W1 shift of the corpus pack-temperature distribution (>= 1 grid step from the UNSNAPPED carried quantile; seasonal and confounded; not model invalidity or degradation), W2 cold candidate on a band that does not overlap the lowest final level's band, W3 range extension >= 1 grid step (new-spec trigger), W3-info any extension (zero tolerance, with events and days outside), W4 support loss, F03 flag for a changed raw hash of a frozen basis drive (separate from drift). Gate (release_check.py): FAIL on a missing or stale monitor (masterMd5, drive count, cache sha256, cache file set), a changed selection code (m119v2_model.py, tools/m318_run.py, tools/m320_ladder.py; whole files, so comment-only edits force a rebase), a ladder basis that differs from socHysteresisV2.corpusSizeAtRecompute (a V2 refit without a re-derived ladder), and an unacknowledged W2/W3; WARN for W1, W3-info, W4 and F03 flags. W2 REDEFINED POST HOC (rev 3) after the pre-registered falsification check fired on the zero-drift corpus; Director-reviewed; the fix is structural (candidate level <= lowest final level - 2 x BAND, constants imported from the M320 config) and its quiet result on today's data was known when it was chosen.
