MC with `seed=20260822`, B=20,000) — confirms the MC recompute is fully
deterministic and this milestone's code changes are purely additive with
zero side effects on any pre-existing computation. `drive_master.csv` MD5
verified unchanged before and after (this milestone touches no drive-level
data, only derived arrays).

**Methodology note on this session's execution environment.** The
sandboxed verification environment used to implement and test this
milestone enforces a per-command execution time limit shorter than a

**Trigger.** Andrii's line-by-line review of seven dashboard sections, including

speed channel only, with no OBD-generic fallback. Silently dropped **90 of

## M218 (2026-09-04) — RPM histogram: 1400-1600 bin split into its two governed setpoints, same +/-25rpm logic as the M205 2000rpm fix

**Trigger.** Andrii: "let's implement following the same logic as for 2000+/-25
RPM" — closing M205's own ancillary finding (flagged, not acted on at the
time) that the "1400-1600 secondary mode" is actually two distinct governed
setpoints under one label.

**Method — deliberately identical to M205's, not a new approach.** Standalone
1Hz-grid re-derivation (same `_RawAccum` convention, independent read of every
raw file), this time across the full 320-drive corpus and extended down to
1400 and up to 1975 (the M205 boundary) to characterize the whole region in
one pass rather than two. For each spike: weighted center of mass, then a
+/-25rpm window around the rounded center (mirroring 2000.30→2000→1975-2025
exactly); valley/decay-tail density checked on both sides to confirm genuine
separation, not residual spike mass.

**Result.** Two setpoints confirmed, both sharper than the 2000rpm mode
(>90% of each spike's own mass sits in a single 10rpm sub-bin):
- ~1500rpm: weighted center 1499.69-1500.08 rpm (window-dependent) → 1500 →
  window **1475-1525**.
- ~1589rpm: weighted center 1588.62-1589.29 rpm (window-dependent) → 1589 →
  window **1564-1614**.

True background/valley density: 10.1 s/rpm (1400-1475, decay-in from the
300-1400 transient band), 21.9 s/rpm (1525-1564, between the two spikes),
29.7 s/rpm (1614-1975, rising shoulder toward the 2000rpm mode) — all far
below either spike's own in-window density (274 and 183 s/rpm respectively).
Corpus-wide corrected occupancy (pooled, engine-on-relative %): 1475-1525
2.4%, 1525-1564(valley) 0.1%, 1564-1614 1.6%, 1614-1975(valley) 1.9% — vs the
old single "1400-1600" (2.5%) + "1600-1975"(valley, 1.9-2.0%) pair. Mass
conserved exactly: new-bin sum == old "1400-1600" + "1600-1975" == 35,172 s
at this session's snapshot.

**Engine-load separation (investigated alongside the bin fix, not itself
encoded in the histogram).** The two setpoints are cleanly distinguished by
engine load: `eng_load_calc` median 31% vs 46% (IQRs barely overlap), boost
-0.41 vs -0.10 bar, coolant 54°C vs 77°C — consistent across 76-77 of the
corpus's 77 driving dates (not a logging-era artifact), NOT separated by
`drive_type`. Reported in the dashboard prose as a hypothesis consistent with
(not proof of) two adjacent rungs on the generator's discrete load-point
ladder already established at M41/M118 — resolved one level finer, not a new
mechanism. Deliberately NOT built as a load-conditioned bin split or a new
detector: that would be a materially bigger change than what was asked for
this milestone (a bin-edge fix, mirroring M205 exactly).

**Fix.** `RPM_HIST_EDGES`/`RPM_HIST_LABELS`: the single `1400`/`1600` edge

## M217 (2026-09-03) — H-01/F-12 resolved: energyUncertaintyMC moves from manual carry-forward to full recompute every ingestion (Andrii decision)

**Trigger.** The second of the two M207 Tier-2 audit items got its decision this
session: full-recompute-every-ingestion, over disable-when-stale or refresh-
every-K-drives.

**Implementation.** `build_summary_arrays()` gains a new `recompute_energy_mc`
parameter (default `True`, unlike `recompute_m119v2` which stays opt-in/`False`
— this one is not OOM-bound, costs ~185-200s single-threaded at the current
corpus size, well under the cost of a routine ingestion's other steps). When
true and `raw_dir` is supplied, it runs `energy_mc_precompute.build()` (raw I/V
re-integration on the 500-2000ms tolerance grid, 308/320 metric-valid drives)
then `energy_uncertainty_mc.build()` (20,000-draw MC) in-process, sourcing the
offset point estimate + 95% CI live from the already-computed
`offsetUncertainty` block rather than re-deriving it — placed after
`offsetUncertainty`/`ledgerCrossCheck` in the function body for that reason,
not immediately after `socHysteresisV2` where M119-v2's analogous flag lives.
Falls back to carry-forward (tagged `carriedForward_recomputeFailed`, error
message attached) if the recompute raises, so a transient failure can't silently
drop the key. A `recomputePolicy` string documenting the decision is stamped on
the shipped block either way.

**Bug caught before shipping.** In-process chaining of the two scripts'
`build()` functions bypassed an implicit contract: `energy_uncertainty_mc.build()`
reads each drive's tolerance grid via string keys (`d['grid'][str(t)]`), which
is only true after the JSON file round-trip both scripts' own `__main__` CLI
performs (`json.dump` then `json.load` stringifies dict keys) — `TOL_GRID_MS`
itself is a list of ints, so the in-memory `grid` dict has int keys. Fixed by
replicating the round-trip explicitly (`json.loads(json.dumps(...))`) in the
new orchestration code, rather than changing either script's separately-
validated on-disk JSON contract.

**Result.** `energyUncertaintyMC.grossThroughputMC.nominalReleasedThroughputKwh`
1259.3405 → **1263.7067 kWh**, matching `meta.grossThroughputKwh` (1263.7 kWh,
320-drive corpus) to 0.00% — the +0.35% staleness disclosed at M215/M216 is
cleared. Validation re-integration deviation from shipped `drive_master.csv`
columns: max 5e-05 kWh (confirms the independent re-implementation, as at
M208/M214). `energy_mc_precompute.py`/`energy_uncertainty_mc.py` themselves
unchanged — only `compute_summary_arrays.py` (new orchestration code) and the
one spliced `energyUncertaintyMC` key changed.

**Validation.** `py_compile` (`compute_summary_arrays.py`,
`energy_mc_precompute.py`, `energy_uncertainty_mc.py`) clean; strict JSON
re-parse (`allow_nan=False`) clean; neighboring-function signature guard
(`_headroom_utilization_summary`/`_regime_transition`/`_heat_soak_carryover`/
`_thermal_step_response`/`_dissipation_census`) confirmed intact post-edit;
`build_html.js` provenance gate confirms `energyUncertaintyMC: nominal
1263.7067 kWh vs current 1263.7 kWh (-0.01 kWh, 0%)`; the pre-existing
hardcoded-snapshot-literal WARN (7 literals, unrelated to this change) verified
present identically against the pristine pre-session `summary_arrays.json` too
— not a regression. jsdom: 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors, **0 semantic
warnings** (both `socHysteresisV2` and `energyUncertaintyMC` now current, so
neither disclosed-staleness semantic gate fires). T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all
PASS (T-01 golden snapshot INFO-drift n=289→320, pre-existing, non-gating).
Isolation diff vs pristine Project Knowledge `summary_arrays.json`: **exactly
one key changed** (`energyUncertaintyMC`), 0 added/removed, 125/126 other keys
byte-identical. `drive_master.csv` unchanged (this session: code + one spliced
array key only, no ingestion).

## M216 (2026-09-03) — M119-v2 full recompute at the 320-drive corpus (explicit
user request); M148 OOM root cause fixed, not merely worked around

**Trigger.** Andrii explicitly requested a recompute of M119 and M119-v2 on
the current 320-drive corpus, flagging sandbox compute limits.

**M119 (v1, `socHysteresis`).** Already current — unlike v2 this block is
recomputed unconditionally on every `build_summary_arrays()` call (not
gated behind a flag), so M215's routine ingestion already refreshed it for
the 320-drive corpus. `nDrivesCovered=318` (2 of 320 drives lack a usable
per-second frame for this detector's own gating, unrelated to the
corpus-wide drive count elsewhere). No action needed.

**M119-v2 (`socHysteresisV2`) — frozen at n=259 since M147, now fresh at
n=320.** `run_ladder`'s GLM-fit sequence was isolated at M148 as a
reproducible OOM kill in this environment's <=4GB-RAM sandbox; every
session since M148 correctly deferred the recompute per the standing
opt-in policy (M179's `frozenBasis` freeze stamp). This session:

- **Root-cause fix, not a workaround.** Added explicit memory hygiene to
  `m119v2_model.py`: `del` + `gc.collect()` at every fold boundary in
  `oos_predict`, every candidate boundary in `sensitivity_screen`, every
  ladder-rung boundary in `run_ladder` (keeping only the `fiveVarDur` and
  `socOnly` prediction vectors — the two actually read downstream — and
  dropping `socSpeed`/`fourVar`'s), every 20 files in `_corpus_tables`, and
  between the START/STOP passes in `build_m119v2`. statsmodels'
  `GLMResults`/`GLM` hold reference cycles CPython's refcounting alone
  cannot reclaim; across ~120 fold/candidate fits per side these
  accumulated unreclaimed and caused the M148 OOM. This is pure cleanup —
  no change to `fit_glm`, `DesignSpec`, or any spline/interaction term —
  verified by smoke tests on 15/60/150-drive subsets before the full run.
- **Safety margin, not the actual fix.** A session-scoped 4 GB swapfile
  (`fallocate`+`mkswap`+`swapon` at `/home/claude/swapfile`, not persisted
  across sandbox sessions) was added as a precaution. It was not needed:
  swap usage stayed at 0 B throughout; peak RSS was 1874 MB, comfortably
  under the ~3.6 GB available even without swap. The memory-hygiene patch
  alone resolves the M148 ceiling.
- **Timing (single core).** Full run: 689.9 s (~11.5 min). Breakdown:
  corpus tables (raw CSV parse + 1 Hz grid + at-risk sampling, 320 files)
  348.8 s → `len(S)`=306,228, `len(T)`=269,315; `run_ladder` START 51.7 s,
  STOP 45.8 s; `sensitivity_screen` START 94.8 s, STOP 123.7 s; day-cluster
  bootstrap + `assemble` (final cluster-robust fit, partial dependence,
  surfaces) 25.1 s.
- **Fit comparison, n=259 (frozen, M147) → n=320 (fresh, M216):**
  - `nDays` 63→77; `speedSources` vcm 230/230 unchanged, `obd_fallback`
    29→90 (all 61 new drives fell to the OBD speed fallback — cross-checked

  - START `fiveVarDur`: logLoss 0.07966→0.07398; PR-AUC 0.0625→0.0594 (CI
    [0.0572,0.0677]→[0.0535,0.0639]); calSlope 0.962→0.976; calIntercept

    still non-overlapping with `fiveVarDur`'s CI at n=320, same as at n=259.
  - STOP `fiveVarDur`: logLoss 0.07409→0.07369; PR-AUC 0.0918→0.0918
    (unchanged to 3 s.f.; CI [0.0859,0.1025]→[0.0849,0.1011]); calSlope
    0.934→0.934 (unchanged); calIntercept −0.259→−0.241. `socOnly` PR-AUC CI
    [0.0353,0.0406]→[0.0361,0.0414] — still non-overlapping.
  - Ladder is still monotonic (socOnly→socSpeed→fourVar→fiveVarDur improves
    Brier/logLoss/PR-AUC every step, both models, both fits) — the
    headline finding is stable under a 24% larger, 14-day-longer corpus,

  - Sensitivity-screen retained-candidate *composition* is unchanged (START:
    none of socSince/coolant/keyOnS retained at either n; STOP:

## M215 (2026-09-03) — Routine ingestion: 5 new Sep 3 drives (315→320); determinism
proof + config mirror re-synced to the new corpus size

Standard incremental append per standing workflow, no methodology change.
Single-day batch: three cold-morning micro-trips (D1–D3, all under 1.5km,
+14°C constant) followed by two evening legs (D4 1.8km at +19°C, D5 11.0km
across +15→+14°C), 16.1km total. All 5 files carry the same 78/79-column
raw schema variant seen throughout the recent batches (header-verified
before ingestion, not assumed — the "10 sec" instantaneous-consumption
column is present/absent per-file exactly as in prior sessions, handled by
name-based column lookup, not position). All 5 are ens_outlier_v2-clean,
sign_check ok, f_domain-clean, fully urban (pct_highway 0.0% on D1–D4;

D5 (`20260903_213855.csv`, 11.0km) is the batch's dominant leg by both

## M213 (2026-09-03) — Dashboard chart-review batch: label collisions, one stale

## bracket-notation band, and a box/interval-plot redesign

**Trigger.** Andrii reviewed the dashboard end-to-end and flagged a list of
chart-level defects and one open design question:
- `ENGINE-ON FRACTION BY ROAD SPEED` band labels used raw pandas `Interval`
  bracket notation (`[70, 200)`), and the open top bin's `200` upper bound
  was never a real observed speed.
- `114-Day History`: marker date-labels overlapping/clipped.
- `3 — Battery SoC Band by Speed` and `Duration distribution by drive type
  (M74)`: median-value labels partially covered by their own IQR box.
- `2 — Engine Warm-Up Curve`: redundant "80°C — thermostat / optimal
  efficiency" label.
- `Coolant / Oil Warm-Up & Thermal Lag`: no axis-unit legend on either axis.
- M119-v2 twin thermal-transition maps: Y-axis label partially off-canvas.
- `C — Cycle Rate by Driving Condition` / `E — Engine ON/OFF Cycling`:
  lollipop-chart mean-value labels overflowing their marker circles, plus a
  question on whether the 0-anchored stem and the "engine-on ≈50%" framing
  were correct.
- `R — Regenerative Energy Analysis` (By speed zone): efficiency labels
  overlapping the connecting polyline.
- `1 — C-Rate vs Battery Temperature Risk Map`: is "20-40°C optimal" an
  accurate Li-ion NMC claim?
- `Battery Thermal Pattern`: redundant "<XX drives — composition changes"
  label.
- `Battery Temperature — Observed Range`: reviewed for a 5-point redesign
  (box/interval plot, per-dimension panels, long-haul as its own panel, the
  corpus record as a callout instead of a bar, one consistent color).

**Diagnosis.**

1. *Band labels.* `_thermal_fuel_penalty`'s `bySpeed` table built its label
   with bare `str(sbnd)` on a `pd.cut(..., right=False)` `Interval` —
   `[70, 200)`. `200` was a permissive `pd.cut` ceiling only (chosen to
   safely exceed any recorded speed), never a real value; the true max
   speed *within this 42-drive cold-start subset* is 137 km/h (verified by
   re-running the qualifying-drive filter directly against raw_dir). The
   corpus-wide max (170 km/h, across all 315 drives) is a different, larger
   number that does not describe what this specific chart summarizes.

2. *History labels.* `daysSpan` is now 114 with 76 plotted points on the
   same fixed-width canvas the M72 label-selection logic was tuned for.
   Three compounding failures: (a) the three fixed-day milestone
   annotations (Jun 9-13/19/22-27) now compress into ~57px of a 360px plot
   and their text collided regardless of exact placement; (b) the
   forward-scan MINGAP selection could still leave two tail labels closer
   than the gap threshold once measured edge-to-edge (the last label is
   right-anchored and extends left, the previous one is centre-anchored and
   extends both ways — pure anchor-to-anchor spacing didn't account for
   that asymmetry); (c) circles and labels were interleaved point-by-point
   in a single render pass, so on any densely-logged stretch a *later*
   point's circle painted over an *earlier* point's text in SVG paint
   order, clipping it (visible as "17 Ju" — the trailing "l" eaten by the
   next marker). Separately, the X-axis month ticks were three literal
   `<text>` elements at hardcoded days 5/26/48 (May/Jun/Jul) — authored
   when the corpus ended in July; Aug and Sep were silently missing from
   the axis with no error, just an axis that quietly stopped growing.

3. *Box-label overlap.* Both `SocBySpeed` and `DriveDurationDist` anchored
   their median-value label 4px above the *median line*, which sits inside
   the box fill whenever the box's top edge (q3) is close to the median —
   thin boxes hid the label under their own fill.

4. *M119-v2 Y-axis label.* `<text x={8} y={mt+8} transform="rotate(-90 8
   ...)">` — with `textAnchor` defaulting to `"start"`, the glyphs run
   *away* from the pivot in the rotated direction, pushing almost the
   entire label above `y=0` and off the left edge of this inner `<svg>`
   (no `viewBox`/`overflow:visible` here, unlike the outer chart svgs that
   already use the correct centred-pivot pattern).

5. *Lollipop circle labels.* `fontSize={8}` on 4-character cycle-rate
   values ("15.4") and up to 3-digit engine-start values ("113") inside an
   `r=8` (16px-diameter) circle — measured too wide to fit cleanly.
   Separately: the 0-anchored "stem" in both lollipop charts (`x1={xP(0)}`)
   is an intentional design choice — a magnitude-from-origin bar layered
   under the translucent true-range band, not a bug — confirmed by reading
   the component and cross-checked against the legend text already printed
   under each chart ("● = mean · | = median · bar = full observed range").
   The "engine-on ≈50%" prose (`Z.find(z=>z.pct>=50)`) was independently
   re-derived from `S.engineOnBySpeed` and is correct: it reports the
   `60-80` km/h zone (56% ≥ 50%), not `40-60` (46%, the fallback string
   that only fires if no zone crosses 50%) — the on-chart 50% line is a
   fixed reference gridline, not a data value, and no zone's pct is
   literally 50.

6. *Regen zone labels.* `<text x={cx+7} y={...}>` placed the efficiency
   value beside the diamond at the same height, directly in the path of
   the connecting polyline on any upward-sloping segment between zones.

7. *C-rate "optimal" range.* Checked `20-40°C` (`cRateRefLines.zones`)
   against published Li-ion NMC guidance (Battery University and
   peer-reviewed sources on NMC thermal aging/plating risk): the commonly
   cited window for NMC is roughly 15-45°C, with ~25°C singled out as the
   single "sweet spot" in several sources. `20-40°C`, with the caption's
   already-disclosed plating/aging thresholds (~20°C, ~44°C), sits
   comfortably inside that range — defensible as stated. No code change.

8. *Battery Temperature — Observed Range.* `RangeBar` rendered only a
   plain lo-hi filled bar with no median/IQR marker (medPeak existed only
   in prose), one arbitrary color per row assembled from unrelated
   per-group palettes (a genuine rainbow with no shared meaning once all
   groups render together), and the single-row "corpus record" group drawn
   as a nearly invisible sliver bar at the far right of a 0-51 scale.
   `_battery_temp_ranges`'s `_bar()` helper already collects the full
   per-drive Sensor-1 `peaks` array per group but only reduced it to
   `medPeak` — the p25/p75 needed for a proper box was one `np.percentile`
   call away.

**Fix.**

1. `compute_summary_arrays.py` — `_thermal_fuel_penalty`: band labels
   rebuilt as clean dash notation (`"0-5"`, `"5-20"`, `"20-40"`, `"40-70"`,
   `"70-137"`) from `_OF_SPEED_BINS` directly, with the open top bin's
   display bound to `ceil(D['spd'].max())` for *this* subset — self-healing
   as the corpus grows, same convention as the M212 dateSpan text, rather
   than a second hardcoded literal replacing the first. **Flagged for
   Andrii:** this ties the label to the cold-start subset's own observed
   max (currently 137), not the whole-corpus 170 — a deliberate choice
   favoring what the chart actually summarizes over a number that reads
   as more "complete" but doesn't describe this data. Isolation-diffed
   clean (only the 5 `band` strings changed).

2. `xtrail_summary.jsx` — `HistoryView`: (a) the three annotations now sit
   on three fixed vertical tiers so they cannot collide with each other
   regardless of how narrow the corpus growth squeezes their shared
   column; (b) label selection rewritten as a single backward greedy scan
   anchored on the always-shown last point (`MINGAP=60`, widened from the
   naive 46/48 to account for the right-anchored last label's asymmetric
   extent), replacing the forward-scan-plus-patch approach; (c) rendering
   split into two passes — every circle first, then every kept label on
   top — so a label can never be occluded by a marker painted after it,
   plus a white text halo (`paintOrder="stroke"`) so a label landing on a
   dense run of same-day markers stays legible against the coloured dots
   underneath; (d) month-axis ticks now derived from the first point
   actually carrying each new month in its own date label, so Aug/Sep
   appear now and the axis keeps growing on its own as the corpus does.

3. `SocBySpeed` and `DriveDurationDist`: median-value label now anchored
   4px above the box's top edge (q3) instead of the median line, so it
   never sits inside the fill regardless of box thickness.

4. M119-v2 `Surface()`: Y-axis label repositioned to the plot's vertical
   midpoint with `textAnchor="middle"`, matching the rotated-axis-title
   pattern already used correctly everywhere else in this file.

5. Lollipop mean-value label `fontSize` reduced 8→6.5 in both
   `CycleRateChart` (TypeView) and `EngineCyclingChart` (StartsView) to
   clear the 16px circle. No change to the 0-anchored stem or the 50%
   reference line — both correct as designed; findings above written back
   to Andrii rather than "fixed."

6. `RegenChart` ZoneChart: efficiency label recentred directly above each
   diamond (`textAnchor="middle"`, no rightward offset), clear of the
   polyline except at the point itself.

7. No change — literature-defensible as stated.

8. New `TempIntervalPlot` SVG component replaces `RangeBar` (now dead code,
   removed): thin whisker = true lo-hi extrema, box = IQR (new
   `p25Peak`/`p75Peak`), thick tick = median peak — the same convention
   `SocBySpeed`/`DriveDurationDist` already use, including the same
   above-box-top label-anchoring fix from item 3. `ambient`/`class`/
   `duration` each render in their own bordered panel (still sharing one
   °C x-scale across panels — °C is directly comparable across dimensions;
   only the per-row color was meaningless, not a shared axis) rather than
   one continuous list. `duration` (long-haul, single row) gets the same
   panel treatment rather than a different visual language for a one-row
   case. The `record` row is pulled out of the plot entirely into a
   standalone callout card (large red `51°C` + one line of context); the
   interval-plot rows now share one consistent slate-blue, with the
   record callout's red reserved specifically because it is a materially
   different kind of figure (a single-drive absolute ceiling, not a group
   distribution). `_battery_temp_ranges._bar()`: added `p25Peak`/`p75Peak`
   (IQR of the per-drive Sensor-1 peak) alongside the existing
   `lo`/`hi`/`medPeak`/`n`. Isolation-diffed clean (18 keys added, 0
   removed, 0 pre-existing values changed).

**Validation.** `py_compile` (all 8 touched/related `.py` files) clean;
`node --check` (`build_html.js`, `validate_jsdom.js`) clean; full jsdom
suite 9/9 tabs, 52/52 buttons, 0 console errors (baseline unchanged);
`validate_jsdom.js` semantic gate: 0 new warnings (the pre-existing
disclosed `socHysteresisV2`/`energyUncertaintyMC` staleness carries
forward unchanged, unrelated to this batch); isolation diff against the
prior `summary_arrays.json` shows exactly the two intended changes (5
`thermalFuelPenalty.dutyCycle.bySpeed[*].band` strings, 18 new
`batteryTempRanges[*].p25Peak`/`p75Peak` fields) and nothing else;
`drive_master.csv`, `summary_config.json`, `soc_patterns.json` confirmed
byte-identical to Project Knowledge (no ingestion, no config drift). Every
fixed chart re-rendered via a headless-browser build of the actual output
HTML and checked against the reported defect: History-tab labels
DOM-geometry-verified collision-free end to end; the Battery-Temperature
redesign DOM-geometry-verified for label/box overlap and correct
`medPeak`/`n` values in all three panels after in-session screenshot
tooling became unavailable partway through review.

**Open item for Andrii.** Item 1's top-bin label (`70-137`) is bound to the
fuel-accumulator subset's own observed max, not the corpus-wide 170 km/h —
confirm this is the intended semantics, or say which figure should anchor
it if not.

## M212 (2026-09-03) — De-stale the fuel-accumulator sections; "economy"→"consumption" terminology fix

**Trigger.** Andrii flagged two issues in the "SoC-Balanced Fuel Economy (August
subset)" section: (1) fuel-accumulator data now runs through September, so the
"August subset" label is stale; (2) the metric is L/100km — a *consumption*
figure (lower=better) — not *economy* in the km/L/mpg sense (higher=better),
so the "Economy" naming was imprecise. Same "August subset" staleness also
present in the sibling "Cold-Start Thermal Fuel Penalty" section (both consume
Module H's (M192) fuel-accumulator subset).

**Diagnosis.** `_hf_perdrive()`/`_of_grid()` (Modules H/M192 and O-fuel/M201)
were never date-filtered — the subset is selected purely by presence of a
valid `Використане паливо (L)` accumulator delta. `socBalancedFuel.dateSpan`
on disk was already `['2026-08-12','2026-09-02']` (79 drives, 20 days) and
`thermalFuelPenalty.dateSpan` `['20260812','20260902']` (42 drives, 18 days) —
the underlying computation was correct and current; only the hardcoded
"August"/"single month" prose (module header comments, `methodology` return
strings, and JSX Section titles/Callout/Caveat text) had gone stale, plus the
JSX used "economy" where the rest of the dashboard correctly uses
"consumption" for the analogous kWh/100km panel (line ~5106).

**Fix.**
- `compute_summary_arrays.py`: Module H and Module O-fuel header comments
  de-stringified ("August accumulator subset" → "accumulator subset");
  `_soc_balanced_fuel()` and `_thermal_fuel_penalty()` `methodology` fields
  now build their date-span/day-count/drive-count text from `min(days)`/
  `max(days)`/`len(days)` at compute time instead of a hardcoded month, so
  they self-heal as the corpus grows; "fleet economy"→"fleet fuel
  consumption" throughout.
- `xtrail_summary.jsx`: both Section titles now bind to
  `S.socBalancedFuel?.dateSpan` / `S.thermalFuelPenalty?.dateSpan` rather
  than a literal "(August subset)" string. All "economy" labels/prose in
  `SocBalancedFuel()` (KPI label, Callout, Bar label, regression-panel
  footnote, description, Caveat) renamed to "consumption". `ThermalFuelPenalty()`
  description/Caveat de-staled the same way. Two stray "August" cross-references
  in the unrelated `ThermalWarmupLag()` component (pointing at the fuel
  sections) fixed for consistency.
- No logic change: subset-selection criteria, date filters, and all numeric
  outputs are unchanged.

**Recompute.** Additive splice: `_soc_balanced_fuel()` and
`_thermal_fuel_penalty()` re-run standalone against `raw_dir=/mnt/project`
on the current 315-drive master. Both reproduce every numeric field
byte-for-byte vs the shipped `summary_arrays.json` (nDrives=79/nDays=20/
rawFleetL100=5.434/socBalancedFleetL100=5.319 and
nColdStartDrives=42/nDays=18 respectively) — isolation diff confirms exactly
one leaf field changed per key (`methodology`), nothing else.

**Validation.** `py_compile` (compute_summary_arrays.py, degradation_trends.py)
+ babel JSX parse-check + `node --check` (build_html.js, validate_jsdom.js);
clean `build_html.js` rebuild (REQUIRED_BLOCKS gate clean; pre-existing
disclosed staleness warnings for `socHysteresisV2` (259 vs 315, unrelated,
OOM-bound refit) and `energyUncertaintyMC` (+0.74% drift, unrelated, pending
next Tier-2-style regen) — both out of scope for this fix); jsdom 9/9 tabs,
52 buttons, 0 console errors; manually clicked to the "distribution" tab and
confirmed both titles render evaluated (not raw template-literal source):
"SoC-Balanced Fuel Consumption (accumulator subset, 2026-08-12–2026-09-02)"
and "Cold-Start Thermal Fuel Penalty (accumulator subset,
20260812–20260902)". `summary_arrays.json` isolation diff vs Project

## M211 (2026-09-02) — Routine ingestion: 8 new Sep 1–Sep 2 drives (307→315); two pre-existing defects found and fixed in passing

Standard incremental append per standing workflow, no methodology change.
Two-day batch: Sep 1 D3–D4 (2 legs, +18°C constant) closing out the Aug29–Sep1
window already opened at M202, and a full-day Sep 2 (6 legs, +14→+19→+16°C,
the widest single-day ambient swing of the recent batch), 30.4km total. All 8
files carry the same 78-column raw schema seen since the Aug20 oil-temperature
addition (header-verified before ingestion, not assumed). All 8 are
ens_outlier_v2-clean, sign_check ok, f_domain-clean, fully urban
(pct_highway 0.0% throughout, no 80-120km/h band time).

Sep 2 D5 (`20260902_204646.csv`, 12.2km) is the batch's dominant leg by both
distance and duration and sets the batch's thermal ceiling (33.0°C pack-mean);
it is the only leg in this 8-drive batch long enough to resolve a vreg
pack-resistance window (127.18mΩ, n=1034 samples), and its ML cluster
assignment (`mixed_like`) diverges from the rule-based `urban` drive-type
despite 0.0% highway time — noted, not investigated further. Full per-drive
detail in `sessions` / `sessionGroups` (see below).

### What changed

- **`drive_master.csv`**: 307→315 rows (182 cols unchanged). Procedure:
  archive 16 ML/domain columns → `analyze_bytes` × 8 → append+sort →
  `postprocess_master` on the full 315-row frame → restore the 16 frozen

## M210 (2026-09-02) — M119-v2 dashboard/article usability: demand-unit split, bound median-profile captions, article thermal-map composites

Three requested fixes to the M119-v2 (five-variable hazard model) presentation, all presentational/additive — no model refit, no `drive_master.csv` change, no touch to `summary_config.json` or `soc_patterns.json`.

**1. Demand median-profile chart — unit split (real bug found, not just a labelling gap).**
The single "demand" small-multiple was overlaying two curves that are NOT the
same physical quantity on one shared x-axis: START demand is battery
discharge power (kW, observed range 0–19.5), STOP demand is a
target-torque × speed **index** (observed range 0–7854 index units, NOT
convertible to kW — no calibrated gear-ratio/wheel-radius factor exists;
explicit in `m119v2_model.py`'s docstring). The shared axis compressed the
whole 0–19.5 kW START curve into roughly the first quarter-percent of the
plotted width, next to invisible. Split into two panels — `demand · start`
(kW) and `demand · stop` (idx) — each with its own correctly-scaled axis.
`PD` component gained an `only` prop (`"start" | "stop"`) to render a single
curve; unchanged for the other four predictors, whose start/stop curves
*are* the same physical unit (SoC %, km/h, °C, s) and remain correctly
overlaid. Also fixed in passing (found during this audit, same
unit-labelling gap): the `speed` panel's unit was blank (now ` km/h`) and
`tpack`'s was a bare `°` (now `°C`).

**2. Per-chart median-profile captions — bound to `S.*`, not hand-typed.**
Added a one-line, data-derived caption under each of the six median-profile
panels (SoC, speed, T pack, demand·start, demand·stop, state duration). A
first draft hand-typed the curve-shape numbers directly into caption prose
— caught before shipping as the exact "hardcoded literal" anti-pattern
M209/F-16 remediated elsewhere on this dashboard (numbers baked into text
silently go stale on the next refit). Fixed by adding
`_median_profile_caption_stats()` to `m119v2_model.py`: a pure,
refit-free function that derives `{x0,p0,xEnd,pEnd,xAtMinP,minP,xAtMaxP,maxP}`
per (start/stop × predictor) directly from the already-serialized
`partialDependence` curves. Wired into `assemble()` so it is produced
automatically on any future full M119-v2 refit. For *this* session (model
stays carried-forward at 259 drives, `recompute_m119v2=False` per standing
default — a full refit is a reproducible OOM at 307-drive corpus size),
applied via an additive splice (`splice_caption_stats.py`) that computes the
identical stats from the current `summary_arrays.json`'s already-serialized
`partialDependence` block with no model refit and no heavy deps. JSX
captions now read `V.medianProfileCaptionStats.*` via template literals;
only the surrounding words are static prose. Isolation diff of
`summary_arrays.json` vs. the prior Project Knowledge version: exactly one
added key, `socHysteresisV2.medianProfileCaptionStats` — nothing else
changed.

**3. Thermal-map composites for the article.** The interactive dashboard
exposes 27 SoC×speed hazard-probability grids per model (3 pack-temperature
× 3 recent-demand × 3 state-duration levels = 27; 54 across START+STOP) via
a one-at-a-time selector — not practical to reproduce as 54 separate static
figures in the article. Built `gen_thermal_maps.py`, producing one compact
composite PNG per model (`m119v2_thermal_maps_start.png`,
`m119v2_thermal_maps_stop.png`): a 9×3 trellis (rows = temperature×demand,
nested in blocks of 3; columns = state duration), one **shared colour
scale per model** (computed over supported cells only) so all 27 panels are
directly comparable at a glance — unlike the dashboard, which scales each
panel to its own peak for interactive legibility. Masked (unsupported,
n<20 at-risk seconds) cells rendered in a distinguishable mid-grey, same
masking source (`supportMask`) as the dashboard. Same 5-stop blue→red
palette as the dashboard's `colorFor` for visual continuity between the two.
300 dpi, source data = current `summary_arrays.json`
`socHysteresisV2.surfaces.{start,stop}` (already-serialized, no refit).

**Validation.** py_compile (`m119v2_model.py`, `compute_summary_arrays.py`,
`compute_drive_summary_v6.py`, `splice_caption_stats.py`) + `node --check`
(`build_html.js`, `validate_jsdom.js`); babel/JSX transform clean; clean
dashboard rebuild (1836KB); jsdom 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors;
acceptance T-01 (PASS, informational n-drift 289→307 noted, non-gating),
T-01b, T-02, T-03, T-04 all PASS on the unmodified `drive_master.csv`.
Baseline-vs-edited `build_html.js` warning diff: identical (no new
hardcoded-literal flags introduced by the caption fix). Isolation:
`drive_master.csv` MD5 byte-identical; `summary_config.json` and
`soc_patterns.json` byte-identical; `summary_arrays.json` +1 key only
(above); `xtrail_summary.jsx` and `m119v2_model.py` are the only files with
substantive diffs, both presentational/additive.

## M208 (2026-09-02) — Deep-audit Tier-2: resistance-model reconciliation (C-04/F-08) and energy-MC recompute (H-01/F-12)

**Trigger.** The two audit items that required an owner decision, now resolved:
choose the primary resistance estimand, and recompute the stale energy-MC block.

**C-04/F-08 — resistance-model reconciliation.** The audit flagged two
conflicting resistance trends both presented as authoritative: `powerFade`
+0.105 mΩ/mo (cadence-controlled) and `degradationTrends.resistanceVreg`
+1.2386 mΩ/mo (mixed-effects), with the latter falsely claiming (M161) to be
"one reconciled resistance estimate" matching powerFade. Empirical
determination on the current 181-drive load-excited subset showed they are the
SAME day-cluster bootstrap regression WITH and WITHOUT the M170 HV-current
logging-cadence control:
- cadence-controlled (M170): +0.105 mΩ/mo, CI [-1.876, 2.23], p(slope>0)=0.529
- cadence-uncontrolled:      +1.244 mΩ/mo, CI [-0.19, 2.797], p(slope>0)=0.953
The vreg proxy is biased upward by logging density (regression attenuation;
Barai 2018), density ~doubled mid-corpus (M126: median inter-sample interval
1.25s→0.85s), and density is confounded with calendar time (corr
months~coverage = +0.725; corr coverage~R = +0.239). So the +1.24 is an
instrumentation artifact, not pack aging. **Decision: `powerFade`
(cadence-controlled) is the single primary resistance estimand; resistanceVreg
is a labelled cadence-uncontrolled sensitivity.** The released resistance
equivalence (TOST vs the OEM 75%/14yr bound, 0.5618 mΩ/mo) is now run on the
cadence-controlled slope: equivalent=False, pTOST=0.3322 — the honest null holds
on the correct estimand; both CIs span zero, no resolved trend either way.
Implemented: `compute_summary_arrays._reconcile_resistance_models()` (new,
additive, idempotent; makes powerFade primary and re-points resistanceVreg's
released inference at the cadence-controlled slope); `degradation_trends.py`
withdraws the false M161 "reconciled" claim and labels resistanceVreg
`role=sensitivity_cadence_uncontrolled`; two JSX clauses in the
equivalence-testing paragraph rebound to the cadence-controlled slope and name
the sensitivity. New `degradationTrends.resistanceReconciliation` block records
the full decomposition.

**H-01/F-12 — energy-MC recompute.** `energyUncertaintyMC` was frozen at the
277-valid/289-drive era (nominal 1188.1206 kWh). Regenerated on the current
corpus via `energy_mc_precompute.py` (295 drives, 295 validated; independent
re-integration deviates ≤5e-5 kWh from shipped drive_master gross columns) then
`energy_uncertainty_mc.py` (20,000 draws, seed 20260822). New nominal
1250.0421 kWh (p2.5/p50/p97.5 = 1249.30 / 1253.06 / 1256.80), GTC 595.258, FCE
297.629. Offset −0.4019 A, CI [−0.451, −0.320] sourced live from
`offsetUncertainty`. The build provenance gate now reports the block CURRENT
(0.00% drift vs meta) instead of 4.95%-stale/disclosed; the corresponding
validator semantic warning clears.

**Validation.** py_compile (4 Python) + node --check (2 JS); clean rebuild;
jsdom 9/9 tabs, 52 buttons, 0 console errors; acceptance T-01–T-04 + T-01b pass.
`summary_arrays.json` isolation diff vs Project Knowledge: exactly 5 changed
keys total across M207+M208 (`eligibility`, `rawManifest`, `powerFade`,
`degradationTrends`, `energyUncertaintyMC`); none added/dropped;
`drive_master.csv` byte-identical. Remaining validator warnings: `74% highway`

**Trigger.** Independent deep project audit (E-Power_Deep_Project_Audit_2026-09-01)

`drive_master.csv` MD5 is byte-identical (no ingestion). Article items (§7,
P0-article, P2-restructure) deliberately untouched — owner-manual.

**Fixes.**
- **F-02 / C-02 (Critical) — release provenance now serialized.** `build_html.js`
  mutated `arraysObj.releaseProvenance` at build time, then injected the ORIGINAL
  `${arrays}` string, discarding the mutation; the rendered summary was blank
  ("...  drives /  km, pipeline v"). Now injects `${JSON.stringify(arraysObj)}`.

  (crossVehicle current; socHysteresisV2 259→307 stale/disclosed;
  energyUncertaintyMC 1188.12→1250 kWh stale/disclosed) are now visible in the
  shipped dashboard.

  matched manifest canonical names against raw basenames with byte equality, so an
  archive-native export ('2026-07-30 22-06-51.csv') reported all 307 canonical
  files "missing" and the non-strict fallback re-admitted the typed exclusions.
  Both sides now route through `_canonical_file_name()` before the role decision.
  Verified: archive-native names resolve AND the canonical ingest path is
  unbroken (synthetic strict-gate + regression test).
- **F-06 (High) — current-integral energy denominator.** Eligibility family gated
  on `n_I_samples > 0` (296, header/sample presence) instead of the metric it
  describes. Now gates on `gross_throughput_kwh.notna()` (295 metric-valid) and

- **F-05 / H-06 / F-18 (High/Medium) — verified 1:1 manifest.**
  `summary_arrays.rawManifest.oneToOneVerified` was null (arrays regenerated
  without a raw_dir). Ran the real bijection over the on-disk corpus (307↔307,

**Trigger.** Andrii flagged that the "Engine RPM - Speed Synchronisation"
section's Key Finding claimed 71% of engine-on time at the "generator
load-point", while the RPM Distribution section's Manufacturer Cross-Check
independently reported ~59% for what should be the same ~2000 rpm feature,
and asked whether the load-point should be defined as 2000+-25 rpm rather
than the 1800-2200 rpm band the RPM-sync module was actually using. Two
adjacent questions: (1) whether Y-axis gridlines at 1500/2000 rpm were
feasible on that section's RPM-vs-speed chart, and (2) whether the separate
"Buffer-Saturation Dissipation at Low Speed" chart's 239-drive coverage was
stale against the 307-drive corpus, and whether its "0s" bars below 77.5%
SoC ceiling contradicted the nonzero low-ceiling cases the Mountain-Road
Pattern section documents.

**Investigation.**
- **Band mismatch confirmed, not a data bug.** `_RSYNC_LP_LO,_RSYNC_LP_HI =
  1800.0, 2200.0` was set at M185 (2026-08-29), an unvalidated +-200rpm
  guess made before the peak's true shape was known. M205 (2026-09-01, same
  day) later did a 5rpm-resolution re-derivation and found the generator
  load-point is a genuinely narrow spike -- weighted center of mass
  2000.30rpm, 96%+ of the 1975-2025rpm window's mass within +-25rpm of
  2000 -- but never propagated that back into `rpmSpeedSync`. Andrii's
  proposed 2000+-25rpm (1975-2025) is the corpus-supported definition;
  1800-2200 is confirmed stale.
- **Standalone re-derivation.** `_rpm_speed_sync()` and `_low_speed_dissipation()`
  rerun standalone against all 307 raw files (independent raw_loader reading
  directly from the corpus, not the cached/summary artefacts), matching the
  additive-splice path used throughout this project.
  - With the band corrected to [1975,2025]: median per-drive load-point
    time fraction moves **71.1% -> 65.8%** (298 channel-gated drives,
    unchanged from before -- rho, slope, rpmBySpeed, monotonicIncrFrac,
    lead/lag all bit-identical, confirming the band is the only lever).
    65.8% is close to, but not identical to, Andrii's recalled ~64% and to
    the RPM Distribution section's ~59%: the residual gap is expected and
    is now stated in-dashboard (see Fix) -- this KPI is a MEDIAN of each
    drive's own load-point fraction; the RPM Distribution figure is a
    single POOLED, duration-weighted share across all engine-on hours.
    Higher-speed drives spend a smaller load-point share of their own
    time but contribute disproportionately more engine-on hours to the
    pooled total, which is why the pooled statistic reads lower than the
    per-drive median.
  - **`lowSpeedDissipation`'s 239-drive coverage is NOT stale.** Standalone
    rerun against the current 307-drive corpus reproduced exactly 239
    channel-gated drives (needs soc+rpm+load+boost, >=120 overlapping 1Hz
    samples) and a byte-identical `socThreshold` table to production --
    239 is a legitimate, already-current coverage gate, not a leftover
    from an earlier, smaller batch.
  - **"0s" bars are real medians, not zero incidence.** Below the 77.5%
    SoC-ceiling knee, most drives show 0s of motored dissipation, but a
    documented minority don't: 3/116, 4/61, 6/22 drives in the <72.5%,
    72.5-75%, 75-77.5% bins show brief motoring (up to 6s/2s/3s, totals
    8s/5s/11s) -- consistent with the Mountain-Road Pattern section's own
    incidence table, which independently shows 1/23 drives at <72.5% (1s)
    and 1/9 at 72.5-75% (2s) within its own 53-drive trip window. The
    chart's bar-top label is technically correct as a per-bin median, but
    read in isolation as "never happens below 77.5%", which is what
    prompted the cross-check against Mountain-Road Pattern in the first
    place.

**Fix.**
- `compute_summary_arrays.py`: `_RSYNC_LP_LO,_RSYNC_LP_HI` changed
  `[1800,2200] -> [1975,2025]` (2000+-25rpm), with an inline comment
  citing M205's re-derivation. `rpmSpeedSync` respliced into
  `summary_arrays.json` from the standalone rerun; isolation diff vs
  pristine: **CHANGED `rpmSpeedSync` only** (`loadPointBand`,
  `loadPointFracMedIqr.{median,p25,p75}`, and the `methodology` string's
  echoed band numerals) -- all 126 top-level keys otherwise byte-identical,
  `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged (`6300e8676819449cafcf1087ce2423a0`,
  307 drives), `summary_config.json` byte-identical.
- `xtrail_summary.jsx` (`RpmSpeedSync()`): added two fixed reference
  gridlines at 1500rpm (amber dashed, the M205-identified secondary
  governed setpoint) and ~2000rpm (reusing the existing teal load-point
  line, which now sits exactly on it post-fix) on the RPM-vs-speed SVG,
  replacing reliance on the arbitrary fractional-of-yMax grid alone for
  these two values; chart caption updated to name both lines. Added a
  live-computed (`S.rpmDistribution`-bound, no hardcoded numbers) dashed-box
  reconciliation note directly under the Key Finding, mirroring the M174
  Mountain-Road-Pattern-vs-corpus-wide pattern, explaining why this
  section's per-drive-median % and the RPM Distribution section's
  pooled-duration-weighted % for the same band legitimately differ.
- `xtrail_summary.jsx` (`LowSpeedDissipation()`): zero-median bins that
  still hold a nonzero minority of motoring drives are now flagged with an
  asterisk on the bar label, plus a live-computed (bound to
  `S.lowSpeedDissipation`) caption naming the affected bins, their n/of-n
  counts and total seconds, and cross-referencing the Mountain-Road Pattern
  section's own low-ceiling cases -- so the "0s" reading can no longer be
  mistaken for "never happens" in isolation from that section.
- No changes to `_low_speed_dissipation()`, `lowSpeedDissipation`'s stored
  array, or any other summary_arrays.json key -- confirmed via standalone
  rerun to already be correct and current; only its dashboard presentation
  changed.

**Scope discipline.** Raw re-derivation used a direct-file `raw_loader`
against the 307 raw CSVs on disk (frame_loader/slim-cache not required for
either of these two Category-B passes), avoiding the OOM-risking full
`build_summary_arrays()`. Both standalone reruns first reproduced the
CURRENT production values exactly (`rpmSpeedSync` pre-fix: 298 drives,
[1800,2200], median 0.711 -- matches; `lowSpeedDissipation`: 239 drives,
identical `socThreshold` table -- matches) before the band constant was
changed, confirming the `raw_loader` replicates the production pipeline
faithfully and isolating the band as the only real change.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean.
- Acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS** (`peakChargeA`
  unchanged at 213.0 A; T-01's golden snapshot still pinned at n=289 vs the
  live n=307 corpus -- pre-existing, non-gating, unrelated to this fix).
- Dashboard rebuild: `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` gate passes; jsdom **9 tabs / 52
  buttons / 0 console errors**. Pre-existing disclosed-staleness warnings
  (`socHysteresisV2` basis lag, `energyUncertaintyMC` carry-forward) fire
  as expected and are unrelated to this change.
- Isolation diff: `summary_arrays.json` changed **`rpmSpeedSync` only**
  (126/126 top-level keys otherwise identical); `drive_master.csv` and
  `summary_config.json` byte-identical to pristine; `compute_summary_arrays.py`
  changed only the `_RSYNC_LP_LO`/`_RSYNC_LP_HI` constants + comment.

## M205 (2026-09-01) — Bin-edge refinement: RPM Distribution peak isolated from a boundary sitting on top of it

**Trigger.** Andrii asked whether the "Engine RPM Distribution" chart's bin
edges near 1500 and 2000 rpm were representing the true shape correctly, or
whether real-world oscillation (readings like 1499/1501) risked splitting a
genuine spike across a bin boundary.

**Investigation.** Standalone re-derivation, independent of
`summary_arrays.json`: same `_RawAccum` 1 Hz-grid duration-weighted
convention as M82/M83, replayed at 5 rpm resolution against all 307 raw
files in `drive_master.csv` (not the cached/summary artefacts).

- **2000 rpm — confirmed split by a bin edge.** The mode is a genuinely
  narrow spike, not a broad shoulder: weighted center of mass over
  1975-2025 rpm is **2000.30 rpm**, and 96%+ of that window's mass sits
  within ±25 rpm of 2000. The OLD `RPM_HIST_EDGES` placed an edge **exactly
  at 2000**, splitting this single physical mode 45.3%/54.7% across the
  1900-2000 / 2000-2100 bins. Not a data-loss bug (only ~7.2% of the
  combined old bin pair was true valley/decay-tail dilution) but a
  presentational one: two ~200rpm-wide bins straddling 2000 read as a broad
  shoulder when the mode is actually <50 rpm wide. True valley density
  (flat, ~25-30 s/rpm) extends to ~1975, not 1900; the spike decays back to
  background density (~50-60 s/rpm) by ~2025-2050, not 2100.
- **1500 rpm — confirmed NOT split.** Weighted center of mass over
  1485-1515 rpm is **1500.08 rpm**. 1500 was never a bin edge — it sits
  mid-bin inside `1400-1600`, so 1499/1501-type oscillation was already
  fully contained. No edge change made on this side.
- **Ancillary finding, not acted on this milestone** (flagged for a future
  decision): `1400-1600` is actually bimodal, not one smeared ~1500 region
  — a second, distinct governed setpoint at weighted center **1588.62
  rpm** (7,569 s) sits alongside the 1500.08 rpm spike (11,045 s) under one
  label. Left as-is pending Andrii's direction on whether it's worth
  resolving into its own bin.

**Fix.** `RPM_HIST_EDGES` changed `[…, 1900, 2000, 2100, …]` →
`[…, 1975, 2025, 2100, …]` (2 of 11 edges moved; bin count unchanged at
10; labels' bare-numeric convention preserved rather than annotating the
peak bin, to avoid overflowing the chart's fixed-width per-bin x-axis
column and colliding with the `{bins[peakIdx]} rpm` prose template).
Corpus-wide corrected occupancy: peak bin **1975-2025 = 43.219 h = 27.3%**
of all gridded time (58.8% of engine-on time); valley **1600-1975 =
3.125 h**; decay tail **2025-2100 = 1.587 h** (down from the old
2000-2100 bin's 23.014 h, since that bin no longer straddles the spike).
Old vs new bin-pair total mass conserved (1600-2100 span: 47.932 h old vs
47.931 h new, rounding only) — edges only redistribute, nothing lost.

`xtrail_summary.jsx`'s `RpmDistributionChart()`: color ramp updated (bin 5,
2025-2100, recolored from red to orange — it's decay tail post-M205, no
longer peak-magnitude); pooled-view caption's "1600-1900" → "1600-1975"
plus a new sentence distinguishing the true spike from the old
edge-straddling appearance; intro paragraph notes the M205 refinement. The
Manufacturer Cross-Check (M105) paragraph's previously-hardcoded "1900-2100
rpm... ~62%" literal replaced with a live computation
(`peakBinIdx`/`peakPctOfEngineOn`, derived from `S.rpmDistribution` the
same way `RpmDistributionChart` already derives its own peak) so the claim
can't go stale if the bin scheme is revisited again.

**Scope discipline.** Raw B-pass (`category_B()`) rerun standalone against
all 307 files — the correct additive-splice path, avoiding the OOM-risking
full `build_summary_arrays()`. Isolation diff vs M204 state: **CHANGED**
only `rpmDistribution` and `crossVehicle` (the latter because
`crosscheck_events.inject()` was rerun to refresh
`crossVehicle.turboPattern`'s embedded rpmDistribution comparison against
the e-4ORCE aux corpus — `eventDetectors`/`pureElectric` reconfirmed
byte-identical except `_meta.generated` timestamp). `eolBaselines`
initially appeared to differ in the standalone `category_B()` output; root
cause was a schema-superset gap (3 sub-keys — `socBandMedianPp`,
`socWindow`, `vreg` — added by a separate downstream pass not invoked by
this standalone call), not a real change — discarded, production
`eolBaselines` kept byte-identical. `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged
(`6300e8676819449cafcf1087ce2423a0`, 307 drives); `summary_config.json`
byte-identical. No raw ingestion, no corpus change — methodology-only
session.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean.
- Acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**. (T-01's golden
  snapshot still pinned at n=289 vs the live n=307 corpus — pre-existing,
  unrelated to this fix, peakChargeA unchanged at 213.0 A so no actual
  drift.)
- Dashboard rebuild: `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` gate passes; jsdom **9 tabs / 52
  buttons / 0 console errors**. Pre-existing disclosed-staleness warnings
  (`socHysteresisV2` basis lag, `energyUncertaintyMC` carry-forward) fire
  as expected and are unrelated to this change.

## M204 (2026-09-01) — Interpretive fix: crawl/stop-go engine-start rate denominator visibility (Module D)

**Trigger.** Andrii flagged the "BY DRIVE TYPE" tile in Crawl & Stop-Go —
highway showing a *higher* `startsPer10minStopGo` (3.85) than urban (2.27)
looked backwards, and asked whether the breakdown was silently restricted to
drives where a stop-go cycle was actually detected.

**Investigation.** Confirmed via code inspection and an independent
standalone replication against the raw CSVs (not just re-reading the JSON)
that both numbers are correctly computed — this is not a bug and not a
filtering artefact:

- `byDriveType` is **not** filtered to drives with detected stop-go activity.
  `_csg_events()` only gates on ≥120 valid 1 Hz speed samples; every drive of
  a given type that clears that bar is included, including drives with zero
  stop-go activity. Proof: `byDriveType` n's sum exactly to `nDrivesCovered`
  (20 + 22 + 30 + 1 + 230 = 303).
- `startsPer10minStopGo` is `startsLowSpeed / (lowSpeedTimeS/600)` — a ratio
  whose **denominator is not fixed**, it's whatever low-speed (≤30 km/h) time
  that one drive happens to contain. Re-derived per-drive from the raw
  corpus: highway drives spend a median of only **8%** of drive duration
  below the ceiling (mixed_highway 15%), touching it only in brief episodes
  — ramps, toll gates, a congestion pinch-point — not a sustained stop-go
  duty cycle. Urban drives spend a median of **62%** of drive duration there
  — a large, stable denominator. A handful of discrete engine starts landing
  inside a short highway low-speed window inflates the ratio (worst case:
  9 starts in a 415 s window → 13.0/10min); the same-size window with zero
  starts reads 0 (3 of the 20 highway drives do). Hence highway's wide IQR
  (p25 1.71 / p75 4.95 / p95 10.34) vs urban's tighter one (p25 1.28 / p75
  3.31). Same structural pattern as the corpus's already-documented
  short-trip throughput denominator effect (M35), here affecting a rate
  instead of an intensity figure.
- `cyclesPerDrive` (the "2.5" Andrii separately queried) was never a rate —
  it's stop-go cycles **per whole drive** (dashboard label already reads
  "cyc/drive"). 2.5 cycles across an entire highway drive is unremarkable.

**Fix.** `_crawl_stop_go()` now reports the denominator alongside the rate
instead of leaving it implicit. Added to each `byDriveType` entry:
`lowSpeedTimeS` (median/IQR window size, seconds), `lowSpeedFracOfDrive`
(median/IQR window as % of drive duration), `startsLowSpeedAbs` (median/IQR
raw start count — the numerator). Added corpus-derived
`out['smallDenominatorDriveTypes']` (types with median window <20% of drive
duration; currently `['highway', 'mixed_highway']`) and `out['rateCaveat']`
(full interpretive text). `methodology` updated to state explicitly that
`byDriveType` is not detection-filtered.

`xtrail_summary.jsx`'s `CrawlStopGo()` BY DRIVE TYPE tiles now show the
window size and raw start count under the rate, with a ⚠ marker on flagged
types, and a `Caveat` block (driven by `smallDenominatorDriveTypes`, not
hardcoded) spelling out the mechanism and the corrective reading: the
numbers are real, but the rate is high-variance by construction for
episodic-low-speed drive types and should be read together with the window
size and raw count, not in isolation. No claim that highway driving produces
more frequent stop-go engine cycling in absolute terms — the opposite holds;
urban carries far more absolute low-speed/engine-start volume.

**Verification.** Additive-splice regeneration of `crawlStopGo` only
(raw-CSV re-derivation, ~13.6 min); isolation diff confirms every existing
field byte-identical (`whCycleNet`, `startsPer10minStopGo`, `cyclesPerDrive`,
etc. all unchanged — 3.85/2.27/2.5 reproduce exactly) with only the four new
fields plus updated `methodology` text added. `drive_master.csv` MD5
unchanged (data-only splice, no raw pipeline re-run). `energyUncertaintyMC`
and `socHysteresisV2` carried forward untouched. T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04
all PASS. `build_html.js` clean build (pre-existing disclosed staleness
warnings only, unrelated to this change). `validate_jsdom.js`: 9/9 tabs, 52
buttons, 0 console errors — matches the post-M197 baseline.

## M203 (2026-09-01) — Bug fix: engine operating-point state machine occupancy statistic (M190/K correction)

**Trigger.** Andrii flagged two apparent problems in the "Engine Operating-Point
State Machine" dashboard section: Mid and High RPM bands showing 0% occupancy
("definitely not true"), and the section's 67% engine-off figure disagreeing
with the ~50% reported elsewhere on the dashboard.

**Root cause — one bug, two symptoms.** `_engine_state_machine()` (M190)
computed `occupancy.<state>` exclusively as the **per-drive median** of each
drive's own state-time-fraction. That statistic is a poor fit for this data:

- **mid/high read 0%** because those RPM bands are zero-inflated across
  drives — most individual drives never reach ≥2300 rpm at all, so the
  median-across-drives collapses to 0.0 even though the module's own pooled
  dwell/entry counts (mid: 5,835 dwell events, 81.4 entries/eng-hr; high:
  1,171 events, 16.3 entries/eng-hr) prove the excursions are real and
  routine.
- **off reads 67.4%** because a median-of-ratios is skewed upward by
  short/idle-heavy drives, and this diverges from the corpus-pooled,
  duration-weighted off-fraction reported elsewhere
  (`rpmDistribution.pooledPct[0]` = 53.6%, `evTraction.evPctTime` = 53.0%) —
  both computed independently over the same underlying per-second
  classification. The module's own stated design ("...across ALL engine
  time") calls for the pooled statistic; the per-drive median was simply the
  wrong number to headline.

**Fix.** `_engine_state_machine()` now also emits `occupancy.<state>.pooled`
— the corpus-pooled, duration-weighted share of all classified engine
time — computed for free from the transition-matrix row sums already
accumulated inside the function (`rows = T.sum(1, keepdims=True)`, already
present). No raw-corpus re-read required. Row *i* excludes only the single
last classified sample of each drive (no outgoing t→t+1 transition to
count) — a disclosed ~0.05% relative undercount at this corpus size
(306 drives / 567,025 pooled seconds), not corrected with a second raw
pass. `pooledTotalSeconds` added alongside for transparency.

Corrected values (289→306 covered drives, same as M190's basis):

| state | per-drive median (unchanged) | pooled (new, M203) |
|---|---|---|
| off | 67.4% | **54.5%** |
| low | 0.8% | 1.3% |
| loadPoint | 29.6% | **36.5%** |
| mid | **0.0%** | **6.7%** |
| high | **0.0%** | **1.1%** |

`xtrail_summary.jsx`'s `EngineStateMachine()` component: the three KPI
cards, the key-finding `Callout`, and the per-state table now bind to
`occupancy.<state>.pooled` as the headline figure (Off 54%, Load-point 37%,
Mid 7%, High 1%). The per-drive median is retained and labeled explicitly
("per-drive median 67%") rather than dropped — it answers a legitimately
different question ("what does a typical single drive look like") and
remains available for anyone who wants it. The `Caveat` block spells out
why the two numbers diverge and by how much, so the discrepancy is
documented rather than silently resolved.

**Scope discipline.** Isolation diff vs M202 state: **CHANGED** only
`engineStateMachine.methodology`; **ADDED** only
`engineStateMachine.pooledTotalSeconds` and the five
`engineStateMachine.occupancy.<state>.pooled` leaves. No other key in
`summary_arrays.json` touched. `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged
(`6300e8676819449cafcf1087ce2423a0`, 307 drives); `summary_config.json`,
`soc_patterns.json`, `build_html.js`, `validate_jsdom.js` byte-identical to
M202 state. No raw ingestion, no corpus change — methodology-only session.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean.
- Acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**. (T-01's golden
  snapshot is still pinned at n=289 vs the live n=307 corpus — peakChargeA
  unchanged at 213.0 A so no actual drift, flagged as a pre-existing
  snapshot-refresh item, unrelated to this fix.)
- Dashboard rebuild: gates pass; jsdom **9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console
  errors**.
- Rendered output spot-checked via headless DOM extraction: KPI cards,
  finding callout, per-state table (Mid 7%, High 1%) and caveat all read
  correctly and consistently post-fix.

## M202 (2026-09-01) — Routine ingestion: 17 new Aug 29 – Sep 1 drives (290→307)

Standard incremental append per standing workflow, no methodology change.
Four-day batch spanning Aug 29 (4 drives), Aug 30 (8 drives, the largest
single day of the batch), Aug 31 (3 drives) and Sep 1 (2 drives), 417.8km
total. All 17 files carry the same 79-column raw schema seen since Aug 20
(seven files drop only the unconsumed `Середня витрата
палива (л/100 км) 10 sec (L/100km)` fuel-economy display column, the
familiar logging-app toggle, not a PID-configuration change; header-verified
before ingestion, not assumed). All 17 are ens_outlier_v2-clean, sign_check
ok, f_domain-clean.

Aug 29 D1 (`20260829_100447.csv`) sets a **new corpus-maximum 80–120km/h
deficit of 77.5%** (band_80_120_s=173.4s, M14-valid), surpassing the prior
71.2% record (Jul13 D4). Three long Aug 30 legs (D3 118.0km, D4 82.6km, D5 101.0km =
88.1% of that day's distance) are each individually close to net-neutral
(net corr2p +0.11 / −0.20 / +0.13 per 100km) — three consecutive clean
buffer-closure illustrations on the batch's longest drives, all three
clearing the M14 deficit-validity gate. D4 sets the batch's speed ceiling
at 166.0km/h and its thermal/motor maxima (98°C motor, 103°C oil). The
three closing Aug 30 evening urban legs hold pack-mean at 43–45°C through
a cooling 22→21°C evening — the same cumulative-heating / thermal-lag
pattern documented in the Aug 2–Aug 4 sessions, reproduced here within a
single highway-heavy day. Sep 1's two legs are the coolest and
lowest-volume of the batch (+17°C constant, 2.5km combined), both
net-charging cold-start hops. Full per-drive detail in `sessions` /
`sessionGroups` (see below).

## M201 (2026-08-31) — New analysis: cold-start thermal fuel penalty (August subset), closing Module O's deferred fuel-cost question

**Scope.** Builds the fuel-consumption sub-analysis that Module O
(`_thermal_warmup_lag`, M191) deliberately deferred: "The fuel-consumption
penalty is a separate August-subset analysis and is not computed here."
Uses Module H's (M192) August fuel-accumulator channel on cold-start drives
(coolant start <60 °C, warms past 70 °C) and DECOMPOSES the naive trip-level
penalty into a duty-cycle component (how much the ICE runs) and a combustion
component (how thirsty it is once running), each controlled for the confound
the other view ignores.

**Two reusable bugs found & fixed while prototyping.** (1) Index-alignment
trap: constructing the 1 Hz frame with `index=t` while component Series still
carried an integer RangeIndex silently reindexed everything to NaN — fixed by
using `.values` on every column (as Module H already does). (2)
`ffill(limit=5)` starved the coolant channel, which polls in a slower ~0.25 Hz
multiplex group (~4 s interval) distinct from the ~1.23 Hz core group
(accumulator/engine-rpm/load/SoC/speed) — fixed with `ffill(limit=15)`. A
third suspect (list- vs callable-form `usecols`) turned out to be the actual
root cause of one intermediate all-NaN result: the list form mis-parsed the
unicode `℃` coolant column name; the callable form (`lambda c: c in want`,
already Module H's convention) parses it correctly.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_thermal_fuel_penalty(dm,
  raw_loader, raw_dir)` + `_of_grid` helper + `_OF_*` constants, inserted
  before `_day_label_by_file` (immediately after the `_full_cell_case_study`
  block), wired `arrays['thermalFuelPenalty']` right after `fullCellCaseStudy`
  in the raw-module pass.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `ThermalFuelPenalty()` component
  (Distribution tab, registered as a `Section` right after "Full-Cell Array
  Worked Examples", accent `#dc2626`): three headline KPIs (naive / duty-cycle
  / combustion ratios), a reconciliation callout, paired on-fraction bars by
  speed band (cold vs warm), a top-matched-cells table, and idle/trip-level
  detail. All figures bind to `S.thermalFuelPenalty.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `thermalFuelPenalty` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**:
  `125 → 126` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; all other core files byte-identical.

### Method
August accumulator subset, **35 cold-start drives, 14 days** (Aug 12 – Aug 28,
2026). Four views:
1. **tripLevel (naive)** — within-drive warm-up-window vs warm-window
   L/100km, per-drive ratio. Confounded by driving regime (warm-up is
   early/low-speed/urban) and slightly by SoC banking (disclosed).
2. **combustionPenalty** — fuel per engine-ON second at a matched RPM×load
   operating point, cold vs warm; exposure-weighted by warm-state cell
   counts; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws).
3. **dutyCycle** — engine-ON fraction at matched road speed, cold vs warm;
   day-clustered bootstrap on the matched 20–40 km/h band.
4. **idle** — fuel L/h at standstill (<3 km/h), cold vs warm.

### Findings
- **tripLevel**: warm-up window 9.09 L/100km (IQR 7.64–14.27) vs warm window
  4.91 L/100km (IQR 4.13–5.51); per-drive ratio **median 2.14×** (IQR
  1.44–2.94). SoC drift during warm-up +1.2 pp (minor banking confound,
  disclosed).
- **combustionPenalty**: exposure-weighted ratio **1.073×**, 95% CI
  **[1.069, 1.10]**, resolved above unity, 8 matched RPM×load cells (rests
  largely on the best-populated cell, [1700,2200)×[25,50)). A modest
  cold-friction/enrichment effect.
- **dutyCycle**: ratio ranges 2.6× (idle-speed band) down to ~1.4× (highway);
  matched **20–40 km/h band ratio 1.91×**, 95% CI **[1.56, 2.47]** — the
  **dominant** mechanism: the series-hybrid runs the ICE nearly twice as much
  when cold.
- **idle**: 0.329 vs 0.106 L/h, ratio **3.11×**.
- **Reconciliation**: duty (1.91) × combustion (1.073) ≈ **2.05×**, close to
  the naive 2.14× trip-level ratio — the small remainder is driving-regime.
  Physically sensible, honest-null discipline maintained throughout (no
  effect inflated beyond what the matched comparison supports).

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**
  (`drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged throughout).
- Production `_thermal_fuel_penalty` reproduced the standalone prototype
  exactly: n=35 drives / 14 days, trip ratio median 2.138, combustion 1.073
  (CI [1.069, 1.10]), duty 1.907 (CI [1.558, 2.467]), idle ratio 3.106.
- Isolation diff vs the pristine M200 baseline: **ADDED** `thermalFuelPenalty`
  key only (125→126 keys); **REMOVED** none; **CHANGED** none.
  `compute_summary_arrays.py` +292 lines / 0 deletions (module + one 8-line
  wiring block); `build_html.js` +1 line; `xtrail_summary.jsx` +108 lines / 0
  deletions across exactly 2 hunks (component definition + `Section`
  registration). All other core pipeline/JSX files byte-identical to
  pristine.
- Dashboard: build gates pass (M94 `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` incl.
  `thermalFuelPenalty`); jsdom **9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors**.

### Method (see the block comment above `_FCS_FILES`)
Each cell updates only a handful of times across an entire drive (slow round-robin
poll), so no single row has a full snapshot. Per file: resample to 1 s, forward-fill
(limit 90 s), take the timestamp with the highest cell completeness as the
RECONSTRUCTED snapshot (disclosed, not simultaneous). Report mean/min/max/spread/
std across the reconstructed cells and the 3 lowest/3 highest cells by number.

### Findings (3 worked examples)
- **`20260513_182950.csv`**: 80/80 cells reconstructed, SoC 62.5%. Mean 3.7385 V,
  spread **8.0 mV**, std 1.62 mV. Lowest: #32, #04, #18; highest: #07, #35, #37.
- **`20260515_075207.csv`**: 60/80 cells, SoC 73.5%. Mean 3.8675 V, spread
  **21.0 mV** (the widest of the three), std 4.87 mV.
- **`20260511_185709.csv`**: 25/80 cells. Mean 3.7098 V, spread **7.0 mV**, std
  1.49 mV.

**Reading (case study, not a corpus claim).** All three examples show tight
balance (spread ≤21 mV) across the observed SoC range, consistent with a
well-balanced pack. Illustrative only — three snapshots, not a statistical sample.

### Method (see the block comment above `_aux_load_ambient`)
Per-drive standstill draw (key-on, stationary median, `standstill_draw_kw`) paired
with drive-start ambient temperature. Spearman rank correlation (day-clustered
bootstrap, seed 42, 4000 draws); an OLS slope (kW/°C) reported as a descriptive
summary, not causal. Binned median/IQR by ambient band (10–15/15–20/20–25/25–30/
30–40 °C).

### Findings (215 drives, 50 days, ambient 11–38°C)
- **Spearman ρ = 0.64** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [0.54, 0.72]) between ambient
  and standstill draw.
- **Monotonic rise above ~15°C**: 0.99 kW (15–20°C) → 1.22 (20–25) → 1.46 (25–30)
  → 1.91 kW (30–40°C). Slope 0.053 kW/°C (descriptive).
- The 10–15°C bin (n=8) is sparse and slightly elevated — consistent with cold-
  weather heating load, but too thin to characterise.

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver, NO causality claim).**
Consistent with an AC-compressor climate-load proxy at the warm end, but there is
no HVAC state channel (compressor on/off, fan speed, setpoint), so the mechanism
cannot be confirmed — reported as correlation only. No sub-15°C data exists
(warm-season corpus); this characterises the warm end of the range.

## M198 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: barometric/air-density compensation, circularity-disclosed (feasibility-review candidate P, §2 exploratory)

**Scope.** Seventh §2 module (after H, B, N, S, R, F): candidate **P**, barometric/
air-density compensation — exploratory, circularity-disclosed. Corpus- and
methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…`
unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_baro_compensation(dm, raw_loader,
  raw_dir)` + `_bc_aligned` helper + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['baroCompensation']` after `energyShifting`.
  Reads sparse baro/MAP/MAF/RPM channels from raw, time-aligned. (A stale partial
  P block from an earlier interrupted attempt was found duplicated in the file and
  removed; the shipped source now has exactly one clean definition, verified against
  the regenerated arrays.)
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `BaroCompensation()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `EnergyShifting`, `Section` accent `#2563eb`, EXPLORATORY tag): three
  KPI cards, a method `Callout` leading with the circularity disclosure, the
  load-point MAF-by-baro IQR chart, and the caveat block. All figures bind to
  `S.baroCompensation.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `baroCompensation` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `122 → 123` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_BC_BARO`)
Sparse channels (baro/MAP/MAF/RPM) time-aligned by 1 s ffill (limit 30 s).
Circularity: residual boost−(MAP−baro)/100 (median/std, frac |resid|<0.05 bar).
Baro range overall and at the load-point (rpm 1800–2200). Air-density compensation
test: MAF (air mass) at the load-point by baro bin + rank correlation — baro-
invariant MAF ⇒ compensated. Boost is NOT used as an outcome (circular).

### Findings (218 files, 55 days)
- **Circularity confirmed**: calc-boost = (MAP−baro)/100 to within sensor noise
  (residual median 0.0 bar, std 0.0023, |resid|<0.05 for 100% of samples) — boost
  is gauge pressure and cannot test baro compensation.
- **Baro range**: 92–101 kPa overall (9 kPa, ~756 m altitude-equivalent), but only
  98–101 kPa (3 kPa, ~252 m) at the load-point.
- **Load-point air mass is near-constant across baro**: MAF 18.84 g/s (98–100 kPa)
  vs 18.66 g/s (100–103 kPa), span 0.18 g/s, rank corr −0.30 — consistent with the
  engine holding a fixed air-mass operating point (density-compensated).

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The firm result is the
circularity disclosure. The compensation signal — near-invariant load-point air mass
— is suggestive but under-powered: the barometric range at the load-point is narrow,
so this is exploratory, not conclusive. Flat terrain; baro is weather-driven.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_baro_compensation` reproduced the standalone prototype (circularity
  residual 0.0/0.0023; baro 9 kPa overall / 3 kPa load-point; MAF span 0.18 g/s;
  corr −0.30). Additive module; FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED the
  fifteen prior new keys plus `baroCompensation`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.**
  `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

candidates.

## M197 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: energy-shifting behaviour (feasibility-review candidate F, §2 exploratory; no acoustic claim)

**Scope.** Sixth §2 module (after H, B, N, S, R): candidate **F**, energy-shifting
behaviour — exploratory, no acoustic claim. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged
session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_energy_shifting(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` + `_esh_grid` helper + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['energyShifting']` after `highSocRegen`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `EnergyShifting()` component (Distribution tab,
  after `HighSocRegen`, `Section` accent `#7c3aed`, EXPLORATORY tag): three KPI
  cards, a key-finding `Callout`, a dual chart (engine-on bars + net battery kW
  line vs speed), and the caveat block. All figures bind to `S.energyShifting.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `energyShifting` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `121 → 122` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_ESH_COLS`)
Per-drive 1 Hz grid (speed via M167 priority). Per speed bin: engine-on fraction
(rpm>400), per-drive median/IQR with a day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws)
at low speed; and pooled median NET battery power p=(-I)·V (M11, discharge-positive).

### Findings (288 drives, 70 days)
- **Engine-on fraction rises monotonically** with speed: ~1% (0–5 km/h) → 8%
  (5–15) → 37% (30–50) → 61% (50–70) → 93% (90–110) → 98% (110+). At 5–15 km/h the
  engine is off ~92% of the time (day-cluster bootstrap CI [0.061, 0.104] engine-on).
- **Net battery flow flips sign**: net discharge below 50 km/h (+1.7 kW at 5–15,
  buffer supplying electric driving), net **charge at 50–70 km/h** (−0.76 kW,
  engine banking energy at its load-point), then discharge again at the highest
  speeds (+0.82 kW, demand exceeding generator output).

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** Energy is shifted:
banked into the buffer where the engine runs with headroom (mid-speed) and spent to
run electric at low speed. This is the power-buffer used as a time-shifter of
generator energy across the speed range. NO acoustic claim is made — there is no
microphone, and whether the shifting is efficiency-, demand- or noise-motivated is
not identifiable.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_energy_shifting` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (engine-on 1%→98%; net kW +1.7 low / −0.76 charge band). Additive module; FINAL
  isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED the fourteen prior new keys plus
  `energyShifting`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/
  `crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

## M196 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: high-SoC regen reduction (feasibility-review candidate R, §2 thin)

**Scope.** Fifth §2 module (after H, B, N, S): candidate **R**, high-SoC regen
reduction — flagged thin by the review. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session
(290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_high_soc_regen(dm, frame_loader)` +
  `_hr_grid` helper + constants, inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['highSocRegen']` after `vgtAirPath`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `HighSocRegen()` component (Distribution tab,
  after `VgtAirPath`, `Section` accent `#16a34a`, THIN tag): three KPI cards, a
  method `Callout`, the p95/median regen-envelope-vs-SoC curve, and the caveat
  block. All figures bind to `S.highSocRegen.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `highSocRegen` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `120 → 121` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_HR_I`)
Regen samples = charge power I·V/1000 kW in (1, 120) kW (cap drops sensor glitches,
e.g. a 374 kW spike). Envelope = median/p95/p99 charge kW per SoC bin (≥50 samples).
The p95/p99 envelope (not the mean) is used because regen magnitude is set by decel
intensity, not SoC — the envelope is the allowed ceiling. High-SoC reduction = drop
in p95 from the peak bin to the mean of bins at SoC≥69%. Day-clustered bootstrap
(seed 42, 4000 draws) on the peak-bin and top-bin p95.

### Findings (193,689 regen samples; 72k above SoC 66%, 34k above 69%, max 88%)
- The regen p95 envelope is **dome-shaped**: rises from ~20 kW at 40–50% SoC to a
  **peak of 36.1 kW at 60–63%** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [34.9, 36.9]), then
  declines to **~30.9 kW above 69%** (top-bin CI [29.8, 31.9]).
- **High-SoC reduction 14.3%** from the peak; the peak-bin and top-bin CIs do not
  overlap, so the taper is statistically distinguishable — but modest.

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** A real but thin high-SoC
charge-acceptance taper (~14%), not a hard cutoff. Consistent with mild BMS charge
limiting near the top of the operating band; confounded by how driving is
distributed across SoC, so reported descriptively, not as a BMS-strategy claim.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_high_soc_regen` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly (peak
  36.06 kW @ 60–63%; high-SoC 30.89 kW; 14.3% reduction; CIs [34.9,36.9] vs
  [29.8,31.9]). Additive module; FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED the
  thirteen prior new keys plus `highSocRegen`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.**
  `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
