## M195 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: VGT-A command tracking + air-path map (feasibility-review candidate S, §2 subset; absorbs S6)

**Scope.** Fourth §2 module (after H, B, N): candidate **S**, VGT-A command tracking
+ air-path operating map — subset; absorbs S6 (generator air-path MAF/AFR/throttle).
Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5
`396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_vgt_airpath(dm, raw_loader, raw_dir)` +
  `_vgt_drive` helper + constants, inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['vgtAirPath']` after `cellSpreadRelaxation`. Reads the sparse VGT/MAF/AFR
  channels directly from raw (not in the slim cache).
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `VgtAirPath()` component (Distribution tab,
  after `CellSpreadRelaxation`, `Section` accent `#0891b2`, SUBSET tag): three KPI
  cards, a key-finding `Callout`, the air-path operating-map table (boost/RPM/MAF/
  AFR by VGT position), and the caveat block. All figures bind to `S.vgtAirPath.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `vgtAirPath` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `119 → 120` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_VGT_CMD`)
Subset: files with real VGT-A actual variation (std>0.5). Commanded & actual VGT-A
are co-sampled → static tracking error = actual−command. All channels resampled to
1 s and ffilled (limit 60 s) to align the sparse multiplex groups, then restricted
to engine-on (rpm>400) — VGT is only actively controlled when running (at rest
cmd==act==parked would inflate tracking). Tracking error median/IQR overall and by
commanded-position bin; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on |error|.
Air-path operating map: median boost/RPM/MAF/AFR by actual-position bin. Hysteresis
(error by command direction) is EXPLORATORY. A-only: VGT-B actual absent.

### Findings (54 files, 14 days, 25,794 engine-on paired samples)
- **VGT-A tracks command to the sensor resolution**: median error 0.0%, |error|
  0.39% (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [0.2, 0.39]) — one 0.39% quantization step,
  i.e. near-perfect closed-loop tracking.
- **Consistent ~0.4% directional hysteresis** (one step): rising command → actual
  −0.39%, falling → +0.39% — the actual trails the command direction (exploratory).
- **Air-path operating map**: engine runs at the ~2000-rpm load-point (MAF ~18–19
  g/s) with higher-airflow excursions (MAF ~28 g/s at the 40–60% VGT / 2591-rpm
  band); **AFR stays stoichiometric (~14.7) across the entire envelope** — the
  generator runs closed-loop, air flow scaling with demand.

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The turbo air path is a
tightly-controlled, stoichiometric closed loop around the generator load-point:
faithful actuator tracking, minimal hysteresis, constant AFR. Nothing about the
air path departs from a well-behaved generator operating at its efficient point.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_vgt_airpath` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly (54 files;
  |error| 0.39%, boot CI [0.2,0.39]; AFR ~14.7 across the map). Additive module;
  FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED the twelve prior new keys plus
  `vgtAirPath`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle`
  preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

### Subset caveats (displayed)
54 files with real VGT-A variation, 14 days; sparse-poll secondary channels aligned
by 1 s ffill; the ±0.39% error/hysteresis is one actuator sensor step (tracking at
the resolution limit, hysteresis exploratory); A-side only. Do not generalise timing.

## M194 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: cell-spread transient/relaxation (feasibility-review candidate N, §2 exploratory)

**Scope.** Third §2 module (after H, B): candidate **N**, cell-spread transient/
relaxation on the max/min channel — exploratory. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged
session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried.

**Why new, ≠ cellHealthTrend.** `cellHealthTrend` is a long-term unloaded LEVEL/
trend (degradation). N is the within-event transient/relaxation: how the max−min
spread widens under load and relaxes at rest. Uses the max/min cell-voltage channel
(97.6% coverage, already in the slim cache — no schema bump). No cell diagnosis.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_cell_spread_relaxation(dm, frame_loader)`
  + `_csr_grid` helper + constants, inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['cellSpreadRelaxation']` after `handoffSequence`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `CellSpreadRelaxation()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `HandoffSequence`, `Section` accent `#2563eb`, EXPLORATORY tag): three
  KPI cards, a method `Callout`, a loaded-vs-relaxed spread bar, and the caveat
  block. All figures bind to `S.cellSpreadRelaxation.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `cellSpreadRelaxation` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `118 → 119` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_CSR_MAXV`)
Rest window = |I|<5 A sustained ≥5 s, immediately preceded by a loaded period (mean
|I|≥20 A over the prior 3 s). Per window: spread (max−min)·1000 mV at load-off, the
rest asymptote (median of the last ≤5 s), the relaxation magnitude (onset−asymptote)
and half-time (first second below onset−0.5·magnitude, only for >1 mV relaxations).
Median/IQR over rest windows; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the
magnitude. Exploratory; sub-5 s relaxation not resolvable at this cadence.

### Findings (277 drives, 544 rest windows, 59 days) — small-effect / near-null
- **Spread at load-off 11 mV** (IQR 9–13.5); **rest asymptote 10 mV** (IQR 8–12).
- **Relaxation magnitude 1 mV** (IQR −0.5 to 3; day-cluster bootstrap CI [1.0, 1.5]);
  52.9% of rests exceed 1 mV.
- The observed relaxation half-time (~1–2 s) sits below the ~1.3 Hz resolvable floor,
  so the ≥5 s relaxation dynamics the analysis targets are essentially absent.

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The max−min spread is a
stable ~10 mV baseline (cell manufacturing/SoC variation); load adds only ~1 mV that
relaxes almost immediately. The shallow-cycled buffer barely stresses the cells —
consistent with the power-buffer picture — reported honestly as a small-effect
result, NOT a cell-health diagnosis.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_cell_spread_relaxation` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (11/10/1 mV; boot CI [1.0,1.5]; 52.9%). Additive module; FINAL isolation diff vs
  pristine: **ADDED the eleven prior new keys plus `cellSpreadRelaxation`; REMOVED
  none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

### Next in the §2 sequence
**S** (VGT-A command tracking + air-path maps), then **R**, **F**, **P**, **S3**,
**S5** — several are thin/exploratory; each channel will be confirmed before build,
and reclassified honestly if too thin to support a real finding.

## M193 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: battery→engine/turbo handoff sequence, extends M116/M118 (feasibility-review candidate B, §2 coarse)

**Scope.** Second §2 module (after H): candidate **B**, battery→engine/turbo handoff
sequence, coarse timing. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives,
`drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Extends M116/M118.** M116 detects the engine start; M118 measures the ramp latency
to the load-point. B adds the full multi-signal ORDERING at each handoff (battery-
discharge peak, engine start, load-point reached, boost onset, discharge
relaxation), reusing `_engine_start_triggers` verbatim for the handoff set.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_handoff_sequence(dm, frame_loader)` +
  `_hs_grid` helper + constants, inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['handoffSequence']` after `socBalancedFuel`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `HandoffSequence()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `SocBalancedFuel`, `Section` accent `#7c3aed`): the median handoff
  timeline SVG, three-line intro, a key-finding `Callout`, and two panels (coarse
  lags; modal orderings). All figures bind to `S.handoffSequence.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `handoffSequence` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `117 → 118` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_HS_RPM`)
Handoff = canonical engine start. Around each t0, coarse event times on a 1 Hz grid:
battery-discharge peak (argmax p=(-I)·V over [t0−8,t0+30]); load-point reached
(first rpm≥1400 at/after t0); boost onset (first boost≥0.10 bar); discharge
relaxation (first drop below half the discharge peak). Per-event coarse lag vs t0
(median/IQR), the modal event ORDERING, and day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000
draws) on the load-point and boost-onset lags. COARSE ONLY: ordering to ~±1–2 s;
t10/t50/t90 below the ~1.3 Hz cadence floor and NOT reported.

### Findings (4,818 handoffs, boost in 53.5%, 67 days)
- **Coarse lags vs engine start:** battery-discharge peak **−0.8 s** (before the
  start), load-point **+0.5 s** (bootstrap CI [0.5, 0.5]), boost onset **+1.6 s**
  (CI [1.5, 1.7]), discharge relaxation **+0.7 s**.
- **Modal ordering** (19.0%): battery peak → engine start → load-point → discharge
  relax; with boost inserted after load-point when present (next most common).
- The buffer moves first (discharge peaks ~0.8 s before the engine starts), the
  engine reaches the load-point in ~0.5 s, boost builds by ~1.6 s, and the battery
  relaxes as the generator assumes the load.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The
handoff is the power-buffer signature in miniature: the pack covers the instantaneous
demand transient first, the generator is recruited and reaches its load-point within
~0.5 s, and the buffer is relieved once the engine carries the load — the whole
handoff completing in ~1–2 s.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_handoff_sequence` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly (4,818
  handoffs; lags −0.8/+0.5/+1.6/+0.7 s; modal ordering 19.0%). Additive module;
  FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED the ten prior new keys plus
  `handoffSequence`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/
  `crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

### Next in the §2 sequence
**N** (cell-spread ≥5 s relaxation, max/min channel), then **S**, **R**, **F**,
**P**, **S3**, **S5**.

## M192 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: SoC-balanced fuel economy (feasibility-review candidate H, §2 subset) — first §2 module

**Scope.** First §2 (subset/exploratory) module after the tier-1 sequence:
candidate **H**, SoC-balanced fuel economy on the August accumulator subset.
Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5
`396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Why.** Raw trip L/100 km is confounded by SoC drift: a trip ending lower-SoC
borrowed buffer energy (flattering economy); one ending higher-SoC spent fuel
charging the buffer. H corrects this with a physical energy-equivalence.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_soc_balanced_fuel(dm, raw_loader,
  raw_dir)` + `_hf_perdrive` helper + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['socBalancedFuel']` into the raw block after
  `thermalWarmupLag`. Reads the used-fuel accumulator `Використане паливо (L)`
  directly from raw (not in the slim cache) via `raw_loader` (with a `raw_dir`
  fallback; local `import os` so the fallback is robust).
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `SocBalancedFuel()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `ThermalWarmupLag`, `Section` accent `#16a34a`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, a raw-vs-balanced fleet bar comparison, and two panels
  (η-sensitivity; charge-balancing regression). All figures bind to
  `S.socBalancedFuel.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `socBalancedFuel` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `116 → 117` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical to M191 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_HF_FUEL`)
August accumulator subset: drives carrying the monotonic used-fuel accumulator;
trip fuel = accumulator delta, distance = speed integral, ΔSoC = end−start. Raw
L/100 km is SoC-balanced by subtracting the fuel-equivalent of the net battery-
energy change: ΔFuel = ΔE/(η·LHV), ΔE = ΔSoC/100·CAP_KWH (CAP=2.1 kWh,
verified:false), swept over η ∈ {0.25,0.30,0.35} (LHV 8.9 kWh/L), headline η=0.30.
Day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the balanced fleet economy. A
charge-balancing regression (fuel ~ dist + ΔE) is reported as a descriptive
cross-check only — the ΔE coefficient is NOT identifiable (2.1 kWh buffer → tiny
per-trip energy variance), so no generator efficiency is claimed.

### Findings (55 accumulator drives, 15 days, 2026-08-12→08-28, 796.9 km, 42.07 L)
- **Raw fleet economy 5.28 L/100 km** (distance-weighted; per-trip median 5.47,
  IQR 4.8–7.2).
- **SoC-balanced fleet economy 5.13 L/100 km** (η=0.30; day-cluster bootstrap 95%
  CI [4.91, 5.36]); robust to η (5.10 / 5.13 / 5.15 at η 0.25/0.30/0.35).
- **The SoC correction is small (−0.15 L/100 km, ~3%)** — because the 2.1 kWh
  buffer holds <0.1 L of fuel-equivalent, its charge state cannot materially move
  the fuel accounting. Per-trip the correction matters only for short high-drift
  outliers (|Δ| median 0.27, p95 ~2.5 L/100 km).
- ΔSoC per trip median +3 pp (range −14 to +17) — net trips ended slightly
  higher-SoC, so balancing lowers economy.
- Regression (R²=0.95, descriptive): per-trip fixed fuel 0.10 L (15% of a typical
  trip — the cold-start/idle overhead, a bigger per-trip factor than SoC drift),
  SoC-neutral marginal economy 4.56 L/100 km; ΔE coefficient not identifiable.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** SoC-
balancing — which materially shifts economy for large-pack plug-in hybrids — is
nearly immaterial here (≈3%). That the pack is too small for its charge state to
distort fuel accounting is itself a power-buffer (not energy-reservoir)
confirmation.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_soc_balanced_fuel` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (raw 5.28, balanced 5.13, boot CI [4.91,5.36], regression intercept 0.10 /
  marginal 4.56 / R²=0.95). Additive module; FINAL isolation diff vs pristine:
  **ADDED the nine tier-1 keys plus `socBalancedFuel`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.**
  `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

### Subset caveats (displayed)
Single month, urban-dominated (no pure-highway fuel), summer (no seasonal-cold
penalty). CAP_KWH unverified; η assumed and swept; ΔE regression coefficient not
identifiable. Do not generalise to the full corpus.

### Next in the §2 sequence
**B** (handoff sequence, coarse timing), then **N**, **S**, **R**, **F**, **P**,
**S3**, **S5**.

## M191 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: coolant/oil warm-up + coolant–oil lag, extends warmupCurve (feasibility-review candidate O-thermal) — tier-1 sequence COMPLETE

**Scope.** Ninth and final module of the tier-1 "implement now" sequence (after D,
A, C, I, J, E, G, K): candidate **O-thermal**, coolant/oil warm-up + coolant–oil
lag. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5
`396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Extends warmupCurve.** warmupCurve (M31/M86) is distance-domain COOLANT rise only.
O adds the engine OIL warm-up trajectory and the coolant–oil thermal lag, in the
time domain, on cold-start drives. Oil (more thermal mass, indirect heating) lags
the coolant. The fuel-penalty part (Aug-only subset) and emissions (uninstrumented)
are explicitly NOT computed here, per the review's O tiering.

### What changed
- **`drive_raw_cache.py`**: `SCHEMA_VERSION` 6 → 7; added the engine oil-temperature
  channel `Температура олії у двигуні (℃)` to `SLIM_COLS` (~96% corpus coverage,
  reusable by later thermal work). Cache rebuilt from scratch (290 entries, 61 s).
  Same superset-add pattern as M167 (v4→v5) and M184 (v5→v6).
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_thermal_warmup_lag(dm, frame_loader)` +
  `_twl_grid`/`_twl_time_to` helpers + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['thermalWarmupLag']` after
  `engineStateMachine`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `ThermalWarmupLag()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `EngineStateMachine`, `Section` accent `#ea580c`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, the paired coolant/oil warm-up-curve SVG with the 70 °C
  reference, and two summary panels (time-to-threshold; lag & offset). All figures
  bind to `S.thermalWarmupLag.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `thermalWarmupLag` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `115 → 116` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical.

### Method (see the block comment above `_TWL_COOL`)
Cold-start drives (coolant start <60 °C). Per drive on a 1 Hz grid: time from start
for coolant and oil to cross 60/70/80 °C; coolant→oil lag = oil_t70 − coolant_t70;
steady-state offset = median(coolant − oil) once coolant≥80 °C; paired warm-up
curves (median temp by time-from-start bin). Medians/IQR over cold-start drives;
day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the lag.

### Findings (173 cold-start drives of 279; 172 with oil temp; 67 days)
- **Coolant → 70 °C in 262 s** (IQR 180–376); **80 °C in 337 s**.
- **Oil → 70 °C in 600 s** (IQR 436–886); **80 °C in 1060 s** (~18 min) — far slower.
- **Coolant–oil lag to 70 °C = 305 s** (~5 min; day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI
  [250, 382]) — oil trails coolant by ~5 minutes.
- **Steady-state coolant–oil offset 9 °C** (IQR 5–15) — oil runs cooler even once warm.
- Warm-up curves: both start ~36–38 °C; coolant reaches 80 °C by ~420–600 s while
  oil is still ~61 °C there, only nearing 76 °C by 600–900 s.

**Reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The coolant gauge reads
"warm" while the oil is still climbing for several more minutes; the engine is not
fully thermally settled until well into a trip — the thermal basis for the
short-trip penalty (and, on the August fuel subset, its economic cost). No sub-15 °C
ambient data exists, so this characterises warm-season cold-starts only.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_thermal_warmup_lag` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (173 cold starts; coolant/oil t70 262/600 s; lag 305 s; offset 9 °C).
- **Schema-v7 non-perturbation verified**: an existing slim-cache-derived key,
  `lowSpeedDissipation`, recomputes byte-identical to the pristine shipped value
  under the v7 cache, and `crawlStopGo` reproduces its FINAL value — confirming the
  oil-column add changes no existing computed value (the same superset-safety M184
  established via a completed full control build). Full end-to-end build hits the
  documented OOM ceiling (M148), so the module is generated via the production
  function and spliced. FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED
  `['crawlStopGo','accelDecelEnvelopes','rpmSpeedSync','engineStartContext',
  'bufferDebtRecovery','drivingStateTaxonomy','departureArrival','engineStateMachine',
  'thermalWarmupLag']` (all nine tier-1 modules from this session); REMOVED none;
  CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

### Tier-1 sequence status
**COMPLETE.** All nine "implement now" candidates (D, A, C, I, J, E, G, K,
O-thermal) are implemented, corpus-verified, isolation-verified and dashboard-
rendered across M183–M191. Remaining feasibility-review work is the §2 subset/
exploratory tier (H, B, N, S, R, F, …) and the flagged follow-ups: hand-validation
of the engine-start context labels (I), and the O fuel-penalty August-subset
sub-analysis.

## M190 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: engine operating-point state machine, extends rpmDistribution + M118 (feasibility-review candidate K)

**Scope.** Eighth module of the tier-1 sequence (after D, A, C, I, J, E, G):
candidate **K**, engine operating-point state machine. Corpus- and methodology-
unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged);
M119-v2 carried forward.

**Extends, ≠ duplicate.** `rpmDistribution` (M82) is RPM occupancy only; M118 is
start-dwell only. K adds the full operating-point state machine: per-state dwell,
entry rate, the transition matrix and per-state buffer power across all engine time.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_engine_state_machine(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` + `_esm_grid`/`_esm_classify` helpers + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['engineStateMachine']` after
  `departureArrival`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `EngineStateMachine()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `DepartureArrival`, `Section` accent `#7c3aed`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, the 5×5 transition heatmap, a per-state table
  (occupancy/dwell/battery kW with the RPM band), and the caveat block. All figures
  bind to `S.engineStateMachine.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `engineStateMachine` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `114 → 115` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical to M189 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_ESM_COLS`)
Per-second operating-point state on a 1 Hz grid: off rpm<400; low 400–1400;
loadPoint 1400–2300 (the OEM-nominal ~2000-rpm generator load-point — NOT a measured
BSFC optimum, no efficiency claim); mid 2300–3200; high ≥3200. Per drive: occupancy,
within-drive first-order transitions (t→t+1), per-state dwell run-lengths, per-state
entry counts and per-state battery kW (p=(-I)·V, M11). Occupancy is per-drive
median/IQR with a day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws); dwell, entry rate
(per engine-on hour), battery kW and the transition matrix are pooled.

### Findings (289 drives, 67.9 engine-on hours, 71 days)
- **Engine off 67% of the time** (self-transition 0.979); when running it sits
  overwhelmingly at the **load-point (30% occupancy, dwell 8 s, self-transition
  0.944)** — a clear attractor entered **162×/engine-hour**, the most-entered state.
- The engine jumps **off→loadPoint directly**; the "low" band is a 1 s transient
  (self-transition 0.393) it passes through on the ramp.
- Excursions to mid/high are brief (dwell 3–4 s) and fall back to the load-point
  (mid→loadPoint 0.121).
- **Per-state battery power:** off **+1.85 kW** (buffer supplying), load-point
  **−4.22 kW** (generator refilling), low **−8.54 kW** (hard charge during ramp),
  mid **+3.05**, high **+2.64 kW** (demand outruns the running generator).

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The
off↔load-point cycle IS the buffer's charge/discharge cycle at the engine level: off
→ the pack supplies; load-point → the generator refills the pack; brief high-rpm
excursions when demand outruns the running generator. The engine behaves as a
bang-bang generator around a single load-point, exactly as a power-buffer (not
energy-reservoir) architecture implies.

## M189 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: departure/arrival vs matched mid-trip (feasibility-review candidate G)

**Scope.** Seventh module of the tier-1 sequence (after D, A, C, I, J, E): candidate
**G**, departure/arrival behaviour. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session
(290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Why new.** No prior block contrasts trip boundaries against the steady middle;
`shortTripWarmup` touches departure warm-up once, arrival never.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_departure_arrival(dm, frame_loader)` +
  `_da_grid`/`_da_wmetrics`/`_da_speed_matched` helpers + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['departureArrival']` after
  `drivingStateTaxonomy`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `DepartureArrival()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `DrivingStateTaxonomy`, `Section` accent `#ea580c`): three KPI cards,
  a key-finding `Callout`, dep/mid/arr triple bars for the confound-free channels
  (coolant, SoC), the speed-matched control panel, and the caveat block. All figures
  bind to `S.departureArrival.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `departureArrival` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `113 → 114` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical to M188 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_DA_COLS`)
Within-drive paired windows of W=60 s on drives ≥240 s: departure (first W),
midtrip (centre W), arrival (last W), non-overlapping. Per window: median battery kW
(p=(-I)·V, M11), engine-on fraction (rpm>400), mean SoC/speed/coolant, canonical
start count. Boundary-vs-mid reported as within-drive paired deltas (each drive its
own control). **Boundary windows are low-speed by construction**, confounding
engine-on/battery-kW; for those a SPEED-MATCHED control uses mid-third seconds within
the boundary window's [p10,p90] speed band. SoC and coolant are not speed-driven, so
their departure deltas are the confound-free headlines (day-clustered bootstrap, seed
42, 4000 draws). Time-normalised (GPS-free, corpus-wide).

### Findings (275 drives, 71 days)
- **Departure is cold: coolant −25.6 °C vs mid-trip** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI
  [−28.3, −20.8]) — the cold-start signature (departure 51 °C vs mid 83 °C).
- **Departure starts with a depleted buffer: SoC −4.5 pp vs mid** (CI [−6.0, −3.3])
  (departure 57.8% vs mid 62.7%); the trip refills the buffer to its operating band.
- **Arrival is indistinguishable from mid-trip** in coolant (+1.5 °C) and SoC
  (−0.8 pp) — arrival is just a low-speed slice, not a distinct state.
- **The apparent "engine off at boundaries" is entirely a speed artifact**: the
  speed-matched departure engine-on delta is 0.0 (IQR −0.06–0) and arrival 0.0 — once
  speed is matched, the engine-on difference vanishes. A small residual remains: at
  matched speed, departure draws +0.78 kW more battery power (cold-start accessory
  load).

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** Each trip
departs cold and buffer-depleted and is spent warming the engine and refilling the
buffer to its operating band; by mid-trip and arrival the buffer sits in-band. The
boundary engine-on difference is kinematic (low speed), not a distinct control mode —
a clean negative result the speed-matched control establishes.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_departure_arrival` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly.
  Full end-to-end control build hits the documented OOM ceiling (M148); module is
  strictly additive and the schema-v6 cache was proven byte-identical-reproducing in

## M188 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: within-drive driving-state taxonomy (feasibility-review candidate E)

**Scope.** Sixth module of the tier-1 sequence (after D, A, C, I, J): candidate **E**,
within-drive driving-state taxonomy. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session
(290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Why new, ≠ M142.** M142 `regimeTransition` is a BETWEEN-drive first-order Markov
chain over whole-drive TYPES (drive granularity). E is a WITHIN-drive, 1 Hz
instantaneous-state taxonomy — a different granularity and estimand. It is also
distinct from D (stop-go cycles) and A (speed-conditioned envelopes): E adds the
state-occupancy census, the within-drive state Markov structure and per-state
buffer behaviour.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_driving_state_taxonomy(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` + `_dst_grid`/`_dst_classify` helpers + constants, inserted before
  `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['drivingStateTaxonomy']` after
  `bufferDebtRecovery`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `DrivingStateTaxonomy()` component
  (Distribution tab, after `BufferDebtRecovery`, `Section` accent `#2563eb`):
  an occupancy stacked bar, a key-finding `Callout`, the 4×4 within-drive
  transition heatmap, a per-state table (battery kW / engine-on / dwell), and the
  caveat block. All figures bind to `S.drivingStateTaxonomy.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `drivingStateTaxonomy` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `112 → 113` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical to M187 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_DST_COLS`)
Per-second state on a 1 Hz grid (speed via M167 priority; accel from the logged
accel(g) sensor, schema-v6): idle speed<3 km/h; accel accg≥+0.02 g; decel
accg≤−0.02 g; cruise otherwise (moving). Per drive: occupancy fraction, within-drive
first-order transition counts (t→t+1), per-state battery kW (p=(-I)·V, M11),
engine-on fraction (rpm>400) and dwell run-lengths. Occupancy is per-drive
median/IQR with a day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws); transition
probabilities, per-state battery kW and dwell are pooled.

### Findings (289 drives, 71 days)
- **Occupancy (per-drive median):** cruise **38%**, accel **21%**, decel **21%**,
  idle **18%** — accel/decel near-symmetric, cruise the plurality.
- **Per-state battery power** tracks the buffer cleanly: accel **+4.83 kW** (draw),
  decel **−2.07 kW** (regen), cruise **+0.56 kW** (near-balanced), idle **+1.20 kW**
  (accessory/maintenance).
- **Engine-on fraction:** cruise 61%, accel 56%, decel 27%, idle 9% — the generator
  runs where sustained/high demand sits, off at stops and during regen.
- **Within-drive transitions are sticky** (self-transition idle 0.955, cruise 0.914,
  accel 0.860, decel 0.860), with the expected accel→cruise (0.114) and
  cruise→decel/accel structure.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The state
census ties kinematics to buffer flow directly: the pack sources power in accel,
sinks regen in decel, and sits near-balanced in cruise, while the generator runs
where demand is sustained — the power buffer working state-by-state.

## M187 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: buffer energy-debt recovery, extends M116 (feasibility-review candidate J)

**Scope.** Fifth module of the tier-1 sequence (after D, A, C, I): candidate **J**,
buffer energy-debt recovery. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives,
`drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged); M119-v2 carried forward.

**Extends M116.** M116 `bufferImpulse` measures the discharge impulse (energy debt)
the pack sources at each engine start. J measures the recovery that follows: how
fast and how completely the generator refills that debt. It **reuses
`_buffer_impulse_events` verbatim** for the event set and per-event debt (no
re-derivation), then integrates net-discharge energy forward over a recovery window.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_buffer_debt_recovery(dm, frame_loader)`
  + `_bdr_grid` helper + constants, inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['bufferDebtRecovery']` into the raw block after `engineStartContext`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `BufferDebtRecovery()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `EngineStartContext`, `Section` accent `#16a34a`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, a schematic debt→recovery curve using the measured
  half-time with a t½ marker, two summary panels (per-impulse medians + outcome
  shares), and the caveat block. All figures bind to `S.bufferDebtRecovery.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `bufferDebtRecovery` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `111 → 112` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; other core files byte-identical to M186 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_BDR_I`)
Reuse `_buffer_impulse_events` for the impulse set and debt (≥3 Wh floor). On a 1 Hz
I/V grid, integrate net-discharge Wh from the event over a 120 s window (signed
p=(-I)·V, M11). The debt peak is the cumulative-net-discharge maximum (~impulse
end); recovery is measured from there. recoveryHalfTimeS = time to repay 50% of the
debt; fracRecovered120 = net fraction repaid by window end (clamped ≤1);
overshootFrac = peak refill past the debt (generator banking headroom while
running); fracNotRecovered120 = residual; socRecoveredPP = independent SoC
cross-check. Per-event median/IQR; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on
median half-time.

### Findings (2,270 impulses across 215 drives, 62 days)
- **Recovery half-time 8.0 s** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [7.0, 9.0], 61 days) —
  the generator repays half the debt in ~8 s.
- **Energy debt 61.9 Wh / impulse** (IQR 31.6–104.2).
- **Fraction recovered by 120 s: 0.913** (IQR 0.21–1.0); **8.7% median not
  recovered**; **47.3% fully recovered** within the window.
- **57.7% of impulses overshoot** (median +37% past the debt, i.e. the generator
  refills beyond the impulse to bank buffer headroom while already running).
- SoC cross-check rises **+2.5 pp** median — confirms the buffer refills.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** Rapid
discharge burst (~62 Wh), rapid generator-driven refill (t½ ≈ 8 s), typically
overshooting to bank headroom — the defining power-buffer cycle. The pack is churned
and refilled by the ICE on a seconds timescale, never used as a deep reservoir.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_buffer_debt_recovery` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (2,270 events, t½ 8.0 s, debt 61.9 Wh, 57.7% overshoot). Full end-to-end control
  build hit the documented OOM ceiling (M148); module is strictly additive and the
  schema-v6 cache was proven byte-identical-reproducing in M184's completed control
  build, so the payload was generated via the production function and spliced. FINAL
  isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED `['crawlStopGo','accelDecelEnvelopes',
  'rpmSpeedSync','engineStartContext','bufferDebtRecovery']` (this session's five
  modules); REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC`/`crossVehicle`
  preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: build gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console errors.

## M186 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: engine-start context taxonomy (feasibility-review candidate I)

**Scope.** Fourth module of the tier-1 sequence (after D, A, C): candidate **I**,
engine-start context taxonomy. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session
(290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged, no ingestion); M119-v2
carried forward.

**Why new, ≠ M119.** M119/M119-v2 model start PROBABILITY (a hazard model);
`engineStartsByType` counts starts per drive-type. I instead *classifies the
pre-start context* of each start with rule-based multi-label rules and reports the
label mix and the unclassified share — a descriptive "why did it fire?" taxonomy.
It reuses the **canonical** debounced detector verbatim (`_engine_start_triggers`,
the RPM>800-preceded-by-sustained-RPM≤100 trigger shared by M116/M119), not the
frozen M119-v2 model.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_engine_start_context(dm, frame_loader)`
  + helpers (`_isc_grid`, `_isc_context`, `_isc_labels`, grounded threshold
  constants), inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['engineStartContext']` into the raw block after `rpmSpeedSync`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `EngineStartContext()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `RpmSpeedSync`, `Section` accent `#7c3aed`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, a horizontal label-share bar chart (incl. the unclassified
  bar), the threshold-sensitivity note, an illustrative classified-start sample, and
  the caveat block. All figures bind to `S.engineStartContext.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `engineStartContext` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `110 → 111` keys.
- `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged; the other core files are byte-identical to their
  M185 state.

### Method (see the block comment above `_ISC_SOC`)
Canonical start trigger per drive; per start, pre-start context from a 1 Hz grid —
SoC/speed/coolant at the last valid sample in [t0−2s, t0]; demand = median discharge
kW and median clipped TARGET torque over [t0−5s, t0−1s] (M102: actual torque
invalid). Multi-label rules, thresholds grounded on the observed pre-start
distributions (SoC clusters 54–70%, speed 22–85 km/h, coolant mostly warm, demand
median ~10 kW / torque ~27 N·m): lowBuffer SoC≤55; socMaintenance 55<SoC≤63;
highDemand disc≥20 kW or tqTgt≥60 N·m; highSpeedCruise speed≥70; creepLaunch
speed<20; coldEngine coolant≤60 °C. Starts matching no rule are reported as
unclassified. Day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on per-drive starts/100
km. A `thresholdSensitivity` sweep and a `validationSample` (for the pending
hand-validation) are shipped.

### Findings (4,951 canonical starts, all with context; 70 days)
- Label mix (multi-label, so shares sum >100%): **highDemand 28.5%**,
  **highSpeedCruise 27.5%**, **socMaintenance 22.4%**, **lowBuffer 10.8%**,
  creepLaunch 8.8%, coldEngine 4.3%.
- **Unclassified 27.5%** (mean 1.023 labels/start) — mostly SoC at/above setpoint
  with moderate speed and low demand, i.e. no single dominant trigger; reported
  honestly, not force-fit.
- **82.2 engine starts / 100 km** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [73.4, 89.4]).
- Threshold-robust: low-buffer share 4.6 / 10.8 / 18.5% at SoC {50, 55, 60}; the
  label ranking is stable across the sweep.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The two
leading triggers are instantaneous power demand and sustained high-speed cruise
(≈28% each), with a further ~33% driven by SoC-band maintenance (top-up +
low-buffer). The generator fires either when demand outruns the buffer's delivery
or to keep the buffer in-band — both faces of power-buffer, not energy-reservoir,
operation.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- Production `_engine_start_context` reproduced the standalone prototype exactly
  (4,951 starts, 27.5% unclassified, identical label shares). Full end-to-end
  control build hit the documented OOM ceiling (M148); as with M185, the module is
  strictly additive and the schema-v6 cache was already proven byte-identical-
  reproducing in M184's completed control build, so the payload was generated via
  the production function and spliced. FINAL isolation diff vs pristine: **ADDED
  `['crawlStopGo','accelDecelEnvelopes','rpmSpeedSync','engineStartContext']` (this
  session's four modules); REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC` and
  `crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.

## M185 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: engine RPM–speed synchronisation / series-hybrid decoupling (feasibility-review candidate C)

**Scope.** Third module of the tier-1 sequence (`feasibility_review_new_findings.md`,
after D and A): candidate **C**, RPM–speed synchronisation. Corpus- and
methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…`
unchanged, no ingestion) — code-and-arrays-only. **M119-v2 not recomputed**
(carried forward via `prev_arrays`).

**Why new.** No existing block relates engine RPM to wheel speed. The estimand is
architecture-specific: in a series hybrid the engine turns only the generator, so
its RPM is mechanically decoupled from speed; C quantifies that decoupling and
contrasts it against a geartrain reference (ρ≈1).

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_rpm_speed_sync(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` + helpers (`_rsync_grid`, `_rsync_spearman`, `_RSYNC_COLS`/edges),
  inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired `arrays['rpmSpeedSync']` into the raw
  block immediately after `accelDecelEnvelopes`. Spearman ρ is computed
  dependency-free (Pearson on pandas ranks) — no new import added to the core
  module.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `RpmSpeedSync()` component (Distribution tab,
  after `AccelDecelEnvelopes`, `Section` accent `#7c3aed`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, the RPM-vs-speed envelope SVG (median + IQR band with the
  generator-load-point reference line), a per-drive summary panel, an exploratory
  lead/lag histogram, and the caveat block. All figures bind to `S.rpmSpeedSync.*`.
- **`build_html.js`**: `rpmSpeedSync` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt. **`summary_arrays.json`**: `109 → 110` keys.
- Other core pipeline/JSX files byte-identical to pristine; the two files touched
  earlier this session (`drive_raw_cache.py` schema-v6, and A's edits) are unchanged
  from their M184 state. `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged.

### Method (see the block comment above `_RSYNC_COLS`)
Per drive, engine-on (rpm>400) moving (speed≥3 km/h) 1 Hz samples: Spearman ρ (rank
monotonicity), OLS slope (rpm per km/h), and load-point fraction (rpm in
[1800,2200]) as per-drive median/IQR; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws)
on median ρ. `rpmBySpeed` is the pooled engine-on RPM occupancy envelope per speed
bin. Lead/lag is the per-drive best speed–RPM cross-correlation lag over ±2 s,
exploratory only (cadence-limited). No acoustic/NVH claim (no cabin-noise channel).

### Findings (281 drives covered, 70 days)
- **RPM–speed rank correlation ρ = 0.377** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI
  [0.334, 0.425]) — far below a mechanical geartrain's ≈1.
- **slope 8.3 rpm per km/h** (per-drive median) — shallow; a fixed-gear geartrain
  would be several times steeper and gear-stepped.
- **71% of engine-on time at the ~2000-rpm generator load-point** (IQR 59–81%).
- The RPM-vs-speed envelope is flat at ~2000 rpm across the entire 30–110 km/h
  range (median 1999–2001 rpm), rising only above 110 km/h (2507 rpm at 110–130,
  3464 at 130+) when sustained high-speed demand exceeds buffer supply.
- Lead/lag skews to +lag (speed leads RPM) — the engine responds to demand — but
  this is exploratory at the cadence floor.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The low ρ,
shallow slope and load-point clamp are the defining series-hybrid decoupling
signature: the engine is a generator serving power demand and the buffer at a
near-constant efficient RPM, not a traction source geared to the wheels.

### Validation
- `py_compile` clean; acceptance tests **T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS**.
- The production `_rpm_speed_sync` (run via the pipeline module against the real
  frame_loader) reproduces the standalone prototype byte-for-byte (ρ boot 0.377,
  CI [0.334,0.425], load-point 0.711, slope 8.301). The full end-to-end control
  build hit the documented ≤4 GB sandbox OOM ceiling (M148) on this corpus; since
  C is strictly additive (new function + new key, no edit to any existing function)
  and the schema-v6 cache was already proven in M184's completed control build to
  reproduce every base key byte-identical, the module's output was generated
  directly and spliced. FINAL isolation diff vs the pristine shipped file:
  **ADDED `['crawlStopGo','accelDecelEnvelopes','rpmSpeedSync']` (this session's
  three modules); REMOVED none; CHANGED none.** `energyUncertaintyMC` and
  `crossVehicle` preserved verbatim.
- Dashboard: `build_html.js` gates pass; jsdom 9 tabs / 52 buttons / 0 console
  errors, M119-v2 still renders.

## M184 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: accel/decel speed-binned dynamics envelopes (feasibility-review candidate A)

**Scope.** Second module of the tier-1 sequence (`feasibility_review_new_findings.md`,
after D): candidate **A**, acceleration/deceleration dynamics envelopes. Corpus-
and methodology-unchanged session (290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…`
unchanged, no ingestion) — a code-and-arrays-only addition. **M119-v2 not
recomputed** (`recompute_m119v2=False`, carried forward from M182 via
`prev_arrays`, unchanged).

**Why new, not a duplicate.** `torqueBySpeed` is a speed × target-torque
*occupancy* histogram only — no phase split, no dynamics envelope. A conditions
the joint dynamics (acceleration, battery power, engine RPM, boost, target
torque, SoC-rate) on speed AND on accel/decel phase, which no existing block does.

### What changed
- **`drive_raw_cache.py`**: `SCHEMA_VERSION` 5 → 6; added the logged longitudinal
  acceleration channel `Прискорення (g)` to `SLIM_COLS`. This is a first-class
  batched-synchronous sensor reading (~1.26 Hz, same rows as speed/RPM/SoC), NOT a
  diff(speed) derivative — the sensor is far less noisy. The bump invalidates the
  slim cache; it was rebuilt from scratch (290 entries, 66 s). Same pattern as M167
  (v4 → v5 for OBD speed). The channel is reused by the later C (RPM–speed sync)
  and E (driving-state taxonomy) modules, so it belongs in the cache once.
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_accel_decel_envelopes(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` and helpers (`_ade_grid`, `_ade_mi`, `_ade_dayboot`, `_ADE_COLS`,
  `_ADE_SPEED_EDGES`), inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, wired
  `arrays['accelDecelEnvelopes']` into the raw block immediately after
  `crawlStopGo`. frame_loader-preferred with raw_loader fallback.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `AccelDecelEnvelopes()` component (Distribution
  tab, after `CrawlStopGo`, `Section` accent `#ea580c`): three KPI cards, a
  key-finding `Callout`, a battery-power-vs-speed dual envelope SVG (accel + / decel
  −, median line + IQR band), a per-band medians table, the threshold-sensitivity
  line and the resolution/caveat block. Every figure binds to
  `S.accelDecelEnvelopes.*` — no computed literals in the JSX.
- **`build_html.js`**: `accelDecelEnvelopes` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`.
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt.
- **`summary_arrays.json`**: `108 → 109` keys.
- The other core pipeline/JSX files are byte-identical to pristine; `drive_master.csv`
  MD5 `396d157…` unchanged.

### Method (see the block comment above `_ADE_COLS`)
Per-drive 1 Hz grid (resample → ffill(limit=3); speed via the M167 VCM/OBD priority
rule). Phase from the logged accel(g): ACCEL accg ≥ +0.02 g, DECEL accg ≤ −0.02 g,
moving samples (speed ≥ 3 km/h) only. Battery power p=(-I)·V/1000 kW (M11 discharge-
positive): +ve = traction draw, −ve = regen/charge. Ten speed bins (0–130+ km/h);
per (phase, bin) pooled sample median/IQR of accg, battKw, engine RPM, boost, per-
second SoC-rate and TARGET motor torque (M102: actual torque/RPM invalid). Unit
discipline: pooled samples give the per-bin envelope shape (nSamples), but CIs use a
day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) over PER-DRIVE medians — never 1 Hz
seconds as replicates. thresholdSensitivity sweeps the accel/decel threshold
{0.015, 0.02, 0.03} g.

### Findings (289/290 drives covered, 277 with I&V; 71 days)
- **median battery power, accel phase: +3.95 kW** (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI
  [3.31, 4.61], 67 days) — the pack sources traction power. Per-band: accel draw
  peaks mid-range (≈ +7.7 kW at 30–40 km/h).
- **median battery power, decel phase: −1.72 kW** (CI [−2.10, −1.31]) — the pack
  sinks regen; per-band regen deepens strongly with speed (≈ −4.9 kW at 20–30 up to
  ≈ −32 kW at 130+ km/h).
- **Engine RPM = 0 through the low/mid accel bands** (pure-electric launch), rising
  to the ~2000-rpm generator load-point only from ~50 km/h and higher (~2560–3950)
  at sustained high-speed demand; boost and target torque track the same recruitment.
- Robust to threshold: accel median 3.14 / 3.95 / 5.44 kW and decel −1.51 / −1.72 /
  −2.03 kW across {0.015, 0.02, 0.03} g — same sign and order of magnitude.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver).** The
speed-conditioned envelope is a clean power-buffer signature: the pack sources
launch/accel power and sinks decel regen, with the engine recruited (at a fixed
generator load-point) only when sustained demand exceeds what the buffer supplies —
exactly power-buffer, not energy-reservoir, behaviour.

**Resolution limits (disclosed).** Acceleration is the logged sensor, but sub-second
latency / time-constants remain below the ~1.26 Hz cadence floor and are NOT
reported. Jerk (|d accg/dt|, p95 ≈ 0.077 g/s accel / 0.041 g/s decel) and the per-
second SoC-rate column are exploratory only — SoC-rate is quantisation-dominated
(0.5 % steps at ~1 Hz), so the battery-kW envelope is the real energy-flow signal.

## M183 (2026-08-29) — New analysis: crawl & stop-go operating-mode census (feasibility-review candidate D, top priority)

**Scope.** First module of the Phase-1 feasibility/novelty review's tier-1
"implement now" sequence (`feasibility_review_new_findings.md`): candidate **D**,
crawl & stop-go operating mode. Corpus- and methodology-unchanged session
(290 drives, `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged, no ingestion) — a
code-and-arrays-only addition. **M119-v2 not recomputed** (`recompute_m119v2=
False`, carried forward from M182 via `prev_arrays`, unchanged).

**Why new, not a duplicate.** The only prior low-speed-halt reading is
`standstillStats` (M26), which is *pure* key-on standstill (speed==0)
parasitic draw and says nothing about the launch→crawl→approach→stop CYCLE
that dominates urban duty (219/290 drives). D segments that cycle and
integrates the buffer energy each phase moves — a genuinely new estimand.

### What changed
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: added `_crawl_stop_go(dm, raw_loader,
  frame_loader)` and helpers (`_csg_grid`, `_csg_events`, `_csg_runs`,
  `_csg_med_iqr`, `_csg_dayboot`), inserted before `_day_label_by_file`, and
  wired `arrays['crawlStopGo']` into the raw block immediately after
  `lowSpeedDissipation`. frame_loader-preferred with raw_loader fallback,
  matching `_low_speed_dissipation`.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: added the `CrawlStopGo()` dashboard component
  (rendered in the Distribution tab, immediately after
  `LowSpeedDissipation`, as a `Section` accent `#0891b2`). Four KPI cards
  (net Wh/cycle + bootstrap CI, gross launch-out, gross approach-in, engine
  starts/10 min), a key-finding `Callout` with an `EvidenceBadge`, a
  per-cycle energy-flow SVG (launch-out vs approach-in median + IQR + p95),
  a by-drive-type grid, the threshold-sensitivity table, and coverage/caution
  `Caveat`s. Every figure binds to `S.crawlStopGo.*` — no computed literals in
  the JSX.
- **`build_html.js`**: `crawlStopGo` registered in `REQUIRED_BLOCKS` (the
  build now aborts if a future regeneration drops the dashboard-bound key).
- **`xtrail_dashboard.html`**: rebuilt from the above.
- The remaining core pipeline/JSX files (the other 11) are byte-identical to
  the pristine M182 tree; `drive_master.csv` MD5 `396d157…` unchanged.
- **`summary_arrays.json`**: `107 → 108` keys. Isolation-diff vs the pristine
  M182 file: **ADDED `['crawlStopGo']`; REMOVED none; CHANGED none.**
  `energyUncertaintyMC` (out-of-band MC block `build_summary_arrays` never
  emits) carried forward verbatim; `crossVehicle` preserved verbatim
  (a fresh `crosscheck_*.inject()` reproduced its payload byte-for-byte,
  differing only in `_meta.generated` wall-clock stamps, so the shipped block
  was retained to keep the on-disk diff to the single new key).

### Method (see the block comment above `_CSG_COLS`)
Per-drive 1 Hz grid (`resample('1s').mean().ffill(limit=3)`; speed resolved by
the M167 VCM/OBD priority rule before use). STOP = speed<1.5 km/h sustained
≥3 s; LAUNCH/APPROACH = transient to/from 15 km/h (cap 20 s); STOP-GO CYCLE =
consecutive-stop pair with inter-stop speed peak ≤30 km/h. Energy uses the
module convention `p_dis=(-I)*V/1000` kW (M11 discharge-positive):
`whCycleNet` = signed integral over the cycle; `whLaunchOut` / `whApproachIn`
= GROSS discharge-out / regen-in over the phase windows; `recoveryRatio` =
in/out. The gross/net split is deliberate — at ≤15 km/h approach regen is
small and net approach flow is frequently still discharge (creep + accessory
load), so a single signed "approach regen" would mislead. Aggregation is
cycle/drive/day (never 1 Hz seconds as replicates); median/IQR for skewed
energy; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) for headline CIs.
Threshold sensitivity sweeps STOP_V ∈ {1.0,1.5,2.5} and stop-go-ceiling ∈
{25,30,40} km/h.

### Findings (286/290 drives covered, 275 with I&V for energy; 1394 stop-go
### cycles, 2844 stops, 2404 launches)
- **net Wh per stop-go cycle: 6.13 Wh** (day-cluster bootstrap median, 95% CI
  [5.50, 7.17], 67 days; cycle-level median 6.13, IQR 2.52–15.03).
- **launch-out 4.13 Wh** (IQR 1.68–10.83) vs **approach-in ≈ 0.0 Wh**
  (IQR 0.0–1.68); **recoveryRatio median ≈ 0** (IQR 0.0–0.09).
- **engine starts per 10 min of low-speed operation: 2.31** (bootstrap CI
  [1.99, 2.67], 70 days).
- Headline robust to thresholds: net Wh/cycle median 5.56–7.16, starts/10 min
  1.86–2.97 across the sweep.

**Buffer-thesis reading (descriptive, single-vehicle / ~single-driver; no
causal or control-strategy claim).** In low-speed stop-go the pack is spent to
launch (≈4 Wh) and returns almost none of it on the deceleration
(recovery ≈ 0, because e-POWER regen is minimal below ~15 km/h) — so the
cycle's energy is closed by the GENERATOR (~2.3 restarts / 10 min of
low-speed operation), not by regen. This is a clean power-buffer signature:
the pack is churned and refilled by the ICE, not replenished by braking, at
crawl speeds.

**Resolution limits (disclosed).** Sub-second launch dynamics (jerk,
t10/t50/t90) are below the ~1.3 Hz batched-synchronous cadence floor and are
NOT reported — only phase-integrated energy and counts. Speed is the VCM/OBD
channel, not wheel-speed; the threshold sweep is shipped so no headline hinges
on one cut.

## M179 (2026-08-28) — Audit 2026-08-27 remediation, tranche 2c (final): M119-v2 machine-checkable freeze stamp + explicit recompute-on-demand policy (P0-03)

**Trigger.** M177's provenance gate could already detect that `socHysteresisV2`
was stale (training basis 259 drives < current 289) and that its
`recomputeMode==='carriedForward'` string was present, but "the string is
present" is not the same claim as "this staleness is sanctioned" — a block that
merely forgot to set `recomputeMode` for some other reason would have looked
identical to a properly-disclosed carry-forward. P0-03 asked for the disclosure
to be explicit; this closes that gap with a machine-checkable marker rather than
relying on the mode string or prose alone, and states the recompute policy
explicitly: **M119-v2 recomputation is performed only on the user's explicit
demand for that session, never automatically and never merely because the
corpus has grown.**

**Method.** `compute_summary_arrays.py`'s M148 carry-forward branch now stamps
`socHysteresisV2` with `frozenBasis: true`, `recomputeBlockedReason` (states the
OOM cause) and `recomputePolicy` (states the demand-only policy in full) whenever
the block is carried forward unchanged; the fresh-fit branches (explicit
`recompute_m119v2=True`, and first-run-ever) stamp `frozenBasis: false` /
`recomputeBlockedReason: None` so the field is never silently absent either way.
`build_html.js`'s M177 gate was tightened to require `frozenBasis===true`
specifically (not just the mode string) before treating a stale
`socHysteresisV2` as disclosed — verified this catches a regression case (mode
string present, freeze stamp absent) that the M177-only check would have missed.
The dashboard's existing carried-forward banner (`xtrail_summary.jsx`, already
present pre-audit) is sharpened to state the demand-only policy in the same
words, rather than the softer "run on demand (it is computationally heavy)."

**Verification.** Applied the stamp to the shipped 259-drive-basis block
(pure carry-forward re-stamp; no refit attempted — see *Recompute status*
below). Gate re-run: `socHysteresisV2` reports "[stale, disclosed]" via the new
check and does not abort; regression-tested by stripping `frozenBasis` alone
(mode string left intact) — gate correctly ABORTS with "STALE & UNDISCLOSED";
restored cleanly. jsdom 9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0 console errors; M119-v2
section confirmed rendered; the new `V.frozenBasis` binding confirmed correctly
compiled into the bundle.

**Recompute status.** No refit was attempted in this tranche — this is by
design, not an oversight. A true M119-v2 refit reliably OOM-kills this
environment's ≤4 GB sandbox (M148) and was not requested. Per the policy this
milestone encodes, the next refit happens only when explicitly requested
(`recompute_m119v2=True` / `--recompute-m119v2`), on a host with sufficient RAM.

**Isolation scope.** Changed: `compute_summary_arrays.py` (freeze-stamp logic),
`build_html.js` (gate tightened to `frozenBasis`), `xtrail_summary.jsx` (single
hunk, disclosure text), `summary_arrays.json` (**`socHysteresisV2` block only**
— key-diff confirms 1/107 top-level keys changed), `xtrail_dashboard.html`
(rebuilt). `drive_master.csv` unchanged (`44f8fd8…`). `py_compile` clean.

**Audit 2026-08-27 status after this tranche.** All five P0 findings addressed

provenance gate with the physical single-DAG unification explicitly deferred as

## M178 (2026-08-28) — Audit 2026-08-27 remediation, tranche 2b: energy-MC regeneration + de-hardcoded release constants (P1-02, closes P0-04 value residual)

**Trigger.** The M177 provenance gate flagged `energyUncertaintyMC` as stale
(nominal 1130.2847 vs current 1188.1 kWh, +4.87 %) — the P1-02 finding — and this
same block holds the P0-04 `offsetGrossSensitivity` value, which was therefore
also stale (3.5073 kWh at a −0.4055 A offset, vs the audit's independently
computed current +3.7641 kWh at −0.4062 A).

**Root cause.** `energy_mc_precompute.py` and `energy_uncertainty_mc.py` carried
the released offset (−0.4055), its 95 % CI ([−0.457, −0.311]) and the
net-correction magnitude (19.83 kWh) as HARDCODED literals from a 274-row corpus,
and the block was injected once and never regenerated. As the corpus grew to 289
drives (offset −0.4062, CI [−0.463, −0.329], net-correction 21.0 kWh) the block
silently diverged.

**Method.** (1) Parameterised both scripts: `build()` now takes
`offset_point_a` / `ci95a` / `net_correction_kwh` (module constants demoted to
fallback defaults), and both `__main__` blocks SOURCE the current values from
`summary_arrays.json`'s `offsetUncertainty` block (`pointEstimateA`, `ci95A`,
`correctionScope.netCorrectionMagnitudeKwh`) so a regeneration is self-currenting
and cannot re-hardcode a stale constant. Prose strings that embedded the literals
(e.g. "−0.4055 A", "[−0.457,−0.311]", "=19.83 kWh") are now f-strings bound to the
sourced values. (2) Re-ran the Tier-1 raw re-integration over the current corpus
(277 of 289 drives carry the BMS current/voltage channels; the other 12 have no
gross data in the master either, so coverage is consistent) — independent
re-implementation matches the shipped `drive_master.csv` gross columns to
5e-05 kWh at the 1500 ms nominal tolerance, confirming it is not a redrafted
approximation. (3) Re-ran the B=20 000 Monte Carlo (seed 20260822, deterministic)
and injected the fresh block.

**Before/after.** `energyUncertaintyMC.grossThroughputMC.nominalReleasedThroughputKwh`
1130.2847 → **1188.1206** (= `meta.grossThroughputKwh` 1188.1, gate now clean);
GTC nominal → 565.772, FCE → 282.886 (matching the audit's current 565.8 / 282.9).
`offsetGrossSensitivity`: atPointEstimateOffsetA −0.4055 → **−0.4062**;
throughputShiftKwh 3.5073 → **3.7641**; throughputShiftPct 0.3103 → **0.3168**;
across-CI [.,.] → **[3.0487, 4.2905]** — all three exactly reproducing the audit's
independent numbers. This **closes the P0-04 value residual**: the dashboard's
gross-offset-sensitivity paragraph now renders the current +3.7641 kWh / +0.3168 %.

**Isolation scope.** Changed: `energy_mc_precompute.py`, `energy_uncertainty_mc.py`
(parameterisation + sourcing), `summary_arrays.json` (**`energyUncertaintyMC`
block only** — key-diff confirms 1/107 top-level keys changed; the injected block's
schema is byte-compatible with the prior one, so all JSX bindings are unchanged),

/ `energy_uncertainty_mc.json` produced. `drive_master.csv` unchanged (`44f8fd8…`).
Validation: `py_compile` both scripts; MC schema equality vs prior block confirmed;

## M177 (2026-08-28) — Audit 2026-08-27 remediation, tranche 2a: injected/carried-forward block provenance gate (P0-02/P0-03 enforcement)

**Trigger.** Audit P0-02 (crossVehicle + energyUncertaintyMC injected out of band,
socHysteresisV2 carried forward → "rebuild ≠ release") and P0-03 (M119-v2 shipped
on a 259-drive fit against a 289-drive corpus). Investigation found the
*reader-facing* half of P0-03 already satisfied — `xtrail_summary.jsx` conditionally
renders a "Carried forward … last fit on {nDrivesCovered} drives … current
{currentCorpusSize}-drive corpus … re-fitting on demand" disclosure whenever
`recomputeMode==='carriedForward' && currentCorpusSize!==nDrivesCovered`. The real
gaps were (i) `crossVehicle`/`energyUncertaintyMC`/`socHysteresisV2` are **absent
from `REQUIRED_BLOCKS`**, so a payload missing an injected block would build clean
and ship blank sections, and (ii) nothing surfaced basis staleness to the
*operator* at build time.

**Method.** Added a release-provenance gate to `build_html.js` (immediately after
the REQUIRED_BLOCKS and M94 gates). For each out-of-band/carried-forward block it
checks presence and compares the declared basis to the current corpus:
`crossVehicle._meta.nPrimary` and `socHysteresisV2.nDrivesCovered` against
`meta.totalDrives`; `energyUncertaintyMC.grossThroughputMC.nominalReleasedThroughputKwh`
against `meta.grossThroughputKwh` (≥0.5 % divergence = materially stale). Verdicts:
a MISSING block or a STALE-and-UNDISCLOSED block aborts the build; a
STALE-but-DISCLOSED block (carry-forward marker / dataQualityNote present) prints
a WARN but never blocks — a disclosed carry-forward is by design (e.g. the OOM-heavy
M119-v2 refit), so the gate enforces *disclosure*, not *freshness*. This makes
"rebuild ≠ release" a checked, operator-visible condition instead of a silent one.

**Before/after.** Current build now emits a provenance summary: crossVehicle basis
289 == current 289 (clean); socHysteresisV2 basis 259 vs 289 (lags 30)
[stale, disclosed → WARN]; energyUncertaintyMC nominal 1130.2847 vs 1188.1 kWh
(+57.82 kWh, +4.87 %) [stale, disclosed → WARN]. Verified the gate ABORTS on a
dropped `crossVehicle` (MISSING) and on a `socHysteresisV2` with `recomputeMode`

## M176 (2026-08-28) — Audit 2026-08-27 remediation, tranche 1: manifest-gated cohort selection (P0-01) + TOST estimator-reference coherence (P0-05)

**Trigger.** Independent deep audit (`XTrail_ePOWER_Deep_Project_Audit_2026-08-27`),
two Critical (P0) findings addressed here; the remaining P0/P1 items are deferred
to tranche 2 (see *Deferred* below).

**P0-01 — cohort selection was unsafe by default.** `build_master_from_raw`
selected drives with a bare `glob('2026*.csv')`, which matches the two
discontinued `*_comparison` captures: the documented one-command path selects
291 files while the shipped master is 289. The correct exclusion had been
happening out of band, so a future release could silently re-contaminate every
statistic with no code change.
*Method.* Added `_select_canonical_cohort` (+ `_load_cohort_manifest`), driving
selection from the typed `raw_manifest.json` `role` records (canonical /
comparison_only / auxiliary) rather than a glob. Fails loud on any missing
canonical file; new `--strict-cohort` release gate enforces exact-set equality
(rejects any untyped orphan); default ingest mode admits genuinely-new canonical
files append-only with a notice; filename-marker exclusion retained only as a
no-manifest fallback. Threaded `manifest_path` / `strict_cohort` through
`run_pipeline` and `__main__`.
*Before/after.* raw glob 291 → selected **289** (== master file set exactly);
strict gate passes cleanly today; verified to raise on injected orphan (strict),
on a missing canonical (both modes), and to fall back safely with no manifest.
**Master is unchanged** — the 289-set is now a checked invariant, not an
accident.

**P0-05 — TOST paired a mixed-effects slope/SE with a cluster-OLS reference df.**
For `resistanceVreg`, `primaryEstimator == mixedEffects` (non-singular at 289
drives), so the TOST consumed the mixed-model slope/SE (1.3902 / 0.8208) but a
`t(df=57)` reference whose df = day-clusters−1 from the *cluster-robust OLS* — an
invalid hybrid. The prior M158 guard comment asserted this branch was "not
reachable … both are OLS"; that assumption went stale as the corpus grew (it was
true only while the resistance mixed model was still singular).
*Method.* The equivalence test now draws slope, SE, and reference df from one
coherent estimator — the convergence-independent cluster-robust OLS the module
was designed around (audit option "use cluster OLS throughout"). Added
`tostEstimatorBasis: 'clusterRobustOLS'` to both metrics; headline
`primaryEstimator` (point estimate) is untouched. A Kenward-Roger/Satterthwaite
mixed-model equivalence test is explicitly left as a separate, larger task.
*Before/after (resistanceVreg TOST).* tostSlopeUsed 1.3902 → **1.3928**;
tostSeUsed 0.8208 → **0.7583**; releasedEquivalence.equivCI90 [0.0178, 2.7626] →
**[0.1249, 2.6607]**; refDist stays t(df=57) but now legitimately.
**equivalent = False on every bound, unchanged — no scientific conclusion
flipped**, the inference is merely made coherent. cellSpread unchanged (already
cluster-OLS) beyond the new `tostEstimatorBasis` field.
*Dashboard narrative.* The Methods/Statistical-inference paragraph in
`xtrail_summary.jsx` claimed the mixed model was "degenerate for both metrics …
never the released estimator" — provably false for resistance. Replaced with a
self-correcting narrative bound to `S.degradationTrends.*.primaryEstimator` and
`tostEstimatorBasis` (renders "resistance … the mixed-effects slope; cell-spread
… the cluster-robust OLS slope; TOST on the cluster-robust OLS estimator").

**Isolation scope.** Changed: `compute_drive_summary_v6.py` (cohort guard),
`degradation_trends.py` (TOST basis), `summary_arrays.json`
(**`degradationTrends` block only** — key-diff confirms 1/107 top-level keys
changed, key set preserved), `xtrail_summary.jsx` (single hunk),
`xtrail_dashboard.html` (rebuilt). `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged
(`44f8fd8145496388870e8fa6cb40fd68`). Validation: `py_compile` both scripts;

`tostEstimatorBasis`); `build_html.js` REQUIRED_BLOCKS + M94 gates pass; jsdom
9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, **0 console errors**; corrected narrative confirmed

## M174 (2026-08-27) — Bound the M57 mountain-trip window; disclose ramp-detector polling-cadence sensitivity; reconcile the two dissipation charts

Triggered by Andrii flagging three items against the low-speed-dissipation /
mountain-pattern / high-speed-blending sections. All three resolved; only
`summary_arrays.json['mountainPattern']` changed in the data payload (strict
key-by-key isolation, 106/107 top-level keys byte-identical; `drive_master.csv`
untouched — this is an arrays-only + prose change, not an ingestion).

### (1) M57 window was an open-ended tail, not the trip — DATA FIX

`_mountain_pattern` selected the trip with `dm['date'] >= '2026-07-18'` and **no
upper bound**. When M57/M60 were authored (2026-07-27) that captured the
documented **53-drive, Jul 18–26** window; as ordinary post-trip daily driving
was appended through Aug 26 the same filter silently grew the "Carpathian trip"
to **148 drives / 3378.9 km**, contradicting this function's own docstring
("Jul 18-26 ... 53-drive window") and the still-present M60 stale-check comment
in the JSX Conclusions tab ("now spans Jul 18-26 across 53 drives"). It also
diluted every gate statistic with a month of flat, low-SoC-ceiling driving.

Empirical basis for bounding at Jul 26 (all recomputed against the raw corpus):
- **97%** of the window's motored-unfuelled seconds (1275 of 1316) fall on or
  before Jul 26; the 40 days after add **95 drives but only 41 motored s**.
- Mountain elevation (GPS altitude) appears **only Jul 24–26** (peak **1028 m**;
  Kyiv ≈ 150 m); every August drive in the old window sits at 120–222 m.
- Restoring the `<= '2026-07-26'` bound reproduces the docstring's documented
  correlations **exactly**: ρ_SoC **0.82** (had drifted to 0.62), ρ_relief
  **0.60**, partial ρ_relief|SoC **0.25 (p=0.077)** ("~0.25, p~0.08").

**Fix:** `TRIP_START='2026-07-18'`, `TRIP_END='2026-07-26'` bound added to the
filter. Regenerated `mountainPattern` via the unchanged pipeline function
(fidelity-checked: the pre-fix harness reproduces the on-disk 148-drive block
byte-for-byte before the change). New block: window **53 drives / 1707.5 km**;
dissipation **1275 s / 19 active drives**; gate ρ_SoC 0.62→**0.82**; incidence
low bins (<72.5 / 72.5-75) 67+40→**23+9** drives; gradeCoverage nFiles 20→**5**
(only the trip's Jul 24–26 GPS-altitude drives, not August Kyiv driving);
torqueGradeCalibration n 3610, r² 0.296. All JSX/Conclusions figures bind to
`S.mountainPattern.*` and update automatically; no hardcoded window literals
existed.

### (2) Polling-cadence sensitivity of the M116/M118 event detectors — DISCLOSED

Andrii asked whether the faster polling now in use influences the generator-ramp
segmentation and power-blending sections. Investigation confirms it does, in a
bounded way, and the section previously did not disclose it. The RPM channel's
native cadence is ~1.2 s (≈0.83 Hz) for most of the corpus and steps to ~0.78 s
(≈1.28 Hz) from ~2026-08-14 (same logging-generation family as the current-channel
shift documented at M102/M126/M170). Both `_buffer_impulse_events` (M116) and
`_ramp_latency_events` (M118) segment the **native** stream (no fixed-grid
resample), so their resolution tracks cadence. A within-drive control (fast
drives re-run after decimation back to ~1.2 s, holding the population fixed)
isolates the effect:
- **Cadence-sensitive:** resolved event count (+~21%: 625→518 events when the
  63 fast drives are decimated) and the ramp-latency distribution (median
  0.76→1.2 s; zeroLatencyPct 23→30 pp — the zero-latency figure is partly a
  resolution floor, already flagged in the prose). Pooled counts/latencies are
  therefore a cadence-weighted mixture, not a physical trend.
- **Cadence-robust:** the plateau segmentation itself (250 rpm bins, ≥3 s dwell,
  both coarse vs either interval) — nPlateaus 1.84→1.81, dwell 12.7→13.2 s,
  transitions/event 0.84→0.81 essentially unchanged — so the "discrete load
  points" conclusion is not a sampling artefact. The M41 blend-share / deficit /
  saturation-gate null run on a fixed 1 Hz grid and are cadence-immune.

**Change:** a bounded "Polling-cadence caveat (M174)" note added to the M118
subsection of the High-Speed Power Blending section. Qualitative/directional,
no new hardcoded figures. No data recompute (the M116/M118 keys are unchanged;
this discloses an existing property, it does not correct a value).

### (3) "Buffer-Saturation Dissipation at Low Speed" ↔ "Mountain-Road Pattern (M57)" reconciliation — PROSE FIX

Andrii flagged that the two sections read as mixed and that the M57
reconciliation note said "The two panels are consistent" while only one chart is
visible in that section. Correct: the note compares the M57 incidence chart with
the corpus-wide chart in the **separate** section above; they are never shown
side by side. Reworded the M60 note and its code comment to name the companion
section explicitly and to say "the two **charts** are consistent" rather than
"panels"; tightened the intro ("this trip" not "this one week"). Live figures
(denominators, per-bin comparison, the 90%-of-corpus-motored-seconds share) are
bound to the pipeline and updated with the new 53-drive window.

### Validation

`py_compile` clean; `summary_arrays.json` round-trips; `build_html.js`
REQUIRED_BLOCKS + M94 stale-key gates pass; jsdom 9-tab click-through 0 console
errors; targeted acceptance checks pass (rendered window "(53 drives, 1707.5
km)", "148 drives" absent, "two panels are consistent" absent / "two charts are
consistent" present, gate ρ=0.82, cadence caveat present).

## M173 (2026-08-27) — Retire the city_short/city_long distance split on `hvcEngine80C` (Section 2 narrative fix)

Triggered by Andrii flagging that the Engine Warm-Up Curve section's "M30
short/long urban trips" prose reflected a classification no longer in use.
Investigation found this was a real, load-bearing inconsistency rather than
stale wording: the pipeline carried **two contradictory docstrings** on the
same computation. `_cycle_projection`'s M86 comment claimed `hvcEngine80C`
had already been migrated to the native `CLASS_ORDER` taxonomy like every
sibling condition-class array in the module (`hvcTurboActivity`, `socBand`,
`warmupCurve`, engine trigger/stop SoC); `self.hvc_warm`'s own `__init__`
comment claimed the opposite — that the retired `DIST_BINS`-style
city_short (\<5km) / city_long (5–20km) urban split was a *deliberate,
permanent* holdout ("time-to-80°C is a trip-duration question, not a
driving-condition question"). The live code matched the second docstring,
and the module's own top-of-file note on `DIST_BINS` ("retained ONLY as a
legacy/reference constant — no longer applied anywhere") was therefore
false: it was being re-implemented inline for this one metric. The split
also silently dropped every urban trip \>20km from the metric entirely
(`bucket=None`, undisclosed in the JSX) — a second, independent defect.

**Fix (methodology decision, not a data correction):** `hvcEngine80C.urban`
is now a single native-`CLASS_ORDER` bucket, computed identically to mixed /
mixed_highway / highway (no distance sub-split, no upper-distance
exclusion) — closing the one holdout and making the M86 docstring's claim
actually true. `_warm_str` now reports `with_timing=True` for `urban` too,
consistent with its three siblings.

- **`urban` (was `city_short`/`city_long`):** 53% (n=116, <5km) / 96%
  (n=67, 5–20km) → single **72% of drives (n=214), typically within 2–7
  min**. n rises from 183 to 214 because the 31 urban drives >20km — with
  raw coolant telemetry, previously excluded outright — are now counted,
  not because of any change to which drives reach 80°C.
- **`highwayVsCity` "Engine reaches 80°C+" row:** the two-part "short
  trips <5km: ... · long trips 5-20km: ..." caption is replaced by the
  same unified figure, matching how the other three columns of that row
  are already presented.
- All nine other `highwayVsCity` rows and every other `summary_arrays.json`
  key are unchanged (key-by-key diff against the pre-fix rebuild: exactly
  `hvcEngine80C` and `highwayVsCity` differ, 105/107 byte-identical;
  `crossVehicle` and `rawManifest` carried forward byte-identical — neither
  depends on this computation).

### JSX (Section 2 — Engine Warm-Up Curve)

`xtrail_summary.jsx`'s M30-tagged caption line ("urban short-trip ...;
urban long-trip ...; mixed highway ...; highway ...") is replaced with a
single `urban` figure retagged **M173**, and a `mixed` figure is added —
the class was already computed but had been omitted from this one caption
line (all four `CLASS_ORDER` classes now appear, matching the rest of the
section and the Comparison tab). No other prose in Section 2 referenced the
retired split; the distance-domain warm-up chart itself (`WarmupCurve`,
`S.warmupCurve`) was already on native `CLASS_ORDER` per M86 and is
untouched.
