## M170 (2026-08-24) — Power-fade trend: HV-current sampling-cadence normalization; stale `powerFade.note` fixed

**Trigger.** The M25 temperature-controlled power-fade slope (`powerFade.slopeMohmPerMoTctrl`) had drifted monotonically upward across recent batches — roughly −0.001 → +0.60 → +0.77 → +1.19 → +1.28 → **+1.57 mΩ/mo**, with `pSlopeGt0` rising 0.16 → 0.72 → **0.977** and the day-cluster CI just clearing zero (**[0.021, 3.165]**). A jackknife showed the entire zero-crossing was created by the post-Aug-8 drives (slope = −0.001 through Aug 8, +0.49 through Aug 17, +1.19 through Aug 21, +1.57 through Aug 24), i.e. an edge phenomenon on a 3.32-month, single-season (May–Aug 2026) window.

**Diagnosis (mechanism, not battery).** Ruled out empirically, in order: (1) time↔temperature collinearity — refuted, corr(months, T_pack)=0.032, VIF=1.03; (2) linear-T-control misspecification — refuted, slope survives quadratic/cubic-T (1.65/2.10) and a common-T-band restriction (2.57); (3) drive-length/excitation composition — refuted, survives distance/duration/peak-I controls and a ≥20 km & ≥120 A restriction (1.70). What survived: the recent batch carries a genuine ~+7 % `vreg_R` level shift (133.8 vs 124.6 mΩ) **not** explained by mean-T, p95-I, distance, duration, or peak-I. Root cause is the **HV-current logging cadence**: the raw-logging PID configuration changed mid-corpus (see M126, fifth configuration; M102 corrupt-PID rejection at Aug 8), roughly doubling `[BMS] HV Battery Current (A)` coverage (4.1 % → 10.3 % of rows; effective inter-sample interval 1.27 s → 0.82 s). Denser I/V sampling reduces regression dilution and captures more of the true instantaneous sag under the 1500 ms (`V_ALIGN_TOL`) alignment, biasing the load-excited proxy **upward**; because coverage is confounded with calendar time (corr(months, I_coverage)=0.66), the OLS reads the instrumentation shift as a positive time trend.

**Fix.** `_powerfade_trend(dm, raw_loader=None)` (compute_drive_summary_v6.py) now, when a `raw_loader` is supplied, adds the per-drive HV-current sampling density (median inter-sample interval + coverage, via new `_i_channel_sampling_density`) as OLS covariates in both the point fit and the seeded day-cluster bootstrap, so the reported time slope holds logging cadence constant. `raw_loader=None` preserves the pre-M170 design byte-for-byte (postprocess_master report path unchanged). `_power_fade(dm, raw_loader=None)` (compute_summary_arrays.py) threads `raw_loader` through and the `build_summary_arrays` call site passes it; if absent, the block degrades gracefully to uncontrolled and emits an explicit WARNING in `note`.

**Result (corpus-wide, 4000-draw day-cluster bootstrap, nClean=163 unchanged):** cadence-controlled slope **+0.303 mΩ/mo**, CI **[−1.62, 2.462]**, `pSlopeGt0`=0.611 — the CI re-spans zero and the null result is restored. `bTMohmPerDegC` stable (−2.53 → −2.49); `mdeRisePctPerYr` 15.0 → 19.5 (df cost of the two covariates). New field `powerFade.cadenceControlled` (bool).

**Stale-note fix.** The pre-M170 `powerFade.note` hardcoded *"the 95 % day-cluster interval spans zero"* unconditionally; once the confounded slope crossed the boundary this contradicted the shipped CI. The significance clause is now derived from the actual CI (`spans_zero = lo ≤ 0 ≤ hi`) and states whether cadence was controlled.

**Scope / integrity.** Isolation diff: exactly four `summary_arrays.json` keys changed — `powerFade`, `fadeModes`, `officialDisclosureCorrelation` (both consume the trend), and `_provenance` (new `powerFade` entry). 107 top-level keys preserved; no keys added/removed. `drive_master.csv` MD5 `68c6236d6611af3c1250db3d3ff98295` unchanged (cadence computed at fit-time; no new master column, no re-analyze, 16 frozen ML/domain columns untouched). `py_compile` clean on both scripts; `build_html.js` REQUIRED_BLOCKS + M94 gates pass; jsdom 9/9 tabs, 52 inner buttons, 0 console errors. No capacity/SOH/EOL claim; `CAP_KWH` untouched (this metric is CAP-invariant). Winter/cross-season data remains the way to break the single-season confound at the source (cadence normalization neutralizes it in-model but does not substitute for range in T or time).

## M167 (2026-08-23) — Project-wide VCM/OBD vehicle-speed fallback (closes the socBySpeed 230/274 coverage gap)

Audit finding (prompted by a question about why "3 — Battery SoC Band by
Speed" covered only 230 of 274 drives). Root cause: `RAW_MAP` in
`compute_summary_arrays.py` maps only the native VCM PID
(`'[VCM] Vehicle Speed (km/h)'`) to `'speed'`, with no fallback to the
OBD-generic PID (`'Швидкість автомобіля (km/h)'` — a genuinely distinct
channel, not a locale translation). 44/274 files (the 5 earliest, May
11-13, plus 39 from Aug 14-22 — apparently a logging-app/locale change
reverting speed back to the OBD-generic PID) log speed exclusively under
the OBD channel and were silently dropped from every raw-pass array gated
on `col('speed')`.

`compute_drive_summary_v6.py` already carried the correct fallback
(`speed_source='vcm'`/`'obd_fallback'`, threshold 20 native samples) for
per-drive stats in `drive_master.csv` — those were never affected. The gap
was specific to the Category-B (raw 1 Hz) pipeline stage. The stale M35
(2026-07-14) code comment claiming the 5-file exclusion was "correct, not
a bug" was accurate at 5 files but had gone undetected as the true count
grew to 44.

### What changed

- **`drive_raw_cache.py`**: `SLIM_COLS` schema bumped v4 → v5, adding the
  OBD-generic speed PID so the slim frame cache carries it for every file.
- **`compute_summary_arrays.py`**: replaced seven independent, VCM-only
  local column maps (`RAW_MAP`/`_RawAccum.add()`, plus ad hoc maps/literals
  in `_motor_temp_stats`, `_highspeed_census`, `_ramp_latency_events`,
  `_soc_hysteresis_grid`, `_dissipation_census`, `_mountain_pattern`,
  `_low_speed_dissipation`) with ONE shared helper,
  `_apply_speed_priority()`: VCM channel if it carries >= 20 native
  non-null samples, else the OBD-generic channel — identical rule and
  threshold to `compute_drive_summary_v6.py` and to what
  `m119v2_model.py`'s `build_grid()` had already independently arrived at
  (that file needed no change; it doesn't take a `frame_loader` and reads
  raw CSVs directly via its own `read_needed()`). Added
  `socBySpeedMeta.nSpeedObdFallback` to disclose, per session, how many
  contributing drives resolved speed via the fallback rather than the
  native channel. Corrected the now-stale M35 __init__ comment and a
  stale M147/M148-area comment that had claimed the OBD channel "is not
  in the slim frame cache" (schema v5 now carries it).
- **`extract_soc_patterns.py`**: same fallback applied to the illustrative
  SoC-panel generator's `load()`. No-op for the two current example
  drives (`HIGHWAY_CSV`/`URBAN_CSV`, both VCM-complete) — kept so a future
  re-pointing to a VCM-sparse drive doesn't silently break the panel.
- **`xtrail_summary.jsx`**: Chart 3 ("Battery SoC Band by Speed") coverage
  caption rebound from a hardcoded "May 11-13" gap description to the live
  `socBySpeedMeta` fields (`nDrives`, `hours`, `nSpeedObdFallback`, and any
  remaining gap), so it can no longer drift out of sync with the pipeline.
- Deliberately **untouched**: `_audit_raw_manifest` / `rawManifest` /
  `coverageMap` / `gpsAltitudeCoverage`. These exist to report the actual,
  literal per-file PID inventory (logging-generation/PID-configuration
  history); synthesizing a resolved VCM column into that audit trail would
  have falsified it. They still read `raw_loader` directly, untouched.

### Coverage impact (274-row corpus, `drive_master.csv` unchanged throughout)

`socBySpeedMeta`: **230 → 272 of 274 drives** (141.0 h, was 125.4 h),
**42 via the OBD fallback**. The remaining 2 (not 274) are unrelated: two
pre-existing, documented zero-BMS 19-column-schema files
(`20260816_124817.csv`, `20260816_144003.csv`) that carry no SoC PID under
either name and were never going to contribute regardless of speed
source. `cycleBySpeedMeta`: 224 → 261 (residual gap is separate I/V
coverage, not speed). `engineOnDrives`: 228 → 272.

24 top-level `summary_arrays.json` keys changed value (all col('speed')-
gated or direct downstream propagations of them): `cycleBySpeed`,
`cycleBySpeedMeta`, `engineOnBySpeed`, `engineOnDrives`,
`lowSpeedDissipation`, `motorTemp`, `mountainPattern`, `rampLatency`,
`regenByTempMeasured`, `regenByZone`, `regenCaptureMeasured`,
`regenCaptureMeasuredMassUncertainty`, `regenCaptureMeta`, `socBySpeed`,
`socBySpeedMeta`, `socHysteresis`, `speedDist`, `terrainCoverage`,
`terrainTorqueDist`, `terrainTorqueDistLow`, `torqueBySpeed`,
`turboBySpeedCtx`, `warmupCurve`, `crossVehicle` (only its
speed-conditioned `eventDetectors.rampLatency`/`socHysteresis` sub-fields
and `_meta.generated` timestamps moved; `turboPattern`/`pureElectric`
data is byte-identical, timestamp only; e-4ORCE aux-side fields and all
non-speed cross-vehicle stats untouched). **83/107 keys unchanged**,
including the carried-forward `energyUncertaintyMC` (untouched by this
fix, copied through byte-identical) and `socHysteresisV2`
(`recompute_m119v2=False`, per standing OOM-safety procedure — unaffected
either way since `m119v2_model.py` already had the correct fallback).

through `20260822_215052.csv`, 10:22→22:24), lifting the corpus from
267 → **274 drives / 7,233.3 km / 1,130.28 kWh gross throughput / GTC
538.23 / FCE 269.12 / rf_efc 294.08**.

### Batch detail

Seven legs across the full day (10:22–22:24), 93.5 km / 158.89 min combined,
21.5706 kWh gross throughput, GTC 10.2717, FCE 5.1359, rf_efc 5.5550. D1
(`102139`, 14.3 km, `mixed`, +26→+28°C): SoC 53.5→64.5, `sign_check ok`,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net corr2p −1.35/100km, `pct_highway`=10.9%; clears
the 80-120km/h deficit gate (`band_80_120_s`=126.5s, `deficit_80_120_pct`=
30.4%, `deficit_80_120_valid`=True). D2 (`110317`, 24.0 km, `urban`,
+28→+30°C): SoC 62.5→59.0, `sign_check ok`, `ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net
corr2p +0.07/100km, the batch's longest leg (42.85 min); no 80-120km/h band
time (`band_80_120_s`=0.0, `deficit_80_120_valid`=False). D3 (`141715`,
12.7 km, `urban`, +33°C constant): SoC 54.0→52.5, `sign_check ok`,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net corr2p +0.06/100km; `band_80_120_s`=10.0s falls
short of the 120s deficit-validity floor (`deficit_80_120_pct`=16.0%,
`deficit_80_120_valid`=False). D4 (`173539`, 5.7 km, `urban`, +33°C
constant): SoC 48.0→59.0, `sign_check ok`, `ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net
corr2p −2.70/100km (a per-100km artefact of the short distance denominator
— absolute net draw is only −0.1539 kWh over the whole leg); no 80-120km/h
band time; the batch's warmest leg (`T_pack_mean_max`=40.0°C). D5
(`191324`, 6.9 km, `urban`, +32→+30°C): SoC 51.5→58.5, `sign_check ok`,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net corr2p −1.72/100km (−0.1188 kWh absolute); no
80-120km/h band time. D6 (`205359`, 3.9 km, `urban`, +28°C constant): a
brief 10.4-minute evening hop, SoC 49.5→65.5, `sign_check ok`,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net corr2p −6.05/100km (a per-100km artefact of
the very short distance denominator — absolute net draw is only
−0.2360 kWh over the whole leg); `n_vsag_load`=14 falls below
`VSAG_MIN_LOAD`=15, so `vsag_R_pack_mohm` is NaN for this leg only (a
genuine per-drive coverage gap, not a defect). D7 (`215052`, 26.0 km,
`mixed`, +27°C constant): SoC 62.0→63.0, `sign_check ok`,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean, net corr2p −0.01/100km — the batch's
closest-to-neutral leg, absolute net draw only −0.0023 kWh over the whole
26.0 km leg; clears the 80-120km/h deficit gate (`band_80_120_s`=133.9s,
`deficit_80_120_pct`=69.2%, `deficit_80_120_valid`=True), the batch's
longest-distance leg. All seven legs `sign_check ok`, `f_domain`-clean,
`ens_outlier_v2`-clean throughout — D2, D3 and especially D7 sit close to
net-neutral over their full-length legs, another clean illustration of the
study's central buffer-not-reservoir framing. Pack-mean peak temperature
climbs across the day's warming legs (31.0→38.0→39.0→40.0→41.0°C, D1
through D5) tracking intra-day thermal accumulation through the +26 to
+33°C ambient window, then holds at 41.0°C through the two evening legs
(D6, D7) despite ambient cooling to +27–+28°C — consistent with the
study's heat-soak carryover framing (τ≈18.49h) rather than instantaneous
ambient tracking. All seven files carry the same 79-column raw schema as
the immediately preceding Aug-21 files (no PID-configuration change).

Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrated −0.4093 → **−0.4055 A** (2
passes, 2 domain-excluded, unchanged 4-file `f_domain` set; v5 single-pass
−0.4041 A). Degradation trending remains statistically null: adjusted
loaded-spread slope −0.402 mV/month (v2 OLS; CI [−0.921, 0.075],

CIs straddle zero, consistent with every prior session.

## M164 (2026-08-22) — Audit §5 P2: mass model — replace the pseudo-random hash-split with a point value plus closed-form uncertainty range

No ingestion, no change to `drive_master.csv` (MD5 `28b6c5573570830fb417d02a1e07cc45`
unchanged — the mass model has never been a `drive_master.csv` column; it is computed
entirely inside `compute_summary_arrays.py` and consumed only by the two mass-scaled
physics estimates). `summary_arrays.json`: `ddc6f28c5a20fede624246292e22c413` →
`41f87f6db817cffe7ddfe9ba7e2203bc`. **One new top-level key added** (`regenCaptureMeasuredMassUncertainty`,
additive — the existing `regenCaptureMeasured` chart-series shape is untouched so no
chart-rendering risk); **four pre-existing top-level keys changed** (`regenByZone`,
`regenByTempMeasured`, `mountainPattern`, `constantProvenance`) — verified in every case
that only NEW sub-fields were added and every existing point value (`eff`,
`captureFraction`, `netDropToSaturateM`, etc.) is byte-identical to before. Code
changed: `compute_summary_arrays.py` (`_mass_for_drive`, new `_mass_uncertainty_bounds`
helper, `_RawAccum`'s regen-capture accumulation, `_mountain_pattern`'s descent-budget
computation, `CONSTANT_PROVENANCE`); `xtrail_summary.jsx` (regen-chart mass description,
descent-budget panel).

### What was wrong (audit §5 "Remaining precision gaps")

"The mass model assigns 1,860/1,920 kg using a deterministic file-hash split for some
classes. This is pseudo-random imputation, not a physical measurement; replace with an
uncertainty range or measured payload." `_mass_for_drive` assigned EVERY urban/mixed
drive to either 1860 or 1920 kg via an md5 hash of its filename — a fair coin flip
presented per-file as if it carried physical information, feeding two downstream
physics estimates (regen-capture KE loss, descent-energy-budget PE) that both scale
linearly with the assumed mass.

### Fix

- **Source**: urban/mixed drives now use a single honest point value,
  **1890 kg** (the exact midpoint of the retired 1860–1920 kg range) — matching how
  highway/mixed_highway has always used a single point value (2000 kg), not a split.
  Verified this removes negligible information: the retired hash-split's actual
  per-drive-count mean across 217 urban/mixed drives was 1893.7 kg (95 at 1860, 122 at
  1920) — only 0.20% from the new midpoint, confirming the fair-coin design was already
  close to unbiased and the point-value simplification loses nothing material.
- **Uncertainty, not silence**: every output that scales with the assumed mass now
  carries a closed-form uncertainty range from the disclosed ±30 kg urban/mixed band,
  rather than a single point derived from the retired coin flip:
  - `regenByZone[].effRangeMassUncertainty`, `regenByTempMeasured[].effRangeMassUncertainty`,
    `regenCaptureMeasuredMassUncertainty` (parallel array, keyed the same as
    `regenCaptureMeasured`): **exact** per-zone/per-bin bounds going forward — `_RawAccum`
    now separately tracks `ke_um` (the urban/mixed-only KE contribution) alongside the
    total `ke` per zone/bin/temperature-band, so a future raw rebuild recovers each
    bin's own urban/mixed KE-share exactly (not a worst-case guess: zones dominated by
    highway decel correctly get a tighter band than zones dominated by urban/mixed
    decel). This session's arrays-only patch (no raw rebuild) uses the CONSERVATIVE
    upper bound instead (assumes each bin's entire KE is urban/mixed-uncertain — the
    exact per-bin split isn't recoverable from the already-stored aggregates without
    re-touching raw data), giving ±1.5–1.6% typical.
  - `mountainPattern.descentBudget.captureFractionRangeMassUncertainty` /
    `.toSaturationRangeMassUncertaintyM`, `.urbanMixedRowShare`: **exact**, both in code
    (segments are now tagged `mass_is_urban_mixed` at the point of ingestion) and in
    this session's patch (backed out algebraically from the already-stored
    `assumedMassKg`=1982.8, giving `urbanMixedRowShare≈16.2%` — most qualifying
    descents are highway drives at the fixed 2000 kg point, so the band is tight:
    captureFraction 0.40 → [0.399, 0.401]).
  - **netDropToSaturateM is near mass-invariant** — verified numerically, not asserted:
    the assumed mass appears in both `captureFraction`'s denominator and the
    saturation-distance formula's own denominator and nearly cancels (computed
    explicitly at both mass bounds: all four SoC-entry rows unchanged to the metre).
- **`CONSTANT_PROVENANCE['MASS_BY_DRIVE_TYPE_KG']`** updated to the new point-value
  shape and disclosure note; the corresponding stored `constantProvenance` block in
  `summary_arrays.json` was a static snapshot from a prior run and needed its own
  surgical patch (caught by the live-DOM verification below, not by the isolation diff
  alone — a real gap in the first patch attempt, fixed before landing).
- **Dashboard**: the regen-efficiency chart's mass description now reads "2000 kg
  highway/mixed-highway, 1890 kg urban/mixed" (previously silently rendered
  "undefined–undefined kg" after the value-shape change, from JSX code that indexed the
  old value as a `[lo,hi]` array — caught and fixed before this landed) plus a new
  sentence disclosing the ±1.5% typical band. The descent-budget panel's capture-fraction
  row now shows the range inline, and its note explains the urban/mixed row share and
  the verified near-invariance of the saturation-distance figures.

### Validation

`py_compile` clean · isolation (one key added — additive, existing `regenCaptureMeasured`
chart-series shape untouched — four keys changed with every pre-existing point value
confirmed byte-identical; `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged) · `build_html.js` gates pass ·
`validate_jsdom.js` 9 tabs / 0 console errors · T-01…T-04 all PASS · additionally, a
targeted live-DOM check (same React-18 MessageChannel-polyfilled, `dispatchEvent`
methodology as M163's verification) caught TWO real rendering bugs before they shipped:
(1) the regen chart's mass description initially rendered "1860,1920 kg urban/mixed"
because the stored `constantProvenance.MASS_BY_DRIVE_TYPE_KG` snapshot hadn't been
included in the arrays-only patch (fixed by patching it explicitly); (2) prior to that,
a JSX destructuring pattern (`mp.urban[0]`/`[1]`) that assumed the old array shape would
have silently rendered "undefined–undefined kg" (fixed before the first build). Both
confirmed resolved by re-running the live-DOM check after each fix — the panel now
renders "1890 kg urban/mixed" correctly on the charts tab, and the descent-budget

## M163 (2026-08-22) — Audit §5 P2: Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation for the energy integral

No ingestion, no change to `drive_master.csv` (MD5 `28b6c5573570830fb417d02a1e07cc45`
unchanged). New modules: `energy_mc_precompute.py` (Tier 1, raw re-integration),
`energy_uncertainty_mc.py` (Tier 2, Monte Carlo). `xtrail_summary.jsx`: one new panel
in the Conclusions tab (audit-remediation appendix section, alongside the existing
M155–M158 degradation and §4.3 offset-uncertainty prose). `summary_arrays.json`:
`3ced431cfa61e02bc9a449a9b2ecb714` → `ddc6f28c5a20fede624246292e22c413`; **one new
top-level key added (`energyUncertaintyMC`), all 105 pre-existing keys byte-identical**
— this is the first M163+ change that touches raw CSVs, and it is a pure addition.

### What was built

Addresses the audit's own §5 finding: gross throughput/GTC/FCE quote only the I/V
nearest-voltage-tolerance sweep as uncertainty; current offset, ADC quantization, and
missing-sample/gap-truncation coverage were never propagated. Two-tier design so raw
CSVs are read exactly once (~171s for the full 255-drive usable-I/V corpus), not on
every Monte Carlo draw:

- **Tier 1** (`energy_mc_precompute.py`) re-integrates each drive's raw current/voltage
  samples with the EXACT algorithm in `compute_drive_summary_v6.py` (same COL_MAP,
  artifact filters, discharge-positive sign convention, DT_CAP_S=5s step cap,
  merge_asof-nearest alignment) across a 7-point tolerance grid (500–2000 ms), plus an
  analytic (delta-method) quantization SD, gap-truncation bounds, and an
  offset-on-gross-metrics sensitivity (one extra re-integration pass at the released
  offset, sample-level).
- **Tier 2** (`energy_uncertainty_mc.py`) runs 20,000 Monte Carlo draws over the cached
  Tier-1 outputs (fast — no raw re-reads): tolerance drawn Uniform(500,2000ms) and
  piecewise-linearly interpolated per drive from the real 7-point grid; quantization
  drawn per-drive Normal(0, delta-method SD); gap-truncation coverage drawn as a
  per-iteration severity weight in [0,1], always additive (DT_CAP_S is a one-sided
  conservative-low truncation, never an over-count).

### Validation against independent references

- **Nominal throughput reproduces the audit's own §5 table to the digit**: this
  session's re-implementation gives 1108.714 kWh at 1500ms (audit: 1108.7143), and the
  full tolerance-sweep curve matches: 500ms −0.2320% (audit −0.232%), 1000ms −0.0368%
  (audit −0.037%), 2000ms +0.1569% (audit +0.157%).
- **Cross-validated against `drive_master.csv`** at the nominal tolerance: max absolute
  deviation 5×10⁻⁵ kWh across 255/255 drives (rounding-level agreement, confirming this
  is not a redrafted approximation of the released algorithm).
- **Net-draw-corrected nominal reproduces the master**: -13.484 kWh vs
  `net_draw_kwh_corr2p` sum of -13.4865 kWh in `drive_master.csv`.

### Results

- **grossThroughputMC**: combined 95% credible interval on gross throughput
  **[1108.007, 1115.372] kWh** (median 1111.740, +0.269% mean shift from the released
  1108.714 kWh point value) — GTC [527.622, 531.130], FCE [263.811, 265.565] at
  CAP_KWH=2.1. Right-skewed, not centred on the release point: gap-truncation and most
  of the tolerance-widening effect are one-sided (can only add energy).
  Source budget: alignment tolerance ±0.175%, gap-truncation up to +0.567%,
  quantization ±0.0001% (negligible after per-drive sample-count averaging).
- **Data-quality finding**: 96.0% of the tolerance-widening tail (1500→2000ms) is
  concentrated in just 2 of 255 drives (`20260813_145651.csv`, `20260813_150341.csv`),
  which poll their voltage channel at ~4s intervals (corpus-typical ~0.9–1s) — no
  current sample finds a voltage match within the released 1500ms tolerance at all, so
  both drives contribute literal 0.0 kWh gross throughput at the released tolerance
  (matching `drive_master.csv` exactly), only picking up matches as tolerance widens.
  Flagged explicitly rather than left to read as diffuse corpus-wide alignment noise;
  not excluded or altered here (a corpus-composition decision, not a data question).
- **offsetGrossSensitivity** (deterministic, not Monte Carlo): answers
  `offsetUncertainty.correctionScope`'s own previously-unresolved question ("its
  gross-metric effect is asymmetric and cannot be recovered from master aggregates;
  quantifying it requires a raw re-integration pass"). Applying the released offset
  (-0.4093 A) to raw current before the discharge/charge split would **increase** gross
  throughput by **+3.4788 kWh (+0.3138%)**, +2.788 to +3.935 kWh across the offset's
  95% CI — because a constant bias does not cancel in a |I| integral the way it cancels
  in signed net draw. Reported as a labeled sensitivity alongside the released
  offset-uncorrected values, not applied to them: extending the correction to gross
  metrics is a convention decision, not something this pass should decide unilaterally.
- **netDrawCorrMC**: 95% interval **[-18.977, -8.363] kWh** around the released
  -13.484 kWh, propagating the same tolerance/quantization/gap sources plus the
  offset's own bootstrap uncertainty (reusing `correctionScope.netCorrectionMagnitude
  Kwh=19.63` rather than re-deriving a parallel offset-application formula). A real
  sign bug was caught and fixed here during development: the offset correction is
  ADDED (net_draw_kwh_corr = net_draw_kwh − off_kwh, and off_kwh < 0 at the released
  offset since i_off < 0) — verified directly against `drive_master.csv`
  (`sum(net_draw_kwh_corr − net_draw_kwh) = +19.559`) before landing the fix.
- **Capacity**: not Monte-Carloed (CAP_KWH has exactly one credible alternative
  reference point — the official 5.0 Ah disclosure, ≈1.80 kWh at this corpus's median
  pack voltage — not a distribution shape to assume a prior for). GTC/FCE reported at
  the current CAP_KWH=2.1 convention with a deterministic rescale factor (×1.1667) to
  1.80 kWh alongside, consistent with the existing `capacitySensitivity` table's own
  approach.

### Dashboard

New panel in the Conclusions tab, immediately after the existing §4.3 offset-
uncertainty paragraph, bound to `S.energyUncertaintyMC.*` (no hardcoded figures).

### Validation

`py_compile` clean on both new modules · Tier-1 cross-validated against
`drive_master.csv` (5×10⁻⁵ kWh max deviation) and the audit's own §5 table (matches to
4 decimals) · isolation (one key added, 105 pre-existing byte-identical,
`drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged) · `build_html.js` gates pass · `validate_jsdom.js`
9 tabs / 0 console errors · T-01…T-04 all PASS · additionally, a targeted jsdom check
(React-18 MessageChannel-polyfilled, `dispatchEvent` clicks matching
`validate_jsdom.js`'s proven methodology) clicked into the Conclusions tab specifically
and confirmed every new panel value renders correctly in the live (non-script) DOM text
— not just present in the embedded data payload — with zero `undefined`/`NaN` leakage
and zero console errors.

## M160 (2026-08-22) — Audit §7: replace the "near-memoryless" regime conclusion with a real serial-dependence test

No ingestion. Corpus 267 drives / 7,139.8 km. `drive_master.csv` MD5
`28b6c5573570830fb417d02a1e07cc45` unchanged. Code changed: `compute_summary_arrays.py`
(new `_regime_persistence`; `_regime_transition` builds run-segments and calls it) and
`xtrail_summary.jsx` (§7 conclusion sentence). `summary_arrays.json`
`cd3a430a97bfeda00a83c5b8cc698319` → `db571b3146b71c636a78272e3dfca9bd`; **only
`regimeTransition` changed** (one key `persistence` ADDED; every pre-existing
regimeTransition field byte-identical), other 104 top-level keys byte-identical.

- **Root cause.** The dashboard concluded the regime sequence is "near-memoryless
  day-to-day" because the Markov stationary distribution sits on the empirical
  marginal. That is not an independence test: for an ergodic chain fit to a single
  sequence, the stationary distribution approximates the empirical marginal **by
  construction**, whatever the persistence. The project's own self-transition share
  (0.71) already contradicts "memoryless."
- **Fix.** `_regime_persistence` computes the independence baseline for the same-state
  share, Cohen's κ (from- vs to-state agreement above chance), mutual information
  (nats), the likelihood-ratio G-test of independence (df=(n−1)²), and a
  label-permutation p-value (B=5000, seed=42) that shuffles regime labels within the
  same run-length structure — preserving the marginal, destroying serial order. Runs
  are split at the same chain breaks the matrix uses (unknown-type drives; over-
  threshold idle gaps in session variants).
- **Result (independently reproduces the audit's §7 numbers exactly).** Across all
  262 transitions: observed same-state **71.4%** vs **59.5%** under independence,
  **κ=0.293**, **MI=0.135 nats**, **G=71.0 (df=9)**, **permutation p<0.0002**
  (internal check G=2·N·MI=71.0). Verdict: statistically detectable, moderate short-
  range persistence — same-type drives cluster — NOT a memoryless sequence.
- **Dashboard.** The §7 conclusion now reports these statistics (bound to
  `S.regimeTransition.persistence.*`) and states the stationary-vs-marginal agreement
  is expected by construction and not an independence test; the stationary/marginal
  descriptive pairing is retained. Within/across-session transition matrices and
  day/session-level bootstrapping (audit §7 "preferred methods") remain a P2 item.
- Validation: `py_compile` clean · isolation (only `regimeTransition`, only
  `persistence` added) · `build_html.js` gates pass · jsdom 9 tabs / 0 errors ·
  T-01…T-04 all PASS.

## M157 (2026-08-22) — Audit §6: single-stage cell-spread model (remove the double temperature adjustment)

`28b6c5573570830fb417d02a1e07cc45` unchanged. Code changed: `degradation_trends.py`

### Released-model failure fixed (independent audit, section 6)

- **Root cause.** `_analyse`'s mixed-model acceptance gate (`me_ok`) tested only that
  the fixed-effect SE was finite and positive. statsmodels returns `converged==True`
  on a **singular day random-effects covariance** for the cell-spread outcome and
  emits a fixed-effect SE of **523,394,626.37 mV/month** (95% CI ±1.03×10⁹). That
  "result" passed the naive gate, was published as `cellSpread.primaryEstimator =
  mixedEffects`, **and** fed the equivalence test (`tostSeUsed = 5.23×10⁸`,
  `equivCI90 = ±8.6×10⁸`, `tostSlopeUsed` rounded to 0.0). The dashboard rendered the
  interval as `tostSeUsed × 1.96` = **±1,025,834,617 mV/month**. A numerical optimiser
  returning finite values is not a scientific validity criterion.
- **Fix.** The mixed model is accepted as primary only if it (a) returned a finite,
  positive fixed-effect SE, (b) converged, **and** (c) that SE is not blown up
  relative to the convergence-free cluster-robust OLS SE (`SE_BLOWUP_FACTOR = 25×`;
  the singular case exceeds it by ~10⁸ — the boundary/singular tell). Otherwise the
  cluster-robust OLS is authoritative and **both** the released slope and the TOST
  inherit its slope/SE via the existing `(b, se)` selection. `.converged` alone is
  insufficient (it reports True here); the SE-blowup check does the work. `_mixedlm`
  now also records the day random-intercept variance (`groupVar`) and the gate sets
  `reCovarianceSingular` for transparency. This fits **no new model** — it stops
  publishing an already-computed singular one.
- **cellSpread result (released, now OLS).** slope **−0.3246 mV/month**, SE 0.2611,
  `equivCI90` **[−0.7541, 0.1049]**, `pTOST` 0.6384. Equivalence still **not**
  established (window too short) — the honest "inconclusive, window too short"
  finding is preserved, not reframed. Displayed CI **±1.03×10⁹ → ±0.51 mV/month**.
- **resistanceVreg unchanged.** Already `clusterRobustOLS` (its `_mixedlm` returns a
  non-finite SE and fell back correctly). slope 1.432 mΩ/mo, SE 0.8309, `equivCI90`
  [0.0653, 2.7987] — numerically identical. Only its `degenerateNote` was reworded to
  the accurate reason (non-finite SE) and `groupVar`/`reCovarianceSingular` added.
- **Singular fit retained, not deleted.** The `cellSpread.mixedEffects` block is kept
  in the payload flagged `degenerate: true` + `reCovarianceSingular: true` +
  `degenerateNote`, consistent with the M108 convention already used for the
  resistanceVreg degenerate block. It is never rendered; only the OLS result is
  released and displayed.

### Diagnostic findings (no code change required)

- **Power-fade point estimate is not accelerating fade.** The P — Power-Fade Status
  slope moved from ≈0 to **+1.186 mΩ/mo** over the last ingestion batch. Independent
  re-fit of the M25 model (`vreg_R_pack_mohm ~ months + T_pack_mean_avg + vreg_I_p95_A`,
  ens-clean) reproduces +1.186 exactly at n=147; refit **without the last 23 drives**
  (n=124, window 2.79 mo) gives **−0.001 mΩ/mo**. The entire move is those ~23 recent
  drives, which read higher resistance (median 133.2 vs 121.8 mΩ) while **cooler**
  (32.4 vs 35.7 °C). The proxy is temperature-dominated (`corr(T,R) = −0.848`,
  `bT = −2.553 mΩ/°C`); the linear T-control over-corrects a late-window cool batch and
  leaks seasonal effect onto the time slope (raw slope +0.328 → T-controlled +1.186).
  95% CI [−0.547, 2.958] spans zero, P(slope>0)=0.909, implied 11.5%/yr sits **below**
  the ±16.9%/yr MDE. Correct read unchanged: **no detectable power fade; report the CI,
  not the point estimate.**
- **n=147 is a genuine load-excitation gate, not a stale scalar.** `vreg_R_pack_mohm`
  has exactly 147 non-null rows in the 267-row master; coverage cascade
  267 → 253 (HV-current PID) → 169 (vsag gate, ≥15 load samples) → 147 (vreg V–I
  regression gate). Populated on drives through 2026-08-21; grew 124→147 with the last
  batch. `powerFade.nClean` is pipeline-bound (regenerated each build), not hardcoded.

Applied the concrete, corrective subset of the standing editorial/readability review of `xtrail_dashboard.html` (deliverables A–G; provisional score 64/100, dragged down by accessibility/terminology, not scientific quality). **`xtrail_summary.jsx`-only session, text-only:** both production JSON artefacts byte-unchanged throughout (`summary_arrays.json` MD5 `42ea23244300e0b08227a91ba3c6b9e2`, `summary_config.json` unchanged), `drive_master.csv` MD5 `85e5184b98a926028112645fe69fcbb1` unchanged, corpus 264 drives/182 cols, `run_pipeline()` never invoked, no arrays regeneration. 15 reader-facing string sites changed (14 single-match asserted edits + a 4× global relabel), net JSX +~1.5 KB.

**Terminology — `SOC`→`SoC` standardisation (12 sites).** The dashboard carried both casings (`SoC` 161× / `SOC` 12×); the 12 uppercase whole-word instances (Conclusions fade boxes, etc.) are now canonical `SoC`. The 6 `SOH` (State of Health) instances are correctly untouched.

**§G safety-adjective cluster — prohibited-without-criterion terms replaced with the observed measurement (not a weaker claim).** (a) "well within a **safe** uniformity margin" → "consistent and uniform across the corpus" (Thermal). (b) "**runaway** heating" → "unbounded temperature climb" at all three reader-facing sites (Thermal convergence note, Health risk table, Conclusions) — removes the loaded thermal-failure term while preserving the true observation (the pack reaches an equilibrium plateau). (c) "Both are **normal** operating states, **not faults**" → "Both are expected given the conditions" (Thermal). (d) "**None of this reduces mobility.**" → "None of these prevent the vehicle from operating — the failure mode is graceful degradation (more engine cycling, poorer economy, less EV creep), not loss of drive" (Conclusions capacity-fade box). Item 12's "within traction-motor thermal limits (150 °C+ rated)" was left unchanged — it is the correct pattern (cites an explicit criterion).

**Scientific precision — proxy relabels.** (a) CH-1: the hardcoded `2.1 kWh` in the Chart-C GTC caption is now **bound** to `S.constantProvenance?.CAP_KWH?.value ?? 2.1`, and "X-Trail e-Power nameplate pack capacity" → "assumed pack capacity — unverified, not an OEM nameplate figure" (the value is `verified:false`; describing it as nameplate overstated it). (b) CH-2 and family: all 5 reader-facing "torque-**verified**" labels (charge-mode split, regen attribution, four-way partition, charge-mode shading) → "target-torque-**based** … (a commanded-torque proxy, M12)" — target torque is a commanded set-point, not a measured/verified output. (c) HV-4: the M119-v2 STOP-model "demand **index**" → "demand **proxy** (a stand-in for driver power demand, not measured power)". (d) CH-4 grammar: "no observable whatsoever" → "no observable **signal** whatsoever" in the capacity-fade headline claim.

**Consistency — two disclosures added.** (a) **CH-3:** the C-rate risk-map top caption asserted the cold-plating red zone flatly while Conclusions item 6 correctly caveats it; added an inline caveat ("generic Li-ion guidance, not a pack-specific rating, and no drive in this corpus falls inside it — asserted from chemistry, not observed here") so the two sections agree. (b) **HV-1 (the one dug out of the arrays):** `socHysteresisV2` is `recomputeMode:"carriedForward"` — fit on **259** drives while `currentCorpusSize` is **264** — so the M119-v2 section rendered "259 drives" against 264 elsewhere with no explanation. Added a self-maintaining carried-forward disclosure at the top of the `SocHysteresisV2` panel, gated on `recomputeMode==="carriedForward" && currentCorpusSize !== nDrivesCovered` (auto-hides once refit). **No computed value altered** — the model genuinely was fit on 259.

**CV-1:** "buffer behaviour **conserved** across a heavier dual-motor platform" → "consistent across a heavier dual-motor platform within this 9-drive auxiliary comparison — a cross-check, not an independent validation" (§5: the e-4ORCE rail is auxiliary, not a validation corpus).

**Deferred (documented, not defects).** (1) The 83 reader-facing internal M-tags (descriptive-name-first treatment) and a `<Glossary>` help panel, plus the `<Callout>`-based density splits of the five wall-of-text captions (Battery Operating Map, Chart P, Chart 1, Chart 3, Highway-vs-City analysis blocks) — a larger, judgment-heavy structural change staged as review installment 2, kept out of this build to keep the diff clean. ## M149 (2026-08-21) — `rfDodHistogram` fixed: restored as a reproducible `build_summary_arrays()` computation

Closes the gap disclosed at M148 ("has no reproducing code"). Same defect
class as the F-12 `powerFade` and P0-14 `sessionLedgerAudit` out-of-band
artifacts: correct numbers, hand-injected into `summary_arrays.json` during

SoC trace (frame_loader; raw_loader fallback) under the IDENTICAL

depth-of-discharge. Because the floor and eligibility gate (`len(soc)>=10`)
match M17 exactly, the recomputed cycle count and k=2 damage sum reproduce
`drive_master.csv`'s own `rf_n_cycles` / `rf_damage_k2` column sums by
construction — a live regression guard against any future drift between
this function and the M17 per-drive convention, not an independent
validation.

reproduces the original M146 block to full precision: `nCyclesTotal`=7034.0,

identical (same 5 drives, same order, same values), both `crossCheck` sums
identical (25.95). Confirmed via the actual pipeline module, not a
standalone re-implementation.

**Refreshed to the current 264-drive corpus** (all 264 raw files present on
disk; slim raw cache rebuilt fresh, 264/264, no `raw_cache.tar` carried into
this session — the standing constraint). New values: `nCyclesTotal`=7169.5,

### M119-v2 made recompute-on-demand (root cause + decision)

Routine ingestion's standard full regen (`build_summary_arrays`, raw +
frame loader) was **reproducibly OOM-killed** in this session's sandbox
(≈3.9 GB RAM, no swap). Isolated across three successive repro runs before
any fix was attempted:

1. Full `build_summary_arrays()` on the 264-row corpus → OOM-killed
   (anon-rss ≈3.94 GB) partway through the array-building sequence.
2. `m119v2_model.build_m119v2()` run **standalone**, with no other array
   computation in the process → also OOM-killed at ≈3.94 GB, isolating the
   fault to M119-v2 specifically.
3. Checkpointed/traced instrumentation (external driver scripts calling
   the unmodified module's own functions — no source file touched during
   diagnosis) showed `_corpus_tables()` (per-drive raw-CSV → 1 Hz grid →
   at-risk-second table) completes cleanly at only ≈455 MB RSS
   (S=256,062 at-risk start-seconds, T=238,666 at-risk stop-seconds — both
   sane). The crash occurs immediately after, inside `run_ladder(S, k=5)`
   — i.e. somewhere in the 20 `fit_glm` calls (4-model ladder × 5
   blocked-chronological folds) that fit the complementary-log-log hazard
   GLMs on the ~230k-row complete-case sample.

**Decision:** M119-v2 (`socHysteresisV2`) refitting is no longer part of
routine ingestion. `build_summary_arrays()` gains two new parameters,
`recompute_m119v2=False` and `prev_arrays=None`. Default behaviour now
**carries the last-computed block forward unchanged** from
`prev_arrays['socHysteresisV2']` (tagged `recomputeMode:'carriedForward'`,
`currentCorpusSize:<n>`) instead of refitting on every session; a fresh
fit only happens when `recompute_m119v2=True` is passed explicitly (tagged
`recomputeMode:'fresh'`, `corpusSizeAtRecompute:<n>`), or when no prior
block exists at all (first run — computed once regardless of the flag, so
the key is never silently absent). The same flag is threaded through
`run_pipeline(recompute_m119v2=...)` and exposed as `--recompute-m119v2`
on the CLI. `xtrail_summary.jsx`'s existing `S.socHysteresisV2` bindings
are untouched — the carried-forward block has the identical shape, plus
the two new disclosure fields, so the dashboard section renders exactly as
before (jsdom-verified below).

This session's shipped `socHysteresisV2` therefore still reflects the
**real M147 fit on the 259-drive corpus** (`nDrivesCovered`=259,
`nStartAtRisk`=247,550, `nStopAtRisk`=234,785) — now explicitly tagged
`currentCorpusSize`=264, a disclosed 5-drive (1.9%) staleness gap versus
the corpus this session actually ships, pending a future session that
recomputes it on demand (ideally in an environment with more than ≈4 GB
available, since the OOM is a resource ceiling, not a bug in the modelling
code — no methodology or fitting logic was changed).

## M147 (2026-08-20) — M119-v2: five-variable, duration-aware engine start/stop hazard model

Upgrades the M119 SoC-hysteresis analysis from a binned empirical surface to
two **separate 1 Hz discrete-time hazard models** — a START model on
engine-off seconds and a STOP model on engine-on seconds — each predicting a
canonical debounced engine transition in the following second from five
strictly-lagged predictors: **SoC, validated speed, pack temperature, recent
demand and elapsed engine-state duration**. New module `m119v2_model.py`;
new production key `summary_arrays.json → socHysteresisV2` (additive — the v1
`socHysteresis` block is untouched and still drives its own chart). The
milestone description, per specification, is: *a five-variable, duration-aware
observational model of engine start/stop probability conditional on SoC, speed,
pack temperature, recent demand and elapsed engine-state duration — not a
reconstruction of Nissan's proprietary ECU algorithm.*

### Canonical debounced detector (shared definition, M116/M118 family)

One transition definition, run-confirmation based: a **start** is the first
second of a sustained running run (RPM > 800 for ≥ 2 s) that follows a
confirmed sustained-off run (RPM ≤ 100 for ≥ 3 s); a **stop** is the first
second of a confirmed off run (≥ 3 s) following a running second. Short
dropouts and missing (NaN) samples form no confirmed run and are never counted.
A first implementation used strict adjacency (`off[t−3:t]` immediately followed
by `on[t:t+2]`) and misfired: the RPM ramp transits the 100–800 mid-band
between the two states, so the adjacency requirement stranded the engine in the
ON state (a single urban drive reported 1 start / engine-on 99 % of the time —
physically wrong). Replaced with maximal-run confirmation, which is the correct
reading of "off ≥ 3 s *followed by* on ≥ 2 s" and tolerates the ramp; the same
drive then resolves to 22 start/stop cycles at a realistic ~27 % urban engine
duty. Disclosed here rather than silently patched, per standing convention.

### Corpus at-risk tables (259/259 drives, gated)

Built directly from raw frames (not the slim cache — the OBD-fallback speed
channel `Швидкість автомобіля` is not in `SLIM_COLS`, and v2 honours the full
VCM→OBD speed-source priority of `compute_drive_summary_v6`; 230 drives VCM,
29 OBD-fallback). 1 Hz grids with the specified carry-forward ages (SoC ≤ 5 s,
speed ≤ 2 s, pack temp ≤ 15 s requiring ≥ 3 of T1–T4), physical range gates
(pack sensors −40..80 °C after a 107 °C glitch was found; SoC 0..100; V
100..500; coolant −40..130), START demand = median discharge kW over
[t−8, t−2], STOP demand = median max(target-torque, 0) × speed **index** (not
kW) over [t−5, t−1], and `log1p` state durations.

- **START**: 247,550 at-risk seconds / **4,278 events (1.728 %)** / 63 days.
- **STOP**: 234,785 at-risk seconds / **4,277 events (1.822 %)** / 62 days.
- Common complete-case (5-var) samples: START 233,501 / 4,134; STOP 226,726 / 4,144.

### Models and chronological validation

Complementary-log-log (discrete-time hazard) GAM: intercept + restricted-cubic-
spline smooths f1..f5 (standardised inputs, train-fold-only knot placement) +
penalised reduced tensor interactions **SoC × demand, T × demand, SoC ×
duration**, fit independently for start and stop. **Random-effects disclosure**:
a full crossed day × drive binomial GAMM is not tractable on the installed
Python stack (no mgcv/lme4); the additive smooths and interactions are fit
exactly, and day/drive dependence is carried by day-clustered robust covariance
(final fit) and by **whole-day blocked chronological cross-validation** (k = 5,
contiguous day blocks, days never split across folds) for every reported
generalization metric — the operative guard against treating seconds as
independent. The four-model ladder improves **monotonically** on Brier, log
loss and PR-AUC for both models:

    START (blocked chrono CV, n=233,501 / 4,134 ev)   Brier   logLoss  PR-AUC  calSlope
      SoC only                                        0.01734 0.08758  2.47%   0.904
      + speed                                         0.01708 0.08104  5.12%   0.969
      four-variable                                   0.01704 0.08029  5.72%   0.966
      five-variable + duration                        0.01698 0.07966  6.25%   0.962
    STOP  (n=226,726 / 4,144 ev)
      SoC only                                        0.01781 0.08673  3.78%   0.902
      + speed                                         0.01774 0.08366  4.94%   0.947
      four-variable                                   0.01723 0.07522  8.50%   0.941
      five-variable + duration                        0.01714 0.07409  9.18%   0.934

Both five-variable models are well calibrated (predicted/observed events
4,121/4,134 START, 4,386/4,144 STOP). **Day-clustered bootstrap 95 % PR-AUC
intervals** (200 resamples, whole days) for the five-variable model do NOT
overlap the SoC-only intervals — START [5.72 %, 6.77 %] vs [2.16 %, 2.88 %];
STOP [8.59 %, 10.25 %] vs [3.53 %, 4.06 %] — so the improvement over SoC-alone
is not a pseudo-replication artefact. The fitted partial-dependence shapes are
mechanistically coherent: P(start) falls with SoC and rises with speed / demand
/ off-duration; P(stop) rises with SoC and falls steeply with the demand index
(the dominant STOP predictor), confirming the v1 "demand dominates SoC" finding
as a fitted regression rather than a two-band contrast.

### Sensitivity screen (tested, not part of the primary five)

Each candidate added to the full five-variable model, retained only if it
improves blocked-CV OOS log loss:

- **START**: SoC-change-since-transition (ΔlogLoss +0.000036), engine coolant
  (+0.000009), time-since-key-on (+0.000034) — **none retained** (all worsen
  OOS). Accumulated-charge is degenerate (all-zero on engine-off seconds) and
  not tested for START.
- **STOP**: SoC-change (+0.000067, not retained); accumulated-charge
  (−0.000079), engine coolant (**−0.000448**), time-since-key-on (−0.000015)
  cross the retention threshold, but only **engine-coolant temperature** is a
  non-negligible improvement (PR-AUC 9.21 → 9.66 %); the other two are within
  bootstrap noise and flagged as such. Engine thermal state gating shutdown is
  the interpretable mechanism.

### Dashboard (M147)

New section under the engine/generator control panel (after the v1
`SocHysteresisChart`): the blocked-CV ladder tables for both models with
bootstrap PR-AUC intervals, five partial-dependence small-multiples
(P(start) solid / P(stop) dashed), and twin **P(start) / P(stop) surfaces** on
SoC (x) × speed (y) with **temperature / demand / current-state-duration
selectors** and an **observed-support mask** (SoC × speed cells with < 20
at-risk seconds are greyed, never extrapolated). Every figure binds to
`S.socHysteresisV2`; nothing hand-typed.

### Wiring, provenance, invariants

- `compute_summary_arrays.build_summary_arrays` now calls
  `m119v2_model.build_m119v2(dm, raw_loader=…, raw_dir=…)` in the raw-pass
  block (guarded import; resilient to `None`), so full regens reproduce the
  block from source. This session's artefact was generated by that function and
  placed with the surgical injector `inject_m119v2.py` (splice-before-brace, no
  re-serialisation of existing content).
- **Isolation diff**: `summary_arrays.json` 104 → **105** top-level keys; the
  only added key is `socHysteresisV2`; all pre-existing keys (incl. the v1
  `socHysteresis`) byte-identical (NaN-aware). `drive_master.csv` and
  `summary_config.json` unchanged.
- **Validation**: `py_compile` (all scripts) · `build_html.js` (REQUIRED_BLOCKS
  + M94 stale-key gates pass; wrote `xtrail_dashboard.html`) · jsdom 9-tab

## M143 (2026-08-19) — thermal step response: pack warmup time constant (M139 residual, item 4 of the cleared batch)

Andrii's steer cleared the ordering (heat-soak → regime matrix → thermal step response) and the M142 cell-suppression choice; this is the last of the three. M139 named "thermal impulse response" as distinct from `_thermal_convergence`'s start/peak/end summary, framing it as the thermal analogue of M118's ramp-latency work — a control-systems-style step/impulse-response characterization.

**The event-scale reading does not work — checked empirically before committing to a design.** On the corpus's longest sustained-load leg (`20260619_122407.csv`, 284 km, 249 min highway), correlating a 60 s rolling mean of `|I|` against the pack-mean temperature's minute-by-minute derivative gives **r ≈ 0.06** — essentially zero. The pack thermal mass low-pass-filters transient dissipation far below the ~6.16 s (0.16 Hz) pack-temperature PID cadence established at M123; a per-acceleration or per-event impulse response is below the resolvable floor of this instrumentation, not merely noisy. Reported as a finding (`eventScaleResolvable: False`) rather than forcing a fit that the data cannot support.

**What is resolvable: the bulk first-order warmup.** Every drive's pack-mean trajectory from cold start climbs toward a load-dependent steady state in the classic first-order form T(t) = T_ss − (T_ss − T0)·e^(−t/τ). Fit on the monotone-rising window (key-on to 98% of observed rise), gated for identifiability — the failure mode caught in development: an under-observed 64 min window let T_ss run to its curve_fit bound (80°C) on a drive that never actually plateaued. Four gates, all required: real cold-start transient (rise ≥5°C); plateau **actually reached** in-window (final-15%-of-window slope ≤0.05°C/min, not extrapolated); R²≥0.90; window ≥0.9·τ.

**Corpus result.** Of 91 long-drive candidates (duration ≥1500 s), 9 pass all four gates (38 rejected `no_transient`, 34 `plateau_not_reached`, 6 `poor_fit`). **τ_warmup median 38.7 min** (IQR [28.0, 40.7], range [17.7, 48.3]); T_ss median 41.6°C from a 25.5°C median start (median rise 15.9°C); fit quality R² median 0.950 (min 0.905, n=9). Small-n by construction — most drives are either too short to observe a plateau or start already warm — but every accepted fit is a genuine first-order response, not a forced one.

**Unifying result.** The pack heats under load with τ≈38.7 min but cools when parked with τ≈18.49 h (M141, below) — an asymmetric thermal time constant, cooling ~29× slower than heating. Physically consistent: heating is driven by active internal dissipation (I²R + generator/motor waste heat) against a large thermal mass, while cooling is passive convection to ambient air through the pack enclosure — a much weaker coupling. Ties M141 and M143 into a single physical picture rather than two disconnected time constants.

**Implementation.** `_thermal_step_response(dm, raw_loader, frame_loader=None, ...)`, inserted (with `_full_datetimes`, `_regime_transition`, `_heat_soak_carryover`) between `_headroom_utilization_summary` and `_dissipation_census`; `_dissipation_census` signature re-verified intact post-edit (M116/M118/M140-class guard). Reuses `_battery_temp_traj`'s pack-mean convention (async 4-sensor 1 Hz grid, `ffill(limit=3)`, −40..80°C gate) rather than a new temperature pipeline. Wired as `arrays['thermalStepResponse']` in the raw-dependent block, immediately after `heatSoakCarryover` (both reuse the `_traj` pass already made for `thermalConvergence` — no extra raw read for M141; M143 needs its own pass since it operates on the 1 s continuous series, not the trajectory summary).

**Dashboard.** New `<Section title="Thermal Step Response — Pack Warmup τ (M143 — N identifiable fits)">` on the Thermal tab, directly below the M141 heat-soak section it forms a pair with, guarded by `{S.thermalStepResponse?.available && S.thermalStepResponse.nFits>0 && (...)}`. Per-fit rows, gate-rejection tally, and the explicit event-scale-unresolvable statement are all bound to `S.thermalStepResponse.*`; the closing paragraph computes the heating/cooling τ ratio live from `S.thermalStepResponse` and `S.heatSoakCarryover` rather than hardcoding "~29×".

**Validation.** `py_compile` clean · module functions reproduce the standalone prototype exactly (nFits=9, τ median 38.7 min, gate tallies identical) · `m141_143_arrays.py` surgical injector: 100→103 top-level keys, exactly `{heatSoakCarryover, regimeTransition, thermalStepResponse}` added, all 100 pre-existing keys byte-identical, `drive_master.csv` MD5 unchanged · `build_html.js` (`REQUIRED_BLOCKS`+M94 gates clean) → `xtrail_dashboard.html` 1428 KB · jsdom 9-tab click-through: 0 console errors, all three new sections confirmed present in live-rendered DOM on their correct tabs (one tab-boundary misplacement of the M142 section caught and corrected during this same validation pass — see M142 below) · T-01/T-01b/T-02/T-03/T-04 all PASS.

## M142 (2026-08-19) — drive-type regime transition matrix, cell-suppressed (M139 residual, item 3 of the cleared batch)

Second of the three items in Andrii's cleared order. M139 confirmed no existing code computes drive-type sequence structure — distinct from M118's RPM-plateau transitions (engine load-point, not drive class) and M119's SoC hysteresis state machine (start/stop probability, not a Markov chain over `drive_type`). Andrii's steer specified cell suppression as the reliability guard for small counts.

**Load-bearing bug caught before any corpus number was trusted.** `time_start`/`time_end` are time-of-day only (`"18:57:51.363"`, no date component) — the date lives solely in the separate `date` column. A naive `pd.to_datetime(time_start)` collapses all 256 drives onto one fictitious calendar day, which corrupts both the chronological transition order (drives get sorted by clock time instead of true sequence) and every inter-drive gap computation the same bug would poison for M141. Caught via hand-verification before trusting any output: the naive-parse gap distribution was uniformly negative (median −0.22 h, min −4.13 h) — physically impossible for gaps between two positive-duration drives — which is what surfaced the defect. Fixed with `_full_datetimes(dm)`: anchor `time_start`/`time_end` to `date`, and roll `time_end` to `date+1` when it is numerically less than `time_start` (midnight-spanning drive). Post-fix gaps are physical (median 1.40 h, p75 7.40 h, max 187.54 h ≈ 7.8 days, zero negative/overlapping gaps across 256 drives). The fix materially changed the regime matrix's own headline number: self-transition share moved from a spurious 0.58 (naive ordering) to the correct **0.7131**. `_full_datetimes` is now the shared timestamp helper both M141 and M142 depend on.

**Corpus result.** First-order Markov chain over `CLASS_ORDER` (urban/mixed/mixed_highway/highway), chronological, 3 `unknown`-type drives breaking the chain (neither valid from- nor to-state): **251 transitions**, self-transition share **0.7131** (strongest for urban, 86.2%), 7 of 16 cells suppressed (count <5, per Andrii's steer — still counted in their row's denominator, never dropped; a reliability flag, not a deletion). Clearest off-diagonal structure: highway↔mixed_highway coupling, 7 transitions each direction — fast driving clusters together rather than alternating with urban legs. The Markov **stationary distribution** (urban 75.3% / mixed 6.0% / mixed_highway 11.6% / highway 7.2%) sits almost exactly on the **empirical marginal** (74.6% / 5.9% / 11.3% / 7.0%) — the day-to-day regime sequence is close to memoryless at the whole-corpus scale, with the real persistence structure operating only at short range (within a driving session, not across days). A 12h session-reset variant (54 gap-breaks) gives a consistent picture (self-share 0.7259, same qualitative structure), included for robustness but not treated as the headline.

**Implementation.** `_regime_transition(dm, min_cell=5, max_gap_h=None)`, master-only (no raw pass), same insertion point as M141/M143. Wired unconditionally as `arrays['regimeTransition']`, immediately after `socBandReset` — the master-only Category-A-adjacent section, not the raw-dependent block, since it needs nothing beyond `drive_type`/`date`/`time_start`/`time_end`.

**Dashboard — placement error caught and corrected in this same session.** The regime-matrix `<Section>` was initially inserted at the wrong tab boundary: the anchor used (`</Section>\n</>)}` immediately preceding the `{/* ── THERMAL ── */}` comment) is unique in the file, but the tab it actually closes is **"highway vs city"**, not "distribution" — the two tabs sit adjacent and both close with the identical pattern.
